key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"Blood and bone or urea at 80g/m² when plants reach knee height. Repeat at shoulder height. In zone 10, rapid warm-season growth means the two-feed program must be timed precisely to plant growth stage, not calendar dates.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"In zone 10 warm summers, heat and dry spells at silking are common. Water daily if needed during the 7-10 day silk emergence period. Failure here causes cobs with many missing kernels.","category":"watering"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check silk for harvest readiness","details":"Check from 60-65 days. Harvest immediately and refrigerate or eat.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Succession sow every 3 weeks for continuous harvest","details":"Plant a new block every 3 weeks from September to December. climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply light fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 50g/m² after shoots establish. One application only — excess nutrition in warm zones produces soft poorly-stored shallots.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply potassium at bulbing","details":"Sulphate of potash at 25g/m² when bulbs visibly swell. Stop nitrogen immediately.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Stop water when tops yellow","details":"Stop watering promptly. In subtropical zones the curing period is shorter — the warm dry air cures the neck quickly.","category":"watering"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest September — store in cool dry conditions","details":"Harvest in September before heat returns. Cure for 2 weeks. In subtropical zones shallots store for 3-6 months (shorter than cool-zone equivalents).","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted from individual bulbs — each divides into a cluster of 4-8 new bulbs at harvest. Same day-length sensitivity as onions. Cure thoroughly before storage.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"When corn reaches knee height (30-40cm), apply blood and bone at 100g/m² or pelleted nitrogen fertiliser alongside the row. The milky stage lasts only 2-3 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest at peak sweetness","details":"Pick at milky stage. Twist and pull downward to detach from the stem. extra_care: Short season — quick-maturing varieties (Honey & Pearl); Start indoors 3-4 weeks before last frost
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Mulch root zone heavily","details":"Deep mulch (15cm) protects roots in cool zone winters. climate_note: Extremely drought-tolerant once established. Two crops possible in warm zones: breba (on old wood, Nov) and main (on new wood, Jan-April). Most varieties are self-pollinating.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"When the first flower buds appear, apply sulphate of potash at 40g/m² around plants. Repeat at 6-week intervals through the fruiting period. Potassium is the key nutrient for fruit quality and yield.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Support heavy-fruiting plants","details":"Stake or cage plants as fruit develops — heavy crops can topple unsupported plants. Use soft ties. Harvest green for crisp texture or wait for full colour for sweetness. Each plant can produce 8-12 capsicums per season.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Needs 10°C+ at all times. Pick red for full sweetness — green capsicum is simply unripe.

key_activities: [{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser and potassium at fruit set","details":"Same nutritional program as other zones. In tropical soils, fortnightly liquid fertiliser is more effective than granular.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Apply preventive sulfur spray for powdery mildew","details":"In subtropical zones, apply preventive sulfur spray from 60 days (before mildew appears). Once powdery mildew establishes in warm humid conditions it is very difficult to control.","category":"pest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest before wet season arrives","details":"Aim to complete the main harvest by September in tropical zones. Cure in a warm dry covered position. Winter squash cured quickly after harvest stores well even in subtropical conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Same principles as pumpkin. Harvest at full maturity with hard skin — unlike summer squash. Cures to 3-6 months storage. Needs bees for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest in dry season — best flavour","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, dry season thyme has the best essential oil content. Harvest freely April-October. Wet season growth is often soft and low in flavour compounds.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Hard prune","details":"Cut back by 50% at the start of the wet season. This reduces the soft growth that is vulnerable to fungal disease in humid conditions.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Replace plant","details":"Wet season stress significantly reduces thyme lifespan in warm zones. Replace every 2-3 years from cuttings. Container-grown thyme moved under cover in the wet season lasts longer.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Good but wet season causes root rot — excellent drainage critical
climate_note: Drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial. Thrives in poor, dry, well-drained conditions. Like oregano — rich soil and overwatering reduce flavour and shorten plant life.

key_activities: [{"timing":70,"activity":"Blanch stalks for mild flavour","details":"2-3 weeks before harvest, wrap cardboard or black plastic around the stem cluster to exclude light. This is optional but produces the pale, mild-flavoured celery sold commercially. Blanching takes 2-3 weeks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest outer stalks or entire plant","details":"Harvest outer stalks as needed from 10-12 weeks, or cut the entire plant at the base for bulk use. Cool zone celery holds on the plant for several weeks in cold conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow crop needing consistent moisture and cool but not cold conditions. Blanching by excluding light produces milder, less bitter stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Install drip irrigation and apply mulch","details":"Consistent moisture through drip irrigation is ideal. Heavy mulch insulates roots and prevents soil moisture loss in tropical heat.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Begin harvesting regularly","details":"Harvest fruit when glossy and firm. In tropical zones eggplant produces year-round. This restores productive vigour and removes old unproductive wood. New growth emerges within 2-3 weeks and flowers within 6-8 weeks in warm zones.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Heat-loving crop — needs even more warmth than tomatoes or capsicum. Harvest while skin is glossy and before seeds develop brown inside.

key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Do not protect from frost — improves head quality","details":"In cool zones, a frost on the developing head triggers the formation of a tighter, less bitter head. Do not protect radicchio from frost — it benefits the crop distinctly.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest outer leaves first — check head firmness","details":"Harvest outer leaves as needed from 8-10 weeks. climate_note: Italian chicory family. Frost reduces bitterness and tightens the head. Cut back to stump after first head harvest — radicchio regrows and produces again.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Begin harvesting at 10cm height","details":"Cut leaves with scissors 3-4cm above soil when plants reach 10cm. The plant regrows from the cut base 2-3 times before bolting. extra_care: Excellent cool-season salad — nearly year-round in zone 8
climate_note: Fast-growing salad leaf. Bolts in heat producing very pungent, almost inedible leaves. Succession sow every 10-14 days. Wild rocket (Diplotaxis) is more heat-tolerant than common rocket (Eruca).

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting outer leaves — cut-and-come-again","details":"Harvest outer leaves only. In zone 10 with year-round warmth, a single plant produces for 12+ months with cut-and-come-again management.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 3)","details":"Blood and bone at 80g/m² at planting. Zone 10 silverbeet grows vigorously — consistent feeding sustains this.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 3)","details":"Blood and bone at 80g/m² at planting. climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After fruit removal, thin the canopy to improve airflow. extra_care: Premium orange zone — excellent flavour with cool nights
climate_note: Cool nights in winter are needed for the best flavour (sugar-acid balance). Valencia ripens later than Navel and is the best variety for warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and support plants","details":"In cool zones wind can be damaging. Stake each plant to a 60cm stake at transplant. Apply potassium-rich fertiliser (sulphate of potash at 40g/m²) at flowering — potassium drives fruit development.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest green or wait for full colour","details":"In cool zones the season may end before capsicum fully ripen. Harvest green if frost threatens. Red capsicum is the same fruit — simply allowed to fully ripen — and is sweeter with higher vitamin C.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Start indoors in September for November transplant
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Needs 10°C+ at all times. Pick red for full sweetness — green capsicum is simply unripe.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Apply complete fertiliser at 150g per plant at establishment. Side-dress with blood and bone monthly through the growing season. Cardoon grows rapidly with adequate nutrition.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Blanch stalks for eating — 3-4 weeks before harvest","details":"In late summer-autumn, tie the leaves together in a bundle around each plant and wrap with cardboard, hessian or black plastic to exclude all light. climate_note: Globe artichoke relative grown for the blanched leaf stalks (not the buds). Requires blanching (excluding light for 3-4 weeks) to produce edible, mild-flavoured stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin ruthlessly to 5cm spacing","details":"This is the step gardeners most often skip and most regret. Crowded carrots fork and stay small. Thin in two stages: first to 3cm at 3 weeks, then to 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check progress by brushing away soil","details":"Brush soil from the top of the root at 8-9 weeks. Pull by twisting and pulling steadily, or loosen soil with a fork first to avoid breaking roots.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Trellis and shade cloth","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not recommended). No nitrogen.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Begin harvesting young pods every 1–2 days","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not recommended). climate_note: Flat edible-pod peas. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Harvest before seeds develop inside the pod. Inoculate with rhizobium.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Provide afternoon shade","details":"Shade significantly extends the bolt-free window in subtropical conditions. Sow on the south side of taller plants.","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Harvest fronds young — before bolting","details":"In warm zones harvest fennel fronds early and continuously from young plants. climate_note: Florence fennel (bulb type) is grown for the swollen stem base. Herb fennel is more adaptable. Both bolt readily in heat. Do not plant near dill or coriander — cross-pollination affects flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and apply potassium","details":"Eggplant develops to 80-100cm and branches heavily when fruiting. Stake each plant with a 1m stake. Apply sulphate of potash at 40g/m² at first flower. In cool zones, maximise nutrient support to make the most of the short season.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest before seeds show brown","details":"Cut (do not pull) fruit when the skin is glossy and firm. If pressure with a thumbnail shows no resistance, the fruit is overripe — seeds will be brown and flavour bitter. In cool zones harvest promptly at correct size to encourage continued production.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest all before frost","details":"Remove all remaining fruit before first autumn frost. Green eggplant will continue to ripen at room temperature if kept warm. Frost kills plants immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Heat-loving crop — needs even more warmth than tomatoes or capsicum. Harvest while skin is glossy and before seeds develop brown inside.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Check chill hour accumulation","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). In zone 11a/b, chill hour accumulation determines whether the plant sets fruit. Track minimum overnight temperatures from June-August. Warm winters produce poor crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Remove fruited canes. Thin new primocanes to 6-8 per plant — in subtropical zones excess canes compete for the limited chill hours available to each bud.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest early in the day","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). In zone 11 harvest in early morning. Fruit ripens quickly and softens in subtropical heat. Refrigerate immediately after picking.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 200-700 chill hours. Grown from canes or root divisions, not seedlings. Fruits on second-year canes (floricanes).

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 10cm — thinnings are edible","details":"Thin at 3-4cm seedling height. Thinnings make excellent salad greens. Crowded turnips produce small deformed roots.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Check root size from 35 days","details":"Begin checking by pulling a test root at 35 days. Harvest at 5-7cm diameter — the sweet spot for texture and flavour. Succession sow every 3 weeks for continuous supply of young, sweet turnips.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent cool season root crop — cold sweetens flavour
climate_note: Fast cool-season root crop. Harvest small (5-8cm) — older turnips become pithy and peppery. Leaves are also edible (turnip greens). Frost improves sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Check for scale insects and sooty mould","details":"Soft scale (brown scale) and Asian citrus psyllid are major pests in warm zones. Apply horticultural oil in winter while fruit is absent. Sooty mould on leaves indicates scale insect presence — treat the scale, not the mould.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Prune to maintain compact shape and remove crossing branches. In tropical zones cumquat can crop twice per year — time pruning for after the main harvest.","category":"pruning"}]
extra_care: Productive — monitor for citrus gall wasp and mites
climate_note: Most frost-tolerant citrus. Compact tree suitable for container growing. Self-fruitful. Fruit is eaten whole — skin is sweet, flesh is tart.

Include potassium — critical for fruit development.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Papaya is a very heavy feeder. Include potassium — critical for fruit development.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"Papaya is a very heavy feeder. Papaya leaves die at 0°C; the growing tip (crown) is killed below -1°C. Loss of the crown kills the tree entirely.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest when yellow blush develops","details":"In zone 9b papaya may fruit only in warm years. Harvest when 20-30% of the skin has turned yellow. The fruit continues to ripen at room temperature.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Not suitable — frost kills young plants
climate_note: Fast-growing tropical/subtropical tree. Short-lived (3-5 years productive). May include hermaphrodite, male or female plants from seed — hermaphrodite produces best fruit. Water-sensitive — do not waterlog.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune lightly after harvest","details":"Remove dead wood, crossing branches and any water shoots growing vertically from main scaffold branches. Cumquats fruit on new season wood — some fresh growth is needed annually.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest winter to spring","details":"Cumquats ripen June-October in zones 9-10. The fruit can remain on the tree for months without deteriorating. Harvest by hand — the whole fruit including skin is eaten.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most frost-tolerant citrus. Compact tree suitable for container growing. Self-fruitful. Fruit is eaten whole — skin is sweet, flesh is tart.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train a single permanent trunk","details":"Train a single main stem to the top of the trellis. All side shoots are removed in the first 1-2 years. This single-trunk training creates the permanent framework for all future production. Patience here yields decades of production.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune — remove excess growth","details":"Kiwifruit produces prodigious amounts of growth. In summer (January-February), cut lateral shoots back to 5 leaves beyond the last fruit. Remove all shoots growing into the canopy centre. This is an ongoing summer task.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Do a winter dormant prune — annual reset","details":"In winter while fully dormant, cut all this season's fruited laterals back to 2-3 buds. Remove 1-2 of the oldest permanent arms each year and replace with vigorous new growth. Annual dormant pruning is what makes kiwifruit sustainable.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1825,"activity":"Harvest in late autumn — do not leave in warmth","details":"Harvest in May-June when firmness is correct (firm, not hard, and starch-iodine test shows 6-8% starch remaining). Kiwifruit do not ripen on the vine — they ripen in storage after picking. An ethylene sachet in a sealed bag accelerates ripening.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — late frosts can damage blossom
climate_note: Requires male and female plants (1 male per 8 females). Takes 4-5 years from planting to first crop. Requires 600-800 chill hours. Vigorous vine — strong permanent pergola or trellis essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Remove all flower stalks","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Any energy going to flowering reduces the already-limited stalk production. Remove all flower stalks at the first sign.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Begin light harvest in winter","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Harvest only in June-August (coolest months). Take only 2-3 stalks per plant at a time. Stop completely in September. Zone 11a rhubarb is more of a novelty than a productive food crop.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires cold winters for dormancy and vigorous regrowth. The colder the winter, the better the rhubarb. Only harvest stems — leaves are toxic (contain oxalic acid). Do not harvest in year 1.

key_activities: [{"timing":1,"activity":"Transplant deeply and stake firmly","details":"Plant seedlings (raised from Oct-Nov seed) in February-March in cool zones. Firm planting is critical — wind rock causes loose, leafy sprouts instead of tight buttons. Stake each plant with a 60cm stake tied at 3 points. 60cm spacing in rows 75cm apart.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 120g/m² or complete fertiliser with high nitrogen. Repeat at 30-day intervals. Brussels sprouts are very heavy feeders — under-feeding produces small, yellowing plants.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Remove yellowing lower leaves","details":"As the plant grows, strip away yellowing lower leaves regularly. This improves airflow (reducing fungal disease), keeps the planting base clean, and directs energy into sprout development rather than old foliage.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Top the plant to concentrate sprout development","details":"When the plant is 60-70cm tall and sprouts are visible, pinch or cut out the growing tip (the top 10cm). This forces energy into sizing up the existing sprouts rather than growing taller. Results in larger, tighter buttons.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest from base upward","details":"Twist off sprouts from the bottom of the stem first when they reach 2-4cm diameter and are firm. Work up the plant over 4-6 weeks. A frost improves flavour significantly — do not rush harvest in cold zones.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Best in zone 9 — long cool season develops excellent flavour
climate_note: Slow-growing brassica. Flavour significantly improves after frost. Firm planting prevents wind rock which causes loose sprouts.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Stop nitrogen — switch to potassium","details":"When bulbs begin to swell (visible at the soil surface), stop nitrogen fertilising and apply sulphate of potash (40g/m²). This is the critical transition — nitrogen at this stage produces soft necks with poor storage life.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Stop watering when tops begin to fall","details":"When 50-70% of tops have flopped over, stop all watering. This triggers neck curing. Premature watering at this stage causes soft-necked onions that store poorly and rot within weeks.","category":"watering"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest and cure in dry conditions","details":"Lift onions when tops are fully fallen and yellowed. Lay in a single layer in a dry, airy location for 3-4 weeks. In cool zones, a dry shed or under cover is ideal. Cure until the necks are completely dry before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back to crown after main harvest","details":"After the primary harvest (central heads cut), cut the plant back to 30cm stubs. climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply mulch","details":"Deep mulch (20cm) is essential to protect roots from cold and retain moisture. extra_care: Plant against north-facing wall for maximum heat; Frost cloth when below 2°C

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant spray","details":"Spray lime sulfur or copper while leafless to control fungal diseases. Apply before bud swell. key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut back in winter and mulch","details":"Cut fronds to ground when they yellow. Apply 10cm of well-composted manure as mulch. key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply summer mulch","details":"Deep mulch (10cm) around the drip line. In zone 10, lemons need weekly deep watering in dry summer months. extra_care: Good zone for lemon — Eureka, Lisbon, Meyer
climate_note: Most widely grown backyard citrus. Eureka and Lisbon varieties are nearly ever-bearing — fruit year-round in warm zones. Meyer lemon is a hybrid with softer acidity and more cold-tolerance.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install winter frost protection — essential","details":"Frost kills mango trees under 3-4 years old outright. Cover completely with frost cloth below 4°C. Remove immediately when temperatures rise — heat under frost cloth is also damaging.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Reduce watering in winter — allow dry rest period","details":"Do not irrigate in June-August — the cool dry period triggers flowering. extra_care: Not suitable — frost kills young mango trees
climate_note: Tropical/subtropical tree requiring a warm dry period to trigger flowering. Frost kills young trees. Most varieties need 8-10 weeks of cool/dry weather to induce flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Install drip irrigation and apply mulch","details":"Consistent moisture through drip irrigation is ideal. This restores productive vigour and removes old unproductive wood. New growth emerges within 2-3 weeks and flowers within 6-8 weeks in warm zones.","category":"pruning"}]
extra_care: Treat as short-lived perennial — cut back in winter and regrows
climate_note: Heat-loving crop — needs even more warmth than tomatoes or capsicum. Harvest while skin is glossy and before seeds develop brown inside.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut down fern in winter","details":"After fronds yellow in autumn, cut to ground level. Remove and compost debris. climate_note: Perennial — do not harvest in year 1 (cool zones) or years 1-2 (warm zones). Requires winter dormancy for reliable annual cropping.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray — prevents leaf curl","details":"Apply copper while leafless. Harvest at first sign of ripeness (background colour change, slight softness) and refrigerate immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Low-chill varieties: Anzac, Red Haven, Flavorcrest
climate_note: Like nectarine — requires winter chilling. Most productive and best flavour in zones with 500-1000 chill hours. Brown rot at harvest is the primary management challenge.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Check plant for pests and disease","details":"Water weekly for the first 4-6 weeks. After establishment warrigal greens are essentially self-sufficient. No regular fertiliser needed — they evolved in nutrient-poor coastal conditions.","category":"watering"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Begin cut-and-come-again harvest","details":"Harvest young shoot tips and leaves by cutting back stems by 30-40%. The plant regrows vigorously. In cool zones, production slows in winter but rarely stops entirely.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Blanch before eating — mandatory","details":"ALWAYS blanch warrigal greens before eating: boil in a large pot of water for 2 minutes, then drain and refresh in cold water. This removes oxalates that cause kidney problems if eaten raw. After blanching, treat like spinach in any recipe.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut back hard annually","details":"Once per year, cut back hard to 15cm above ground. extra_care: Dies back in winter but regrows from roots; Blanch before eating
climate_note: Australian native coastal plant (Tetragonia tetragonioides). Edible leaves MUST be blanched (boiled 2+ minutes) before eating to reduce oxalates. Extremely drought and salt tolerant.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"In tropical and subtropical soils, nutrients leach quickly. climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Erect trellis","details":"Snow peas are climbing plants (1-1.5m). Net or string trellis works well.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at first flower. Peas fix their own nitrogen — do not add nitrogen fertiliser. climate_note: Flat edible-pod peas. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Harvest before seeds develop inside the pod. Inoculate with rhizobium.

key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Check bulb size daily in warm conditions","details":"In zone 10, the window between \"ready\" and \"too late\" is only 3-5 days in warm weather. Check daily from 35-40 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Succession sow for continuous harvest","details":"Plant a new row every 2-3 weeks through the cool season to avoid having all plants ready simultaneously.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing brassica. Harvest when bulb (swollen stem) reaches 5-8cm — do not wait or it becomes woody and splits. Quicker to harvest than most brassicas.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train new canes","details":"Tie new primocanes vertically to the trellis wires as they grow. First-year canes (primocanes) will not fruit — they develop into next year's fruiting floricanes.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after fruiting","details":"In summer after harvest, cut all floricanes (old canes that fruited) to ground level. Tie the new primocanes to the trellis horizontally — they will fruit next season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest when fully black","details":"Fruit is ready when it pulls free with almost no resistance and is fully black (not red). Taste — fully ripe blackberries are sweet, not tart. Pick every 2-3 days during the harvest window.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — use thorny or thornless varieties; Mulch roots in severe winters
climate_note: Requires 200-700 chill hours. Grown from canes or root divisions, not seedlings. Fruits on second-year canes (floricanes).

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser","details":"One application of complete citrus fertiliser (including zinc and iron trace elements) in September. In cool zones, avoid late-season feeding that stimulates frost-vulnerable new growth flushes.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install winter frost protection — mandatory in zone 9","details":"Protect all bare-ground lime trees below 2°C with frost cloth. Avoid heavy pruning — lime trees in cool zones are slow to recover.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest when green-yellow and aromatic","details":"Tahitian lime is technically ripe when yellow but is conventionally harvested green for market appearance. Test by squeezing — ripe lime yields slightly. In cool zones lime production is limited but quality is usually good.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Tahitian lime in warmest sheltered spot only
climate_note: Least frost-tolerant common citrus. Tahitian (Persian) lime is the standard commercial variety. Kaffir lime grown for leaves. Both are essentially ever-bearing in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train shoots onto trellis","details":"Train stems onto trellis when 10-15cm tall. In zone 10, growth is faster than in cool zones — get plants onto the trellis early.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash 25g/m² at first flower. Monitor soil moisture carefully in zone 10 — dry spells cause flower drop and empty pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days — complete before heat","details":"Harvest every 2 days at full pod development. Complete all harvesting by September in zone 10 before heat causes the crop to collapse.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Thick-walled edible pod (both pod and peas eaten together). Taller vine than snow peas — needs 1.8m support. Same management principles as snow peas and peas.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train vertically or provide 3–5m run space","details":"Pumpkin vines spread 3-6m. Test: push a fingernail into the skin — it should resist. Cure in a warm sunny position for 10-14 days before storage.","category":"harvest"}]

climate_note: Large vining crop needing 4-6m space or vertical support. Pollination by bees essential — male flowers appear first. Store cured pumpkins in cool dry conditions for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Spray copper hydroxide while leafless to prevent fungal carryover. Mulch 10cm deep, keep clear of trunk.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruitlets","details":"Thin to one fruit per cluster in October-November. Check starch-iodine test or brix levels. Harvest promptly — fruit softens quickly in warmth.","category":"harvest"}]

In warm soils, granular slow-release leaches too quickly. Harvest when solid regardless of size. Season ends before wet season onset.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Dry season only — expect smaller curds
climate_note: More cold-sensitive than broccoli. The curd (head) must be blanched by tying outer leaves over it to prevent yellowing and bitterness in sunny conditions.

Net the tree completely before colour begins to develop — usually 3-4 weeks before harvest. Cherries rain-split if a downpour occurs at ripening — harvest immediately before forecast rain. Cool zone cherry harvest: November-December.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 700-1000+ chill hours for most varieties. Among the most chill-demanding fruit trees. Needs a pollination partner (most varieties). Net for birds before harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Remove flowers in the first season","details":"For spring-planted runners, remove all flowers in the first season — this redirects energy into root and crown development and significantly improves the following year's yield. For autumn-planted runners in cool zones, allow first-year flowering.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply straw mulch at fruit set","details":"When flowers appear in spring, lay straw mulch around and under the developing fruit. Net the bed completely before the first fruit shows colour — after is too late.","category":"pest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Harvest daily when ripe — slug and snail monitoring","details":"Harvest fully red fruit daily. Check under straw and leaves daily for slug and snail damage — they cause clean semicircular bites in fruit. Apply iron-based slug pellets around the bed perimeter.","category":"harvest"}]

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection in first 3 winters","details":"Young grapefruit are vulnerable to frost damage. Cover with frost cloth when temperatures are forecast below 1°C. Remove cloth during the day to prevent overheating.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune minimally — dead wood only","details":"Remove dead wood and crossing branches after fruit removal (August-September). In cool zones, avoid any pruning that stimulates new growth before winter.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest from July onward","details":"Grapefruit holds exceptionally well on the tree — it can be harvested over a 4-6 month window. In cool zones (9a/b), fruit may not develop full sweetness — early harvests will be more tart. Taste before picking.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Least cold-tolerant of commercial citrus. Requires warm nights to develop balanced acidity and sweetness. Self-fertile but large tree — allow 6m spacing.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Apply blood and bone at 120g/m² around transplants. Broccoli is a heavy nitrogen feeder. Side-dress again at 4 weeks with complete fertiliser.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Check for cabbage white caterpillars","details":"Cabbage white butterfly caterpillars (small green grubs) destroy broccoli in weeks. Check undersides of leaves daily. Use Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) spray — safe for edibles and effective on caterpillars.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check head development","details":"In cool zone summers, heads develop well. Heads that begin to open quickly become unmarketable.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest and leave for side shoots","details":"Cut the central head with 10cm of stem. Leave the plant — multiple side shoots will develop over the following 4-6 weeks, extending the harvest significantly.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Summer crop only — sow November for harvest Feb-March
climate_note: Cool-season brassica. Cut the central head before flowers open. Side shoots continue producing after central head harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash 40g/m² at first flower. Repeat every 6 weeks through the long zone 10 fruiting season. Complete fertiliser monthly maintains plant vigour.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest at green or red stage","details":"Harvest at preferred ripeness. Green = fresh/crisp flavour; red/yellow/orange = sweeter and higher in vitamin C. Consistent harvesting extends production in zone 10 from November through to May.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Cut back and overwinter in zone 10b","details":"In zone 10b, cut plants to a 30cm framework in April-May. Mulch heavily. Most plants regrow in spring from the root system — year 2 plants are larger and often more productive than year 1.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Requires warmth to germinate and fruit. Capsicum and Peppers are the same species (Capsicum annuum) — treated identically.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest in dry season — best flavour","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, dry season thyme has the best essential oil content. Harvest freely April-October. Wet season growth is often soft and low in flavour compounds.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Hard prune","details":"Cut back by 50% at the start of the wet season. This reduces the soft growth that is vulnerable to fungal disease in humid conditions.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Replace plant","details":"Wet season stress significantly reduces thyme lifespan in warm zones. Replace every 2-3 years from cuttings. Container-grown thyme moved under cover in the wet season lasts longer.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Container growing recommended for wet season protection
climate_note: Drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial. Thrives in poor, dry, well-drained conditions. Like oregano — rich soil and overwatering reduce flavour and shorten plant life.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Install trellis and train main stem","details":"Train one main stem upward to the top of the trellis. Remove all side shoots until the main stem reaches the top wire. This establishes the permanent fruiting framework faster.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Install winter frost protection","details":"Cover the plant with frost cloth when temperatures are forecast below 2°C. Established vines (3+ years) may survive brief cold periods but young vines are vulnerable. Establishment year 1 of 3 after planting.","category":"planting"},{"timing":540,"activity":"Harvest when fruit falls or shrivels","details":"Passionfruit does not ripen further off the vine — harvest only fallen or naturally shrivelled fruit. A shrivelled, purple fruit is fully ripe and at maximum sweetness. Smooth-skinned, fully purple fruit is still underdeveloped in flavour.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Install winter frost protection","details":"Cover the plant with frost cloth when temperatures are forecast below 2°C. Established vines (3+ years) may survive brief cold periods but young vines are vulnerable. Establishment year 2 of 3 after planting.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Install winter frost protection","details":"Cover the plant with frost cloth when temperatures are forecast below 2°C. Established vines (3+ years) may survive brief cold periods but young vines are vulnerable. Establishment year 3 of 3 after planting.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Sheltered north-facing position — frost protection in first 2 winters
climate_note: Vigorous perennial vine needing a strong trellis. Self-fertile but bee pollination improves fruit set. Fusarium crown rot is the main killer — plant grafted varieties in zones 10-11.

At first sign of powdery mildew (white powder on leaves), apply sulfur fungicide and remove badly affected leaves.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":63,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser through the growing season. climate_note: Warm-season crop. Highly productive but affected by powdery mildew. Male and female flowers separate — pollination by bees essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":120,"activity":"Blanch before spring warmth arrives","details":"In zone 10, begin blanching in July-August — earlier than in cool zones. Wrap with cardboard or black plastic for 3-4 weeks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest before spring heat","details":"Harvest blanched cardoon by September in zone 10. After harvest, the plant can be cut to the ground and mulched — it will regrow for the following season.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut to ground after harvest for perennial management","details":"After harvest in zone 10, cut to ground level (30cm stubs). Apply compost mulch. The plant re-shoots strongly in autumn for the following season.","category":"pruning"}]
extra_care: Good zone — shade cloth helps blanching
climate_note: Globe artichoke relative grown for the blanched leaf stalks (not the buds). Requires blanching (excluding light for 3-4 weeks) to produce edible, mild-flavoured stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 20cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings are 5cm tall. In zone 10, thin to the lower end (15cm) — plants grow faster and thicker in warmth, and spacing prevents fungal disease.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvesting outer stems regularly","details":"Cut from the outside regularly. In zone 10, consistent harvesting delays bolting. As soon as flower stems emerge, harvest the entire plant and resow.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Replace seasonally","details":"Zone 10 parsley rarely achieves the 12-16 month lifespan of cool-zone plants. Plan for 2-3 plantings per year rather than one long-lived plant.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Biennial herb (lives 2 years). Very slow germination (3-4 weeks) — pre-soaking in warm water for 24 hours significantly improves germination rate.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Mulch mounded rows","details":"Heavy mulch (10cm sugar cane or straw) over mounds retains moisture through the dry season and reduces weed competition. In the wet season, the mulch also moderates soil temperature.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Begin partial harvest from one end of row","details":"In tropical zones, sweet potato can be partially harvested (digging from one end of the mound) while leaving the remainder to continue growing. This staged approach is common in tropical food gardens.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Cure for sweetness","details":"Even in tropical zones, cure harvested tubers for 7-10 days in a warm (25-30°C) dry position before eating. Curing dramatically improves sweetness and texture. Store in a cool, dry, dark position — not the refrigerator.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from slips (vine cuttings), not true seedlings or seed. Needs 4-5 frost-free months minimum. Harvest triggers the development of sweetness — cure for 1-2 weeks after harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Light fortnightly liquid feeding through the dry season growing period.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":59,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Light fortnightly liquid feeding through the dry season growing period.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":73,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"Light fortnightly liquid feeding through the dry season growing period.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":87,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (4 of 4)","details":"Light fortnightly liquid feeding through the dry season growing period.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Harvest young and thin","details":"Harvest at 1-2cm shaft diameter. Do not wait for large leeks in tropical conditions. Use as a scallion substitute if full shaft development does not occur.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season allium. Deep planting and earthing up blanches the white shaft — the primary eating part. More cold-tolerant than onions.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply copper spray during minimal dormancy","details":"Apply copper during the brief semi-dormancy period (June-July). Leaf curl in warm zones can be severe — spray thoroughly.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Summer prune for maximum airflow. In zone 11a, brown rot management through canopy airflow is critical.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit aggressively","details":"Any remaining fruit after natural drop should be thinned to 15cm+. Small crops in warm zones must be individually protected from brown rot.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at first colour change — do not delay","details":"In zone 11a, harvest promptly at first ripeness signs. Brown rot can destroy a ripe peach overnight in subtropical warmth. Refrigerate immediately after picking.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Marginal — Anzac or Florida Prince as ultra-low chill option
climate_note: Like nectarine — requires winter chilling. Most productive and best flavour in zones with 500-1000 chill hours. Brown rot at harvest is the primary management challenge.

key_activities: [{"timing":0,"activity":"Succession sow every 2-3 weeks","details":"Sow direct or transplant. Press seed onto surface — lettuce needs light to germinate (do not bury deep, 3-5mm maximum). 25-30cm spacing for head lettuce, 15-20cm for leaf lettuce. In cool zones, lettuce can be grown almost year-round with succession sowing — avoid only the hottest 4-6 weeks of summer.","category":"planting"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Apply liquid nitrogen at thinning","details":"After thinning to final spacing, apply diluted fish emulsion or liquid complete fertiliser. Lettuce is a fast crop — one or two liquid feeds is sufficient for the full season.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Check for slugs and aphids","details":"In cool zones, slugs are the main lettuce pest (particularly in autumn and spring). Use iron-based slug pellets. Aphids cluster in head lettuce centres — blast with water or apply pyrethrum.","category":"pest"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Harvest before bolt","details":"Cut whole heads at the base when firm and full. For leaf lettuce, harvest outer leaves only (cut-and-come-again). Remove plants at first sign of a central flower stalk forming — bolted lettuce is immediately bitter and inedible.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool season — autumn through spring, avoid midsummer
climate_note: Bolts (goes to seed) when temperatures exceed 25°C or day length increases beyond 14 hours. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Support climbing varieties","details":"Erect 2m trellis or individual stakes before sowing. Train stems upward from 20cm height. Climbing varieties in zone 10 can produce for 8-10 weeks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Side-dress with potassium","details":"Apply sulphate of potash at 20g/m² when plants begin to flower. Beans fix nitrogen — supplemental nitrogen causes foliage at the expense of pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Pick at snap stage","details":"Harvest when pods are 10-15cm, bright green and snap cleanly. Pick every 2 days to maximise production. Beans left to mature on the plant signal the plant to stop producing.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — beans resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Mulch heavily — soil warmth is critical","details":"Apply black plastic mulch (plant through holes) or 10cm of straw mulch over the mounds. Soil warmth drives sweet potato growth — cool soils massively reduce yield. Black plastic mulch raises soil temperature by 3-5°C.","category":"planting"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Harvest before first frost","details":"Dig carefully with a fork before first autumn frost. In cool zones the tubers will be smaller than in tropical zones but perfectly good quality. Cure in a warm (25-30°C) humid position for 10-14 days — this converts starches to sugars and heals any wounds in the skin.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from slips (vine cuttings), not true seedlings or seed. Needs 4-5 frost-free months minimum. Harvest triggers the development of sweetness — cure for 1-2 weeks after harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Erect trellis","details":"Snow peas are climbing plants (1-1.5m). Have trellis or peasticks in position before germination — they begin sending out tendrils very early. Net or string trellis works well.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at first flower. Peas fix their own nitrogen — do not add nitrogen fertiliser. Potassium drives pod fill and overall yield.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Harvest when flat and pods are full","details":"Pick snow peas when the pod is flat and full width but before the peas inside begin to bulge. Once peas swell visibly inside the pod, the eating quality drops (they become starchy). Harvest every 2-3 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Clear plants at end of season and compost","details":"At season end, pull plants and compost. Snow pea roots fix nitrogen — leave roots in the soil for 2-3 weeks before digging in. This is a genuine soil improvement benefit.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Flat edible-pod peas. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Harvest before seeds develop inside the pod. Inoculate with rhizobium.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install winter frost protection — essential","details":"Frost kills mango trees under 3-4 years old outright. Cover completely with frost cloth below 4°C. Remove immediately when temperatures rise — heat under frost cloth is also damaging.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Reduce watering in winter — allow dry rest period","details":"Do not irrigate in June-August — the cool dry period triggers flowering. Premature flowering from an irrigated warm tree produces inferior small crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fruit colours and smells aromatic","details":"In zone 9b, mango may produce only in warm years. Fruit ripens November-January. Pick when the fruit colours up, has a sweet aroma and yields slightly to pressure at the tip.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Tropical/subtropical tree requiring a warm dry period to trigger flowering. Frost kills young trees. Most varieties need 8-10 weeks of cool/dry weather to induce flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin ruthlessly to 5cm spacing","details":"This is the step gardeners most often skip and most regret. Crowded carrots fork and stay small. Thin in two stages: first to 3cm at 3 weeks, then to 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check progress by brushing away soil","details":"Brush soil from the top of the root at 8-9 weeks. When the shoulder (top of root) reaches 1.5-2cm diameter, full-size roots are approaching maturity. Do not leave in the ground too long — oversize roots become woody.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest after cold for best flavour","details":"Cold temperatures convert carrot starch to sugar — autumn and winter carrots in cool zones are the sweetest. Pull by twisting and pulling steadily, or loosen soil with a fork first to avoid breaking roots.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Spring/summer crop — sow Oct-Nov; Deeply cultivated stone-free soil essential
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Do winter pruning — critical annual task","details":"In winter while completely leafless, prune all growth back to 2-bud spurs on the permanent cordon arms. This is how grapes are managed every year for life. Remove 90-95% of all growth. Leaving too many buds reduces fruit quality and disease pressure. This task cannot be skipped or simplified.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Thin shoots in spring","details":"When shoots emerge from spurs (October), thin to the 2 strongest shoots per spur. Remove tendrils that wrap around wires — they cause damage over time. Tie shoots loosely to the trellis wires.","category":"planting"},{"timing":240,"activity":"Remove suckers and apply potassium","details":"Remove any shoots emerging from below the graft union (they are from the rootstock and inferior). Apply sulphate of potash (60g per vine) when bunches are pea-sized.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest at full sugar development","details":"Cool zone grapes are harvested late (March-May) — cooler temperatures slow sugar development but retain acid, producing complex flavour. Taste bunches daily near harvest — sugar and flavour are a more reliable guide than colour alone.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — most wine and table varieties perform well
climate_note: Dormant pruning is essential — prune to 2-bud spurs each winter. Grapes fruit on current season growth from last year's wood. Requires chill hours for dormancy and reliable fruiting.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant spray","details":"Lime sulfur spray while leafless controls brown rot, leaf curl and shot hole disease. Critical in cool zones where humidity promotes fungal carryover.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after harvest in summer","details":"Apricots are pruned in summer, not winter (to avoid silver leaf disease entry points). Remove crossing branches and open the canopy to light and airflow.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit in spring","details":"Thin to 8-10cm spacing when fruitlets are marble size. Apricots are prone to alternate bearing — hard thinning in productive years reduces the problem.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured","details":"Apricots do not continue to ripen well off the tree. Harvest when fully orange and yield to gentle pressure. Process or eat immediately — shelf life is short.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Protect blossom from late frost — early flowering is the main risk
climate_note: Requires 300-900 chill hours. Flowers early — frost damage to blossom is the main risk in cool zones. Insufficient chill hours in zones 11b+.

key_activities: [{"timing":7,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings have 2 true leaves. Crowded radish produce small, poorly shaped roots. Thinnings can be eaten as radish sprouts.","category":"planting"},{"timing":22,"activity":"Check root size daily from 20 days","details":"Radish can be ready in 25 days and become pithy within 30-35 days. Left even 3-4 days too long, radish becomes pithy, hollow and extremely hot/harsh. Succession sowing is better than trying to extend a single planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fastest vegetable in the garden (25-35 days). Bolts and becomes hot/woody in heat. Harvest promptly at correct size — even 3-4 days too late produces pithy, harsh radish.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser. In warm zone soils, nutrients flush through quickly — regular light feeding is more effective than one heavy application.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":24,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser. In warm zone soils, nutrients flush through quickly — regular light feeding is more effective than one heavy application.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Check for aphids and leaf-mining flies","details":"In warm zones, additional pests including lettuce leaf-mining flies appear. In warm zone soils, nutrients flush through quickly — regular light feeding is more effective than one heavy application.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Harvest young — cut-and-come-again is best strategy","details":"In warm zones, harvest leaves young and continuously — do not wait for full head development. Full head lettuce in subtropical and tropical zones bolts before achieving commercial size. Cut individual leaves from the outside every few days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":52,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (4 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser. In warm zone soils, nutrients flush through quickly — regular light feeding is more effective than one heavy application.","category":"fertilizing"}]
extra_care: Limited cool season — choose heat-tolerant types (Cos, Oak Leaf)
climate_note: Bolts (goes to seed) when temperatures exceed 25°C or day length increases beyond 14 hours. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a winter renovation prune","details":"Remove 2 oldest canes per plant at ground level each winter. In zone 10, bushes grow vigorously — keep to 6-8 canes. Net immediately as fruit ripens — lorikeets and waxeyes strip bushes overnight.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest when fully sweet","details":"Low-chill varieties in zone 10 ripen October-December. Taste daily near harvest — the flavour jump from \"blue but tart\" to \"sweet\" is noticeable and signals picking time.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Low-chill varieties — soil pH management critical
climate_note: Soil pH 4.5-5.5 is critical — most Australian soils need acidification. Needs cross-pollination from a second variety. Chill hour requirements vary dramatically by variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Spray copper hydroxide while leafless to prevent fungal carryover. Critical in warmer zones where humidity can trigger brown rot.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Winter prune and apply fertiliser","details":"Prune to maintain open structure. Apply blood and bone plus sulphate of potash at drip line after pruning. Mulch 10cm deep, keep clear of trunk.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruitlets","details":"Thin to one fruit per cluster in October-November. In warmer zones check for codling moth larvae — use pheromone traps from September.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Check ripeness regularly","details":"Warm-climate apples ripen earlier (Feb-April). Check starch-iodine test or brix levels. Harvest promptly — fruit softens quickly in warmth.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 500-1000+ chill hours. Standard varieties fail in zones 11b+. Low-chill varieties (Anna, Dorsett Golden) possible in zone 11a only.

key_activities: [{"timing":50,"activity":"Remove laterals on indeterminate varieties","details":"Remove side shoots (\"armpit\" growth) from indeterminate varieties weekly. In zone 10, tomatoes grow vigorously and produce many laterals — allow 1 lateral to develop to a second stem on very vigorous varieties for a two-stem system.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Begin harvesting regularly — check for fruit fly","details":"In zone 10, Queensland fruit fly attacks ripe and near-ripe fruit. Apply Eco-naturalure bait from fruit set (not just at ripeness) and refresh weekly. Harvest at first blush of colour (before fully ripe) if fruit fly pressure is high. Never leave fallen fruit on the ground.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Outstanding — manage for fruit fly and catface in high humidity
climate_note: Stop setting fruit when night temperatures exceed 30°C or drop below 10°C. Consistent watering prevents blossom end rot and fruit cracking.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest from 6-8 weeks","details":"Always harvest outer leaves only — leave at least 4-6 central leaves. This cut-and-come-again method allows a single planting to produce for 12-18 months in cool zones.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Remove any yellowing leaves","details":"Remove yellowing or damaged outer leaves at the base. This keeps the planting clean, prevents fungal disease and redirects plant energy to new growth.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Replace plant at bolting","details":"Silverbeet bolts (runs to seed) in its second year or after exposure to heat. Once a central flower stalk appears, the plant is finished — remove and replace with a new sowing. Scheduled from approximately year undefined after planting.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Stop nitrogen — switch to potassium","details":"When bulbs begin to swell (visible at the soil surface), stop nitrogen fertilising and apply sulphate of potash (40g/m²). This is the critical transition — nitrogen at this stage produces soft necks with poor storage life.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Stop watering when tops begin to fall","details":"When 50-70% of tops have flopped over, stop all watering. This triggers neck curing. Premature watering at this stage causes soft-necked onions that store poorly and rot within weeks.","category":"watering"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest and cure in dry conditions","details":"Lift onions when tops are fully fallen and yellowed. Lay in a single layer in a dry, airy location for 3-4 weeks. In cool zones, a dry shed or under cover is ideal. Cure until the necks are completely dry before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest from 6-8 weeks","details":"Always harvest outer leaves only — leave at least 4-6 central leaves. This cut-and-come-again method allows a single planting to produce for 12-18 months in cool zones.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Remove any yellowing leaves","details":"Remove yellowing or damaged outer leaves at the base. This keeps the planting clean, prevents fungal disease and redirects plant energy to new growth.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Replace plant at bolting","details":"Silverbeet bolts (runs to seed) in its second year or after exposure to heat. Once a central flower stalk appears, the plant is finished — remove and replace with a new sowing. Scheduled from approximately year undefined after planting.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune to control spread if needed","details":"Sea asparagus can spread via runners in moist conditions. Trim back with shears if it exceeds its intended area. The harvested tips are the most tender part — regular tip harvesting acts as pruning.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Harvest young shoot tips 3-5cm","details":"Snap or cut the bright green young shoot tips (the tips, not the thicker woody stems). Cook briefly (blanch or saute) or eat raw in salads. The salty flavour is intense and distinctive — a little goes a long way.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian coastal native (Sarcocornia/Tecticornia species). Extremely salt-tolerant. Crunchy, salty succulent shoots harvested as a vegetable. Almost no care required once established.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Check swollen stem size regularly","details":"Start checking at 40 days — the bulb can go from ideal to woody and split within a week in growing conditions. Harvest at 5-8cm diameter while skin is still smooth.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"This is the most important instruction for kohlrabi: harvest at the correct size (5-8cm). Left too long it becomes woody, fibrous and inedible. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing brassica. Harvest when bulb (swollen stem) reaches 5-8cm — do not wait or it becomes woody and splits. Quicker to harvest than most brassicas.

key_activities: [{"timing":25,"activity":"Harvest as micro-greens or very young","details":"In warm zones harvest spinach as micro-greens (7-10cm) for the best quality. The heat-to-bolt progression is rapid — very young harvest is the only reliable approach.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Dry season attempt only — shade essential
climate_note: Most bolt-prone cool-season vegetable. Bolts within days of temperatures exceeding 20°C. Asian (Malabar) spinach is an excellent heat-tolerant substitute in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Improve bed drainage before wet season","details":"Ensure no waterlogging in wet season — asparagus crowns rot in saturated soil. Mound planting and raised beds are essential. Cut back and mulch heavily before the wet.","category":"pruning"}]
extra_care: Very limited dormancy — reduced spear production expected
climate_note: Perennial — do not harvest in year 1 (cool zones) or years 1-2 (warm zones). Requires winter dormancy for reliable annual cropping.

key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Begin rinsing and draining twice daily for 7 days","details":"Rinse with cool water through the mesh twice daily (morning and evening). Shake gently and drain completely — standing water causes mould. Keep at 18-22°C. Sprouts grow visibly between rinses.","category":"watering"},{"timing":7,"activity":"Move to light when sprouts reach 3-4cm","details":"When sprouts reach 3-4cm with seed leaves visible, move to indirect light for 1-2 days. This greens the leaves and improves nutritional content. Continue twice-daily rinsing.","category":"planting"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at 4-6cm before roots develop extensively","details":"Harvest when sprouts are 4-6cm and the first true leaves are emerging. Rinse a final time, drain well and refrigerate. Use within 3 days.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Grow indoors in any zone — not weather dependent
climate_note: Indoor crop — grown in a jar or tray, not the garden. Not zone-dependent. The same process applies in all climates.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen when thinning","details":"Liquid fish emulsion or diluted blood and bone after thinning. Spinach is a moderately heavy feeder — nitrogen drives leaf production. One or two applications through the season is sufficient.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest at 20cm height","details":"Harvest outer leaves by cutting at the base when the plant reaches 20cm. Leave the central growing tip intact — the plant regrows for 2-3 more harvests before bolting.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":40,"activity":"Remove at first bolt","details":"Once the central flower stalk begins to elongate, remove the entire plant. Bolted spinach is bitter and unpalatable within hours. Resow immediately from the succession sowing already in place.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most bolt-prone cool-season vegetable. Bolts within days of temperatures exceeding 20°C. Asian (Malabar) spinach is an excellent heat-tolerant substitute in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at first true leaf stage","details":"In warm zones, harvest rocket as micro-greens (at first true leaf, 7-10cm) before heat accelerates bolting. This very young harvest has the best flavour in warm conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool dry season — April to September
climate_note: Fast-growing salad leaf. Bolts in heat producing very pungent, almost inedible leaves. Succession sow every 10-14 days. Wild rocket (Diplotaxis) is more heat-tolerant than common rocket (Eruca).

key_activities: [{"timing":1095,"activity":"Prune lightly following harvest","details":"Prune immediately after harvest to maintain form. Remove dead wood and thin crowded branches. In zone 10, Davidson Plum can reach 6-8m — height management by selective pruning keeps the tree accessible for harvest.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1825,"activity":"Harvest deep purple berries — careful handling","details":"Ripe fruit is very soft and stains intensely. Harvest into buckets by hand — do not drop. Process immediately (freeze or cook) as fresh fruit deteriorates within 2-3 days. The fruit is too sour for fresh eating — cook or process.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good production in sheltered warm microclimate
climate_note: Australian subtropical rainforest native. Takes 5-8 years to fruit from seed; 3-4 from cutting. Fruit is extremely sour (high vitamin C) — used in jams, sauces and beverages. Tolerates shade.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Lime trees produce prolifically in warm zones and can overcrowd the canopy. After the main harvest, remove crossing branches and thin the canopy to improve airflow. This reduces fungal disease and improves fruit in the following season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting leaves or stems","details":"In warm zones Tahitian lime produces near-continuously. Harvest green for culinary use or allow to turn yellow for higher juice content. Fruit holds on the tree for several weeks — harvest as needed.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Least frost-tolerant common citrus. Tahitian (Persian) lime is the standard commercial variety. Kaffir lime grown for leaves. Both are essentially ever-bearing in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Apply complete fertiliser at 150g per plant at establishment. Side-dress with blood and bone monthly through the growing season. Cardoon grows rapidly with adequate nutrition.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Blanch stalks for eating — 3-4 weeks before harvest","details":"In late summer-autumn, tie the leaves together in a bundle around each plant and wrap with cardboard, hessian or black plastic to exclude all light. Leave for 3-4 weeks. This blanching process renders the otherwise bitter stalks pale, tender and mild.","category":"planting"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Check blanching progress","details":"After 3 weeks, peek inside the wrapping — the inner stalks should be pale yellow-white. If still green, wrap for another week. The outer stalks may still be bitter — focus on the inner pale stalks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Harvest by cutting plant at base","details":"Cut the entire plant at ground level. Remove and discard the outer green leaves. The pale inner stalks are the edible portion — trim to 30-40cm lengths. Use immediately or refrigerate.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — blanch stalks before harvest
climate_note: Globe artichoke relative grown for the blanched leaf stalks (not the buds). Requires blanching (excluding light for 3-4 weeks) to produce edible, mild-flavoured stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":0,"activity":"Select Southern Highbush or Rabbiteye varieties","details":"In zone 9, Southern Highbush (O'Neal, Sunshine Blue) or Rabbiteye types suit the chill hours available. Acidify soil to pH 4.5-5.5 six months before planting with elemental sulfur.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Mulch with pine bark","details":"Deep pine bark mulch is essential. Blueberry roots die if the top soil layer dries out. In zone 9, summer can be warm and dry — mulch protects roots through this period.","category":"planting"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest at full ripeness","details":"Let berries sit 3-5 days after turning blue before tasting. Fully ripe Southern Highbush berries are distinctly sweet. Net bushes early — birds take berries before peak ripeness.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Do a winter renovation prune","details":"Remove the 2-3 oldest canes at ground level each winter. Keep 6-8 canes total per bush. Well-maintained bushes produce for 20+ years. Scheduled from approximately year 3 after planting.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Soil pH 4.5-5.5 is critical — most Australian soils need acidification. Needs cross-pollination from a second variety. Chill hour requirements vary dramatically by variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Papaya is a very heavy feeder. Monthly complete fertiliser at 200g per plant is the minimum in cool zones. extra_care: Only in warmest coastal spots — frost protection essential
climate_note: Fast-growing tropical/subtropical tree. Short-lived (3-5 years productive). May include hermaphrodite, male or female plants from seed — hermaphrodite produces best fruit. Water-sensitive — do not waterlog.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Do winter pruning — critical annual task","details":"In winter while completely leafless, prune all growth back to 2-bud spurs on the permanent cordon arms. This task cannot be skipped or simplified.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Thin shoots in spring","details":"When shoots emerge from spurs (October), thin to the 2 strongest shoots per spur. Tie shoots loosely to the trellis wires.","category":"planting"},{"timing":240,"activity":"Remove suckers and apply potassium","details":"Remove any shoots emerging from below the graft union (they are from the rootstock and inferior). Taste bunches daily near harvest — sugar and flavour are a more reliable guide than colour alone.","category":"harvest"}]

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Remove flowers in the first season","details":"For spring-planted runners, remove all flowers in the first season — this redirects energy into root and crown development and significantly improves the following year's yield. Check under straw and leaves daily for slug and snail damage — they cause clean semicircular bites in fruit. Apply iron-based slug pellets around the bed perimeter.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from runners (not seed). Plant crowns in autumn, harvest spring. Replace plants every 2-3 years — older plants have lower yield. Protect from birds and slugs at fruit set.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Stop nitrogen — switch to potassium","details":"When bulbs begin to swell (visible at the soil surface), stop nitrogen fertilising and apply sulphate of potash (40g/m²). This is the critical transition — nitrogen at this stage produces soft necks with poor storage life.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Stop watering when tops begin to fall","details":"When 50-70% of tops have flopped over, stop all watering. This triggers neck curing. Premature watering at this stage causes soft-necked onions that store poorly and rot within weeks.","category":"watering"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest and cure in dry conditions","details":"Lift onions when tops are fully fallen and yellowed. Lay in a single layer in a dry, airy location for 3-4 weeks. In cool zones, a dry shed or under cover is ideal. Cure until the necks are completely dry before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant February-March for December-January harvest; Short day varieties for autumn planting
climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train vertically or provide 3–5m run space","details":"Pumpkin vines spread 3-6m. At first flower, switch to sulphate of potash (50g/m²) — potassium is critical for fruit development and skin cure quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Harvest when skin is hardened — before frost","details":"In cool zones, harvest all pumpkins before first frost regardless of whether fully mature — frost ruins the skin and storage life. Test: push a fingernail into the skin — it should resist. Cure in a warm sunny position for 10-14 days before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Large vining crop needing 4-6m space or vertical support. Pollination by bees essential — male flowers appear first. Store cured pumpkins in cool dry conditions for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Erect support stakes","details":"Tall varieties (Aquadulce) reach 1.2m and fall over in wind and rain. Drive stakes at row ends and run string every 30cm of height as plants grow. This prevents lodging which causes disease and reduces yield.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply potassium fertiliser","details":"Apply sulphate of potash at 30g/m² when plants reach 40cm.
