Phosphorus at sowing (superphosphate 40g/m²) improves root development.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Pinch out growing tips when pods set","details":"When the lowest pods are visible, pinch out the soft growing tips (the top 10cm of each stem). This is critical — it deters black bean aphid colonies which colonise the tips, and it redirects energy into pod filling.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest pods when plump","details":"Harvest pods when the beans inside create visible bumps in the pod wall. Do not wait until the pod turns black — beans become starchy. Double-pod varieties: harvest outer pods first. Pick from the bottom up.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season crop. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium. Do not grow where temperatures regularly exceed 21°C at flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back to crown after main harvest","details":"After the primary harvest (central heads cut), cut the plant back to 30cm stubs. In cool zones this triggers a second flush of heads in autumn. Clear all old leaf material to prevent fungal disease.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch crowns heavily for winter","details":"After the growing season, cut plants to ground level in cool zones. Apply 15cm compost mulch over the crown to protect from hard frosts. The crown overwinters underground and re-shoots in spring.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest central bud before scales open","details":"Cut the central bud (largest) first when it is 8-12cm across and the scales are still tightly closed. A small gap between scales indicates the bud is past prime. Cut with 15cm of stem for ease of eating. Side buds follow.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent production — very long lived in zone 9
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Mulch deeply and water in dry periods","details":"Apply 15cm organic mulch from trunk to drip line. Davidson Plum evolved in high-rainfall rainforest — it needs consistent moisture, especially in the first 3 years of establishment.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply native plant fertiliser","details":"Use a low-phosphorus native plant fertiliser (phosphorus toxicity kills many Australian natives). Apply in spring and summer. In cool zones, avoid late-season fertiliser that promotes frost-vulnerable new growth.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Prune minimally for form","details":"Davidson Plum naturally forms a multi-stemmed shrubby tree. Remove dead wood and crossing branches only. In cooler zones, avoid hard pruning — the tree grows slowly and regenerates slowly.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1825,"activity":"Harvest fruit before birds take them","details":"Dark purple-red berries are unmistakably ripe when deep in colour and soft. In cool zone conditions, the harvest window is short — birds and fruit bats find fruit quickly. Net if possible.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian subtropical rainforest native. Takes 5-8 years to fruit from seed; 3-4 from cutting. Fruit is extremely sour (high vitamin C) — used in jams, sauces and beverages. Tolerates shade.

Taste bunches daily near harvest — sugar and flavour are a more reliable guide than colour alone.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good zone — select cold-hardy varieties (Baco Noir, Frontenac); Mulch root zone in harsh winters

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Earth up as plants grow","details":"As leeks grow, mound soil progressively around the shaft every 3-4 weeks. This extends the length of the blanched white portion. In cool zones leeks can be earthed up 3-4 times through their growing season. Each earthing up must cover all previously exposed green growth.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Check shaft thickness","details":"Leeks are harvestable from 1.5cm shaft diameter but best at 2.5-4cm. In cool zones they hold well in the ground through winter — harvest as needed rather than all at once.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest by twisting and pulling","details":"Grip the leek at the base and twist while pulling upward. If the soil is hard, loosen with a fork first. Trim roots and outer leaves. Leeks left in the ground in cool zones continue growing and hold quality for months.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season allium. Deep planting and earthing up blanches the white shaft — the primary eating part. More cold-tolerant than onions.

key_activities: [{"timing":1,"activity":"Transplant deeply and stake firmly","details":"Plant seedlings (raised from Oct-Nov seed) in February-March in cool zones. Firm planting is critical — wind rock causes loose, leafy sprouts instead of tight buttons. Stake each plant with a 60cm stake tied at 3 points. 60cm spacing in rows 75cm apart.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 120g/m² or complete fertiliser with high nitrogen. Repeat at 30-day intervals. Brussels sprouts are very heavy feeders — under-feeding produces small, yellowing plants.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Remove yellowing lower leaves","details":"As the plant grows, strip away yellowing lower leaves regularly. This improves airflow (reducing fungal disease), keeps the planting base clean, and directs energy into sprout development rather than old foliage.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Top the plant to concentrate sprout development","details":"When the plant is 60-70cm tall and sprouts are visible, pinch or cut out the growing tip (the top 10cm). This forces energy into sizing up the existing sprouts rather than growing taller. Results in larger, tighter buttons.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest from base upward","details":"Twist off sprouts from the bottom of the stem first when they reach 2-4cm diameter and are firm. Work up the plant over 4-6 weeks. A frost improves flavour significantly — do not rush harvest in cold zones.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — cold sweetens flavour; Plant firmly and stake against alpine winds
climate_note: Slow-growing brassica. Flavour significantly improves after frost. Firm planting prevents wind rock which causes loose sprouts.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray — prevents leaf curl","details":"Apply copper hydroxide or lime sulfur while completely leafless. Peach leaf curl (Taphrina deformans) overwinters in bark and buds. A single thorough dormant spray followed by a petal-fall spray controls this disease — without it, leaf curl defoliates trees and eliminates the season.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune to open vase form","details":"Prune after harvest in January-February (not winter). Open vase form is ideal — remove any central growth that shades the fruit zone. Adequate light and airflow reduces brown rot. Annual pruning is what maintains productivity for 20+ years.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit to 15cm spacing","details":"When fruitlets are 2-3cm, thin to one fruit every 15cm. Heavy thinning feels wrong but produces large, high-quality fruit rather than many small ones. Crowded touching fruit is the primary vector for brown rot spread at harvest.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when background colour turns yellow","details":"The red blush is varietal colouration and does not indicate ripeness. Watch the background colour — when green transitions to yellow/cream, the fruit is approaching ripeness. The fruit should yield slightly to palm pressure. Pick in the cool of morning. Process quickly — ripe peaches deteriorate within 1-2 days.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good zone — choose 500-700 chill hour varieties
climate_note: Like nectarine — requires winter chilling. Most productive and best flavour in zones with 500-1000 chill hours. Brown rot at harvest is the primary management challenge.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 30cm spacing","details":"Thin to final spacing when seedlings have 3-4 leaves. Do not delay thinning — crowded fennel bolts prematurely.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Hill up soil around the base","details":"When the swollen stem (the bulb) begins to develop at the base, hill up soil around it to 5cm depth. This blanches the bulb, making it whiter and sweeter. Repeat as the bulb grows.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest before bolt or when bolting","details":"Cut the whole plant at soil level when the bulb is 8-12cm across and firm. If flower stems emerge from the centre, harvest immediately — once flowering starts the bulb becomes fibrous.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Florence fennel (bulb type) is grown for the swollen stem base. Herb fennel is more adaptable. Both bolt readily in heat. Do not plant near dill or coriander — cross-pollination affects flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest daily in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat, okra pods reach harvestable size and become fibrous within 2-3 days. During peak production in tropical zones, harvest daily. Pods at 5-8cm are ideal — tender and flavoursome.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Cut back and regrow for second season","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, cut plants back to 40cm after 4-5 months of production. Apply compost and fertiliser. The plant regrows for another productive season rather than requiring replanting.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Heat-loving tropical vegetable. Harvest pods at 5-8cm — older pods become fibrous and tough within 2-3 days of reaching harvestable size.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 20cm spacing","details":"Thin at 3-4 true leaves. Harvest thinnings as salad greens.","category":"planting"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Harvest young to avoid bitterness","details":"Zone 10 chicory becomes bitter faster than in cool zones. Begin harvesting outer leaves at 30-35 days when young and tender. Do not let plants mature fully before harvest.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Remove before heat returns","details":"If approaching summer, harvest all remaining plants before temperatures rise — heat converts palatable leaves to very bitter inedible ones within days.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Leaf quality deteriorates rapidly in heat — becomes tough and very bitter. Forcing chicory for chicons is a separate process requiring root lifting.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Harvest any buds before flowering","details":"In tropical zones, harvest buds as small as 5cm — they open to flower (and become inedible) much faster than in temperate zones.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to strongest seedling","details":"When seedlings reach 5cm, thin to one per cluster (8-10cm final spacing). Thinning is critical — overcrowded beets produce small deformed roots. Thinnings can be eaten as microgreens.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest at golf ball to tennis ball size","details":"Pull when roots are 5-8cm diameter. Cool zone beets develop good sweetness — cold temperatures convert starches to sugars. Twist off leaves leaving 3cm of stem to prevent \"bleeding\" during cooking.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season root crop. Bolts (runs to seed prematurely) in heat. Best grown in autumn, winter and spring.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Apply copper while leafless (June-July). Brown rot is the primary disease challenge in zone 10 — preventive spraying is essential.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune for airflow","details":"Prune after harvest in December-January. Open vase form. In zone 10, canopy airflow is the most important structural factor for brown rot prevention.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit — critical in warm zones","details":"Thin to 8-10cm spacing when fruitlets are 1-2cm. In zone 10 warm conditions, crowded fruit touching each other spreads brown rot rapidly before harvest.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when ripe","details":"In zone 10, plums move from ripe to overripe very quickly. Monitor daily as harvest approaches (November-December). Harvest in the morning when fruit is cool. Brown rot can destroy an entire crop overnight in warm humid conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Japanese plums (Santa Rosa, Mariposa) have lower chill requirements than European (600-800 hrs). Most varieties need cross-pollination. Summer prune to avoid silver leaf disease.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin seedlings to final spacing","details":"Thin to 30cm at 3-4 true leaves. In zone 10, crowding increases bolting risk.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Hill up around developing bulb","details":"Mound soil around the developing stem base to 5-8cm once swelling is visible. This blanching step significantly improves flavour and whitens the bulb.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest before flowering","details":"Check for flower stalk emergence from the centre daily in warm conditions. Harvest immediately at any sign of bolting, regardless of bulb size — a flowering fennel bulb is tough and anise-flavoured turns bitter.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Autumn to spring — bolts in summer
climate_note: Florence fennel (bulb type) is grown for the swollen stem base. Herb fennel is more adaptable. Both bolt readily in heat. Do not plant near dill or coriander — cross-pollination affects flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train a single permanent trunk","details":"Train a single main stem to the top of the trellis. All side shoots are removed in the first 1-2 years. This single-trunk training creates the permanent framework for all future production. Patience here yields decades of production.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune — remove excess growth","details":"Kiwifruit produces prodigious amounts of growth. In summer (January-February), cut lateral shoots back to 5 leaves beyond the last fruit. Remove all shoots growing into the canopy centre. This is an ongoing summer task.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Do a winter dormant prune — annual reset","details":"In winter while fully dormant, cut all this season's fruited laterals back to 2-3 buds. Remove 1-2 of the oldest permanent arms each year and replace with vigorous new growth. Annual dormant pruning is what makes kiwifruit sustainable.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1825,"activity":"Harvest in late autumn — do not leave in warmth","details":"Harvest in May-June when firmness is correct (firm, not hard, and starch-iodine test shows 6-8% starch remaining). Kiwifruit do not ripen on the vine — they ripen in storage after picking. An ethylene sachet in a sealed bag accelerates ripening.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires male and female plants (1 male per 8 females). Takes 4-5 years from planting to first crop. Requires 600-800 chill hours. Vigorous vine — strong permanent pergola or trellis essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main fruiting period, remove the oldest and most thorny branches. In tropical zones, finger limes can produce multiple crops per year — time pruning for after the largest crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest ripe fruit — wear thick gloves","details":"The thorns on finger limes are severe. Wear thick leather or cut-resistant gloves. Harvest individual fruit as they colour up and separate freely from the branch. In subtropical zones, harvest may run from April through to October.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good — monitor for Asian citrus psyllid in wet season
climate_note: Australian native citrus. Thorny shrub/tree from subtropical rainforest. Grafted varieties fruit from 3-4 years; seed-grown may take 7-10 years. Fruit contains "citrus caviar" vesicles.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 8-10cm","details":"Thin promptly in warm zones — overcrowding increases heat stress. Use thinnings in salads.","category":"planting"},{"timing":65,"activity":"Harvest at 5cm diameter or smaller","details":"In warm zones harvest smaller (5cm) and earlier — roots can become fibrous quickly. Do not leave in ground into the wet season or heat.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season root crop. Bolts (runs to seed prematurely) in heat. Best grown in autumn, winter and spring.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Mulch mounded rows","details":"Apply 8-10cm straw or sugar cane mulch over mounds. In zone 10, this retains moisture and moderates soil temperature through the summer growing season.","category":"planting"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Harvest when leaves begin to yellow","details":"In zone 10, harvest in February-April when vine leaves begin to yellow. Dig carefully with a fork. Cure in a warm dry shed for 10-14 days to develop sweetness and seal skin wounds.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from slips (vine cuttings), not true seedlings or seed. Needs 4-5 frost-free months minimum. Harvest triggers the development of sweetness — cure for 1-2 weeks after harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser with trace elements","details":"Apply complete citrus fertiliser (including zinc, iron, manganese) in September. One application per year in cool zones is sufficient — avoid late-season feeding that stimulates frost-vulnerable new growth.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install winter frost protection","details":"Protect plants below -3°C with frost cloth. Container plants can be moved to a frost-free shed in extreme cold. Remove protection during the day. Young trees need more protection than established trees.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do minimal structural pruning","details":"Remove dead wood and crossing branches after the coldest period passes (September). Avoid heavy pruning that removes fruiting wood — lemons fruit on young growth.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest when yellow and slightly soft","details":"In cool zones lemons may not achieve full yellow colour — partially green lemons are still ripe if they yield to light pressure and taste acidic. Harvest as needed year-round — they hold well on the tree.","category":"harvest"}]

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Install drip irrigation and apply mulch","details":"Consistent moisture through drip irrigation. Heavy mulch. In tropical zones, reduce irrigation in the wet season and ensure drainage.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Do a hard winter prune (now or within winter)","details":"Cut to a 30-40cm framework each year in June-July. Stimulates vigorous new fruiting growth. After each annual prune, production increases for the following season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Begin harvesting regularly — check for fruit fly","details":"Harvest ripe fruit consistently. Queensland fruit fly attacks peppers in zones 11-12. Use Eco-naturalure bait from fruit set. Unprotected, fruit fly can destroy a significant proportion of the crop.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Treat as perennial — cut back in cool months
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Requires warmth to germinate and fruit. Capsicum and Peppers are the same species (Capsicum annuum) — treated identically.

Peach leaf curl (Taphrina deformans) overwinters in bark and buds. key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² when first flowers appear. Use exclusion bags over individual fruit or apply approved fruit fly bait stations from fruit set. extra_care: Treat as perennial if protected from monsoon
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Needs 10°C+ at all times. Pick red for full sweetness — green capsicum is simply unripe.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² when first buds appear. High potassium drives fruit heat (capsaicin) and yield. Cool zones need maximum nutrient support to make the most of the short growing season.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Pick first fruit green to encourage production","details":"In cool zones the season is short. extra_care: Warmest available microclimate — against a heated wall
climate_note: Warm-season crop that thrives in heat. Can be treated as a perennial in frost-free zones (10b-12). Extended ripening produces full colour and maximum heat.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Copper spray while leafless to control fungal diseases including pear scab. Pear scab (Venturia pirina) is the main foliar disease — dormant spraying followed by a post-petal-fall spray controls it in most years.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune to central leader or modified leader in winter","details":"Pears are pruned more lightly than apples — they fruit on long-lived spurs that are removed only when unproductive. Do not heavily prune — pears can produce excessive vegetative growth called \"woolly butt\" if over-stimulated.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit lightly — 10-15cm spacing","details":"Thin to one fruit per cluster at 2-3cm fruitlet size. Pears thin naturally to some extent — supplement the natural drop to 10-15cm final spacing.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Harvest hard and ripen off the tree","details":"This is the most important pear-specific instruction: do not wait for pears to soften on the tree. Pick when the fruit separates cleanly with an upward twist but still feels firm. Ripen in a cool area (15-18°C) for 1-2 weeks. Beurre Bosc: harvest April-May; Williams: February-March; Packham: May-June.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — Beurre Bosc, Williams, Packham
climate_note: Requires more chill hours than apple (600-1500+ hours depending on variety). Needs a cross-pollination partner. Pears are picked hard (before soft) and ripened off the tree — unlike most fruit.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train new canes","details":"Guide new growth to trellis. Zone 10 can produce strong cane growth — train horizontal or fan-shaped to maximise sun exposure and airflow.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest","details":"Cut all fruited canes (floricanes) immediately after harvest. Tie new canes to trellis. Apply compost and potassium dressing. This renovation is the foundation of next season's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest in warm season","details":"In zone 10 blackberries ripen November-January. Pick every 1-2 days — fruit softens quickly in warmth. Pick in early morning before heat of the day.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Mulch roots well — heat stress reduces cane vigour
climate_note: Requires 200-700 chill hours. Grown from canes or root divisions, not seedlings. Fruits on second-year canes (floricanes).

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install winter frost protection — essential","details":"Frost kills mango trees under 3-4 years old outright. Cover completely with frost cloth below 4°C. Remove immediately when temperatures rise — heat under frost cloth is also damaging.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Reduce watering in winter — allow dry rest period","details":"Do not irrigate in June-August — the cool dry period triggers flowering. Premature flowering from an irrigated warm tree produces inferior small crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fruit colours and smells aromatic","details":"In zone 9b, mango may produce only in warm years. Fruit ripens November-January. Pick when the fruit colours up, has a sweet aroma and yields slightly to pressure at the tip.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Extremely marginal — sheltered coastal zone 9b only; Kensington Pride in most protected spot
climate_note: Tropical/subtropical tree requiring a warm dry period to trigger flowering. Frost kills young trees. Most varieties need 8-10 weeks of cool/dry weather to induce flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":150,"activity":"Stop watering and fertilising","details":"When approximately half the leaves have yellowed, stop all watering and fertilising. This triggers the final bulb curing process. Premature watering at this stage causes soft, poorly-wrapped bulbs that store poorly.","category":"watering"},{"timing":210,"activity":"Harvest when tops are 50% fallen","details":"Harvest when half the leaves have yellowed and fallen. climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 80g/m². In warm subtropical soils nitrogen moves quickly — liquid feeding every 2-3 weeks is better than slow-release in zone 11.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Cover with fine mesh","details":"Cabbage white butterflies and harlequin bugs are active year-round in subtropical zones. Cover immediately at transplant with fine insect mesh. Remove only for fertilising and harvesting.","category":"pest"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Check for premature bolting","details":"In zone 11, broccoli may attempt to head in warm spells. Harvest immediately when the head forms — do not wait for it to reach full size in subtropical conditions.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest and replant rather than side shoots","details":"In subtropical zones, broccoli side shoot quality declines as temperatures rise. climate_note: Cool-season brassica. Cut the central head before flowers open. Side shoots continue producing after central head harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant spray","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Copper spray in June-July while leafless. Brown rot is a serious risk in zone 10 where humidity can be higher than in cool growing regions.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune to open vase form","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Shade cloth can be used to provide some temperature reduction during fruit development.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Net at petal fall","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Net from petal fall (not just at colour) to protect any fruit that sets.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Begin harvesting fruit when ripe","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Fruiting may be erratic in zone 10a. Harvest any fruit that develops at first sign of colour change — leaving fruit too long in warm conditions causes rapid deterioration.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 700-1000+ chill hours for most varieties. Among the most chill-demanding fruit trees. Needs a pollination partner (most varieties). Net for birds before harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Mulch heavily — soil warmth is critical","details":"Apply black plastic mulch (plant through holes) or 10cm of straw mulch over the mounds. Soil warmth drives sweet potato growth — cool soils massively reduce yield. Black plastic mulch raises soil temperature by 3-5°C.","category":"planting"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Harvest before first frost","details":"Dig carefully with a fork before first autumn frost. In cool zones the tubers will be smaller than in tropical zones but perfectly good quality. Cure in a warm (25-30°C) humid position for 10-14 days — this converts starches to sugars and heals any wounds in the skin.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very marginal — very short warm season; Tunnel or glasshouse growing only
climate_note: Grown from slips (vine cuttings), not true seedlings or seed. Needs 4-5 frost-free months minimum. Harvest triggers the development of sweetness — cure for 1-2 weeks after harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply light fertiliser","details":"Light blood and bone application only. In tropical soils, nutrients leach rapidly — but garlic in tropical zones is limited by cool hours, not nutrition.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest when tops yellow","details":"In tropical zones the cool season is short. Harvest at first signs of yellowing regardless of bulb size — the window closes quickly as temperatures rise.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Tropical varieties only (Creole types) — results variable
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Install support and shade cloth","details":"In zone 11, afternoon shade cloth (30%) can reduce heat stress during the hottest months at the season edge. Erect trellis for climbing varieties before sowing.","category":"planting"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply potassium fertiliser","details":"Sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at flowering. extra_care: Grow in dry season — high humidity causes fungal pod disease
climate_note: Direct sow — beans resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation.

key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Harvest early — at 4-5cm","details":"In warm zones harvest smaller than in cool zones (4-5cm diameter). The texture is better at smaller size and the window before becoming woody is narrower.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Succession sow every 3 weeks","details":"Stagger sowings for continuous supply through the dry season.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Cool dry season — April to August
climate_note: Fast-growing brassica. Harvest when bulb (swollen stem) reaches 5-8cm — do not wait or it becomes woody and splits. Quicker to harvest than most brassicas.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting — cut-and-come-again","details":"In tropical and subtropical zones, mint grows rapidly. Harvest by cutting to 5-10cm every 3-4 weeks. Frequent cutting prevents the plant from flowering and maintains high aromatic oil content in leaves.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Cut back hard","details":"In zone 11b-12, the wet season (October-March) causes rampant growth followed by fungal disease. Cut the plant back hard at the start of the wet season and ensure excellent drainage. Consider bringing container plants undercover during the wet season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Check for fungal disease in humidity","details":"High humidity in subtropical/tropical zones promotes multiple mint fungal diseases (rust, powdery mildew). Good airflow around containers is essential. Remove affected leaves immediately. Replace plants showing severe rust.","category":"pest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Divide plant","details":"Replace pot media and divide root mass annually. Tropical soils in pots degrade more quickly than in cool zones — annual media replacement maintains productivity.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Afternoon shade required in full tropical conditions
climate_note: Perennial spreading herb — grow in containers to prevent invasive spreading throughout the garden. Regrows from roots even after killing frost.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 120g/m² or ammonium sulfate at 40g/m². Side-dress again at 4 and 8 weeks. Consistent nitrogen drives head development. Any yellowing of leaves signals nitrogen deficiency — correct immediately.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Blanch the curd as it develops","details":"When the curd (head) begins to form (visible white dome 2-3cm across), tie the largest outer leaves over it with a rubber band or soft string. This protects from sunlight which yellows and bitters the curd — blanching keeps it white and mild.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check for caterpillars under leaf cover","details":"Cabbage white caterpillars hide in the outer leaves. Check twice weekly and apply Bt spray. Caterpillar damage inside tied leaves is not visible until harvest.","category":"pest"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Harvest before curd separates","details":"Cut when the curd is solid, white and compact. Once the surface begins to look \"ricey\" (separated florets) it is past peak. In cool zones cauliflower holds on the plant for 1-2 weeks — in warm conditions it must be harvested immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: More cold-sensitive than broccoli. The curd (head) must be blanched by tying outer leaves over it to prevent yellowing and bitterness in sunny conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back in summer heat","details":"In zone 11 summer, cut back to 30cm stubs to prevent heat exhaustion of the plant. Mulch heavily and water consistently through summer.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Harvest any buds that form","details":"In subtropical zones, artichoke buds that form will open (flower) much faster than in cool zones. Harvest immediately when buds are tight — do not leave for a day in warm conditions or the scales will open.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Replace plant","details":"Artichokes in subtropical zones are shorter-lived than in cool zones. Replace from divisions every 3-4 years to maintain production quality.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Productive but requires cutting back in summer heat
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Switch to potassium at bulbing","details":"When bulbs are visibly swelling, stop nitrogen and apply sulphate of potash (30g/m²). This firms the bulb layers and improves storage quality and flavour.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Stop watering when tops yellow","details":"Stop all irrigation when 50-60% of tops have yellowed and flopped. This triggers the final curing of the neck — premature watering at this point causes soft-necked bulbs with poor storage life.","category":"watering"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest and cure — 3-4 weeks","details":"Lift when tops are fully yellowed. Lay in a dry, airy shed for 3-4 weeks. Separate the bulb clusters once tops are fully dry. In cool zones, shallots store for 6-12 months in cool, dry, dark conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted from individual bulbs — each divides into a cluster of 4-8 new bulbs at harvest. Same day-length sensitivity as onions. Cure thoroughly before storage.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin ruthlessly to 5cm spacing","details":"This is the step gardeners most often skip and most regret. Crowded carrots fork and stay small. Thin in two stages: first to 3cm at 3 weeks, then to 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check progress by brushing away soil","details":"Brush soil from the top of the root at 8-9 weeks. When the shoulder (top of root) reaches 1.5-2cm diameter, full-size roots are approaching maturity. Do not leave in the ground too long — oversize roots become woody.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest after cold for best flavour","details":"Cold temperatures convert carrot starch to sugar — autumn and winter carrots in cool zones are the sweetest. Pull by twisting and pulling steadily, or loosen soil with a fork first to avoid breaking roots.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Remove flower stalks","details":"In zone 10, rhubarb may produce more flower stalks than in cool zones. Remove all immediately at ground level.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Begin harvesting in cooler months","details":"In zone 10, rhubarb harvesting is best confined to August-October when stalks are at their best. Summer heat significantly reduces quality. Harvest by pulling, not cutting. Do not overharvest in zone 10 — the plant needs every leaf to sustain itself through the warm season.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Needs a cool elevated position — low valleys do not provide enough chill
climate_note: Requires cold winters for dormancy and vigorous regrowth. The colder the winter, the better the rhubarb. Only harvest stems — leaves are toxic (contain oxalic acid). Do not harvest in year 1.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune lightly to encourage bushy growth","details":"Tip-prune stems by 20-30% in late winter to encourage branching and denser fruiting growth. Do not prune heavily — the shrub is slow-growing in cool zones.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest dried berries on the plant","details":"Berries are harvested after they have dried naturally on the plant — they shrivel and turn brown. At this stage the flavour is concentrated and caramel-like. Pick and store in a dry container. Grind before use as a spice.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very marginal — dry sheltered position essential
climate_note: Australian native desert shrub (Solanum centrale). Extremely drought-tolerant. Berries are dried and used as a spice with caramel-tamarillo flavour. Dislikes wet soils.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Trellis and shade cloth","details":"Erect 1.5m trellis. Shade cloth above may extend the productive window by 1-2 weeks in zone 11.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash at 25g/m² at first flower. No nitrogen.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Begin harvesting young leaves regularly","details":"Harvest pods as soon as plump and snap-crisp — do not wait for full development in warm conditions. Harvest every 1-2 days. Complete harvest before October heat ends the crop.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Thick-walled edible pod (both pod and peas eaten together). Taller vine than snow peas — needs 1.8m support. Same management principles as snow peas and peas.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Begin harvesting young tips","details":"Harvest young shoot tips year-round. Cut stems back by 30-40% to stimulate regrowth. In warm zones production is continuous and prolific.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Blanch before eating — mandatory","details":"ALWAYS blanch warrigal greens: boil 2 minutes, drain, refresh in cold water, squeeze dry. The oxalates that cause kidney issues are removed by blanching. Raw consumption is not safe. Post-blanching, use exactly like spinach.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Do a hard prune to manage size","details":"In warm zones warrigal greens can become very large (2m spread). Annual hard pruning to 15-20cm keeps the plant compact and productive. The cut material is edible (blanch first).","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Australian native coastal plant (Tetragonia tetragonioides). Edible leaves MUST be blanched (boiled 2+ minutes) before eating to reduce oxalates. Extremely drought and salt tolerant.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Pinch tips","details":"In warm zones basil bolts very quickly. Pinch the growing tip as soon as the plant is established (15-20cm). Repeat pinching every 2-3 weeks throughout the season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply light liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Diluted fish emulsion or seasol fortnightly. Heavy feeding in warm climates promotes lush growth susceptible to fungal disease — keep feeding moderate.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Apply light liquid fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Diluted fish emulsion or seasol fortnightly. Heavy feeding in warm climates promotes lush growth susceptible to fungal disease — keep feeding moderate.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Check for root rot and mildew","details":"Basil downy mildew spreads rapidly in humid subtropical conditions. Ensure excellent drainage. Water in the morning only. Apply copper-based spray at first sign.","category":"pest"},{"timing":56,"activity":"Apply light liquid fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"Diluted fish emulsion or seasol fortnightly. Heavy feeding in warm climates promotes lush growth susceptible to fungal disease — keep feeding moderate.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Apply light liquid fertiliser (4 of 4)","details":"Diluted fish emulsion or seasol fortnightly. Heavy feeding in warm climates promotes lush growth susceptible to fungal disease — keep feeding moderate.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Begin harvesting leaves to delay bolting","details":"Cut stems back by a third every 2 weeks. Remove flower buds aggressively. In tropical zones basil may only produce well for 8-10 weeks before heat and humidity cause decline.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Treat as year-round crop in cool months; rest in peak summer heat
climate_note: Frost-sensitive annual. Bolts in heat. Best in warm but not extreme conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin to 5cm","details":"Thin as soon as seedlings are identifiable. In warm zones overcrowding is even more damaging than in cool zones — thinning to 5cm spacing is essential for any root development.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Begin harvesting small leaves regularly","details":"In warm zones carrots mature faster and stay at peak quality for a shorter window. Start tasting at 10 weeks (smaller, sweeter). Do not leave in the ground into the wet season.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Complete harvest before wet season","details":"Harvest all remaining carrots by September in tropical zones before monsoon rains waterlog the bed. Small roots are fine — better than leaving them to rot.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Straw mulch in winter","details":"Apply straw mulch around plants in June-July to insulate roots in any mild frosts and to protect developing fruit later in spring.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Net before colour — birds move quickly","details":"In zone 10, lorikeets and waxeyes are major strawberry predators. Net the bed before any colour development. Net to ground level — birds will walk under loose netting.","category":"pest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Check for botrytis in humid spring","details":"In zone 10 humid spring weather, grey mould (botrytis) develops in packed fruit. Ensure good airflow through the planting. Remove any affected fruit immediately. Apply registered fungicide if severe.","category":"pest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Harvest every day at peak season","details":"Zone 10 strawberries ripen rapidly in spring warmth. Harvest daily at peak. After 3-4 weeks the main flush is over — plants produce a smaller trickle until summer heat ends production.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant March-April for September-November harvest — everbearing varieties possible
climate_note: Grown from runners (not seed). Plant crowns in autumn, harvest spring. Replace plants every 2-3 years — older plants have lower yield. Protect from birds and slugs at fruit set.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply summer mulch","details":"Deep mulch (10cm) around the drip line. In zone 10, lemons need weekly deep watering in dry summer months. Drought stress causes fruit drop and bark splitting.","category":"watering"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main heavy crop, remove crossing branches and manage height for access. Lemons do not need heavy pruning — mostly thinning and access management.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting when fruit is ripe","details":"In zones 9-10, Eureka and Lisbon lemons produce multiple crops per year. Harvest when fruit reaches full size and turns from deep green to yellow. The fruit holds on the tree for months — harvest as needed.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant in sheltered position — Eureka or Lisbon variety
climate_note: Most widely grown backyard citrus. Eureka and Lisbon varieties are nearly ever-bearing — fruit year-round in warm zones. Meyer lemon is a hybrid with softer acidity and more cold-tolerance.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Begin harvesting young tips","details":"Harvest young shoot tips year-round. Cut stems back by 30-40% to stimulate regrowth. The oxalates that cause kidney issues are removed by blanching. Raw consumption is not safe. Annual hard pruning to 15-20cm keeps the plant compact and productive. The cut material is edible (blanch first).","category":"pruning"}]
extra_care: Excellent — tolerates drought and coastal conditions
climate_note: Australian native coastal plant (Tetragonia tetragonioides). Edible leaves MUST be blanched (boiled 2+ minutes) before eating to reduce oxalates. Extremely drought and salt tolerant.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin seedlings and apply liquid fertiliser","details":"Thin to 20cm when seedlings have 3-4 true leaves. Thinnings are edible. Apply diluted liquid fertiliser (fish emulsion) after thinning.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Blanch outer leaves for mild flavour (optional)","details":"For forcing or blanching: gather outer leaves and tie loosely around the heart for 7-10 days before harvest. Blanching reduces bitterness significantly. Alternatively harvest young leaves (less bitter than mature).","category":"planting"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Check for slugs and snails","details":"Chicory hearts are vulnerable to slug damage. Apply iron-based slug pellets around plants, especially in cool, moist conditions. Avoid copper-based pellets near harvest.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest as whole head or cut-and-come-again","details":"Harvest the whole plant by cutting at the base, or remove outer leaves individually and allow regrowth (cut-and-come-again). Cool zone chicory can produce for 3-4 months with cut-and-come-again management.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Leaf quality deteriorates rapidly in heat — becomes tough and very bitter. Forcing chicory for chicons is a separate process requiring root lifting.

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² at first flower. Okra is a moderate feeder — heavy nitrogen produces lush foliage at the expense of pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days — mandatory","details":"Okra pods become fibrous and inedible within 2-3 days of reaching 5-8cm. In cool zones harvest every 2 days without fail. Wear gloves — okra spines cause skin irritation. Cut with scissors, not pulling.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Remove old pods to maintain production","details":"Any pod allowed to mature beyond harvestable size signals the plant to slow production. Remove all pods including any missed oversize ones to maintain flowering.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very limited — short season only; Grow in tunnel or glasshouse
climate_note: Heat-loving tropical vegetable. Harvest pods at 5-8cm — older pods become fibrous and tough within 2-3 days of reaching harvestable size.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Blanch for at least 14 days","details":"Longer blanching period needed in warm zones to adequately reduce bitterness. 14-21 days under cover.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Complete harvest by September","details":"Harvest all remaining plants before wet season onset in tropical zones or before summer heat returns in subtropical zones.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Blanching (excluding light for 10-14 days before harvest) is essential to reduce natural bitterness.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Install supports for climbing varieties","details":"Erect 2m stakes or a trellis before plants need it. Climbing beans crop longer than bush types — worthwhile in the short growing seasons of cool zones. Direct tendrils onto the support.","category":"planting"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Use low-nitrogen fertiliser only","details":"Beans fix their own nitrogen. Apply potassium (sulphate of potash) and phosphorus only — excess nitrogen produces lush foliage and poor pod set.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest while pods are slim","details":"Pick when pods snap cleanly (before seeds bulge). In cool zones harvest every 2-3 days — pods left too long reduce further production. Picking encourages continued flowering.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Sow only after last frost — late November; Short season — bush beans preferred
climate_note: Direct sow — beans resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Install trellis and train main stem","details":"Train one main stem upward to the top of the trellis. Remove all side shoots until the main stem reaches the top wire. This establishes the permanent fruiting framework faster.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Install winter frost protection","details":"Cover the plant with frost cloth when temperatures are forecast below 2°C. Established vines (3+ years) may survive brief cold periods but young vines are vulnerable. Establishment year 1 of 3 after planting.","category":"planting"},{"timing":540,"activity":"Harvest when fruit falls or shrivels","details":"Passionfruit does not ripen further off the vine — harvest only fallen or naturally shrivelled fruit. A shrivelled, purple fruit is fully ripe and at maximum sweetness. Smooth-skinned, fully purple fruit is still underdeveloped in flavour.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Install winter frost protection","details":"Cover the plant with frost cloth when temperatures are forecast below 2°C. Established vines (3+ years) may survive brief cold periods but young vines are vulnerable. Establishment year 2 of 3 after planting.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Install winter frost protection","details":"Cover the plant with frost cloth when temperatures are forecast below 2°C. Established vines (3+ years) may survive brief cold periods but young vines are vulnerable. Establishment year 3 of 3 after planting.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Warmest frost-free coastal zone 9 only — sheltered position
climate_note: Vigorous perennial vine needing a strong trellis. Self-fertile but bee pollination improves fruit set. Fusarium crown rot is the main killer — plant grafted varieties in zones 10-11.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Improve bed drainage before wet season","details":"During the monsoon wet season, ensure no standing water near the root zone. Fig roots in waterlogged conditions develop Phytophthora root rot. Mound planting can help.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune in dry season","details":"Prune in the dry season (June-August) after fruiting. Remove crossing branches. In tropical zones figs can crop multiple times per year — time pruning for after the main dry season crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":600,"activity":"Fruit fly exclusion bagging","details":"Queensland fruit fly in tropical zones is severe. Exclusion bagging of developing fruit is strongly recommended. Apply Spinosad-based bait from fruit set as an alternative.","category":"pest"},{"timing":800,"activity":"Harvest when fully soft — process quickly","details":"Tropical fig fruit has good yield but lower sweetness than cool-zone equivalents. Harvest when soft and drooping. In tropical humidity, fresh figs deteriorate within 24 hours of harvest — dry or jam immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Extremely drought-tolerant once established. Two crops possible in warm zones: breba (on old wood, Nov) and main (on new wood, Jan-April). Most varieties are self-pollinating.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply potassium at bulbing","details":"As bulbs start to swell (visible above the soil), apply sulphate of potash at 30g/m². Stop all nitrogen. The warm dry season climate in subtropical zones assists natural curing.","category":"watering"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest and store in warm dry conditions","details":"In tropical zones, bulbs left in the ground after tops fall deteriorate rapidly. climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back to crown after main harvest","details":"After the primary harvest (central heads cut), cut the plant back to 30cm stubs. In cool zones this triggers a second flush of heads in autumn. extra_care: Excellent production — very long lived in zone 9
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 8-10cm","details":"Thin promptly in warm zones — overcrowding increases heat stress. Use thinnings in salads.","category":"planting"},{"timing":65,"activity":"Harvest at 5cm diameter or smaller","details":"In warm zones harvest smaller (5cm) and earlier — roots can become fibrous quickly. Do not leave in ground into the wet season or heat.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool season crop — April to September
climate_note: Cool-season root crop. Bolts (runs to seed prematurely) in heat. Best grown in autumn, winter and spring.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Mulch for moisture retention","details":"Apply 8cm mulch after establishment. Okra is surprisingly drought-tolerant once established but consistent moisture improves pod quality and reduces fibrous texture.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash 40g/m² at first flower. extra_care: Warm season crop — excellent in zone 10 summers
climate_note: Heat-loving tropical vegetable. Harvest pods at 5-8cm — older pods become fibrous and tough within 2-3 days of reaching harvestable size.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Remove side shoots","details":"As with cool zones, remove lateral shoots monthly for best root development.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest small roots by September","details":"Do not wait for large roots in warm zones — harvest whatever size has developed before heat returns. Small celeriac roots still have excellent flavour.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Marginal — difficult to develop large roots in subtropical heat
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season root vegetable. Takes 5-6 months from transplant. One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables — hard frosts improve flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Erect support trellis or peasticks","details":"Even \"dwarf\" peas benefit from support. Tall climbing varieties reach 1.8-2m. Push in peasticks (bushy twigs) immediately after sowing — peas send out tendrils within 2 weeks and need something to grip. Climbing varieties on a wire trellis.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium — no nitrogen needed","details":"Peas fix their own nitrogen — adding nitrogen fertiliser produces lush foliage and poor pod set. Apply sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at first flower. climate_note: Direct sow — peas resent root disturbance. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation. Pod quality drops rapidly in heat — harvest every 2-3 days.

key_activities: [{"timing":150,"activity":"Stop water early","details":"Stop watering when 30-40% of leaves yellow — this arrives sooner in subtropical zones as temperatures warm more rapidly.","category":"watering"},{"timing":210,"activity":"Harvest September-October","details":"Harvest when tops fall regardless of size. Subtropical garlic bulbs will be smaller than cool zone equivalents. Cure in a dry, airy position for 2-3 weeks. Use within 4-6 months — storage life shorter than cool zone garlic.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant June-July only — shorter cool season reduces bulb size
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Apply copper while leafless. Pear scab management is important even in zone 10.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a minimal winter prune","details":"Low-chill pears in zone 10 grow less vigorously than in cool zones. Low-chill varieties in zone 10 may set less fruit than in cool zones — thin conservatively.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Pick firm and ripen off tree","details":"Same principle as cool zones — pick firm and ripen at room temperature. Nashi (Asian pear) is an exception — it is eaten crunchy, directly from the tree.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Marginal — low-chill varieties: Honey Gold, Kieffer
climate_note: Requires more chill hours than apple (600-1500+ hours depending on variety). Needs a cross-pollination partner. Pears are picked hard (before soft) and ripened off the tree — unlike most fruit.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone or urea at 100g/m² at knee height. Repeat at shoulder height. In tropical zones, rapid growth means both feeds may be needed within 3-4 weeks of each other.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest quickly in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat the milky stage passes even faster than in temperate zones. Harvest at milky stage and refrigerate immediately — sugars convert to starch extremely rapidly in tropical heat.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Check for corn earworm","details":"Corn earworm (Helicoverpa armigera) is a major pest in subtropical and tropical zones. Apply Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) into the silk when it first emerges — before the husk closes. Repeat every 5 days until silks brown.","category":"pest"}]
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"In tropical and subtropical soils, nutrients leach quickly. key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Complete fertiliser with high nitrogen at transplant. Side-dress every 3 weeks through the cool months. If plants grow slowly or show yellowing, apply liquid fish fertiliser immediately.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Remove lower leaves and manage caterpillars","details":"Strip yellowing lower leaves. In zone 10, cabbage white butterfly is a persistent pest — apply Bt spray weekly or use exclusion netting from transplant.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Top before warm weather","details":"Top (remove growing tip) by July in zone 10 — earlier than in cooler zones. This accelerates sprout development before spring warmth arrives and causes bolting.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest before spring warmth","details":"In zone 10 the harvest window is August-September. Harvest quickly — warm spring temperatures cause sprouts to open and become bitter. Harvest all at once if warmth arrives unexpectedly.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Sow February-March for best cool season development
climate_note: Slow-growing brassica. Flavour significantly improves after frost. Firm planting prevents wind rock which causes loose sprouts.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply light fertiliser","details":"Light blood and bone application only. In tropical soils, nutrients leach rapidly — but garlic in tropical zones is limited by cool hours, not nutrition.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest when tops yellow","details":"In tropical zones the cool season is short. Harvest at first signs of yellowing regardless of bulb size — the window closes quickly as temperatures rise.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very limited — tropical varieties, dry season only
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply acidic fertiliser","details":"Pineapple prefers slightly acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5). Use azalea/camellia fertiliser or ericaceous fertiliser. Monthly application from spring to autumn.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install full frost protection in winter","details":"Move container indoors or to a frost-free shed at any temperature below 5°C. If it fruits at all, harvest when the base of the fruit begins to yellow. Do not wait for full surface yellowing — overripe pineapple ferments quickly on the plant.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from crowns, ratoons or slips (not seedlings). Takes 18-24 months from crown to fruit in warm zones; up to 3 years in cool zones. Smooth Cayenne and Bethlehem are common varieties.

key_activities: [{"timing":1095,"activity":"Prune selectively to manage height","details":"In tropical zones Davidson Plum grows vigorously — up to 10m if unmanaged. Annual post-harvest pruning to maintain height at 4-5m makes harvesting practical.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1825,"activity":"Harvest before full ripeness for best processing","details":"In tropical zones fruit may ripen in stages throughout the year. Harvest as berries turn deep purple-red, just before full softness — the fruit is more stable at this stage. Freeze excess immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian subtropical rainforest native. Takes 5-8 years to fruit from seed; 3-4 from cutting. Fruit is extremely sour (high vitamin C) — used in jams, sauces and beverages. Tolerates shade.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Do a winter dormant prune","details":"While fully leafless (June-July), prune back to 2-bud spurs on the cordon. Zone 10 produces vigorous growth — heavy pruning is the discipline that converts this vigour into high-quality fruit rather than excessive canopy.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Thin canopy for airflow — critical in zone 10","details":"In zone 10, vigorous shoot growth can shade the bunch zone excessively, causing disease and poor ripening. Remove lateral shoots from the fruiting zone (1-wire below to 2-wires above the bunch) to ensure sunlight reaches developing berries.","category":"planting"},{"timing":240,"activity":"Check for powdery mildew and bird pressure","details":"Powdery mildew (Uncinula necator) is the primary disease in zone 10. Apply sulfur spray from budburst, continuing every 10-14 days until veraison. Bird netting from veraison is essential — birds can strip a crop overnight.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest at flavour maturity — variety dependent","details":"Zone 10 grapes ripen February-April. Table grapes: pick when sweet and flavoursome. Wine grapes: pick at target brix (21-25° depending on style). Harvest in morning when grapes are cool.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Premium grape growing zone — Mediterranean climate
climate_note: Dormant pruning is essential — prune to 2-bud spurs each winter. Grapes fruit on current season growth from last year's wood. Requires chill hours for dormancy and reliable fruiting.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Apply blood and bone at 120g/m² around transplants. Broccoli is a heavy nitrogen feeder. Side-dress again at 4 weeks with complete fertiliser.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Check for cabbage white caterpillars","details":"Cabbage white butterfly caterpillars (small green grubs) destroy broccoli in weeks. Check undersides of leaves daily. Use Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) spray — safe for edibles and effective on caterpillars.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check head development","details":"In cool zone summers, heads develop well. Harvest when head is tight and dark green — do not wait for yellow florets to open. Heads that begin to open quickly become unmarketable.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest and leave for side shoots","details":"Cut the central head with 10cm of stem. Leave the plant — multiple side shoots will develop over the following 4-6 weeks, extending the harvest significantly.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Spring and summer crop — autumn crop fails in cold

Harvest every 2-3 days — pods left too long become starchy and tough. Picking stimulates continued flowering and extends the harvest by 2-3 weeks.","category":"harvest"}]

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 25-30cm spacing","details":"Thin promptly — endive needs space to form a full head. Thinnings are edible (young endive leaves are tender and less bitter than mature).","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Blanch before harvest","details":"10-14 days before harvest, tie the outer leaves loosely over the head with a rubber band, or cover with an upturned pot or plate. Blanching turns the inner leaves pale yellow and dramatically reduces bitterness — this step transforms endive from challenging to genuinely pleasant.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest by cutting at base","details":"Cut the whole plant at the base. In cool zones a frost after blanching improves flavour further. Remove the band or cover before cutting — check for slugs and caterpillars sheltering inside.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Blanching (excluding light for 10-14 days before harvest) is essential to reduce natural bitterness.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin and harvest simultaneously","details":"Thin plants to 5cm spacing, eating thinnings immediately. In warm zones, thinning itself can trigger bolt in remaining plants — be gentle.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Harvest very young for best flavour","details":"In subtropical and tropical conditions, harvest leaves very young (2-3 true leaves stage). Older leaves in warm conditions are still edible but aroma diminishes rapidly.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Collect seed","details":"Allow all bolted plants to set seed in a paper bag. Dry and store. Use as spice or re-sow in the following cool season.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool dry season only (April-August) — bolts rapidly otherwise
climate_note: Notoriously bolt-prone. Direct sow — resents transplanting. Keep cool and harvest before flower stalks emerge. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Apply copper while leafless to control brown rot and fungal overwintering. Plums are particularly susceptible to brown rot at harvest — the dormant spray is preventive foundation work.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after harvest in summer","details":"Prune in summer (January-February) not winter — to avoid silver leaf disease (Chondrostereum purpureum) which enters through winter wounds. Open vase form for Japanese plums. Seal all cuts with pruning compound.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit when marble size","details":"Thin to one fruit per 8-10cm when fruitlets are 1-2cm. This is laborious but essential — without thinning plums produce many small, low-quality fruit and alternate-year bearing becomes entrenched.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at full colour and fragrance","details":"Plums are ripe when fully coloured, slightly soft at the tip and the fruit separates easily with a slight twist. Japanese plums: December-February. European plums: March-April. Handle gently — bruising is invisible but causes rapid rot.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Japanese plums (Santa Rosa, Mariposa) have lower chill requirements than European (600-800 hrs). Most varieties need cross-pollination. Summer prune to avoid silver leaf disease.

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Calcium-rich soil amendment and potassium at first flower","details":"Apply dolomite lime (100g per plant) around the drip zone to prevent blossom end rot (calcium deficiency). At first flower, apply sulphate of potash (60g per plant). Consistent calcium and potassium are the two most important nutrients for fruit quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Remove laterals (side shoots) on indeterminate varieties","details":"For tall/indeterminate varieties: remove all side shoots (laterals) growing in the \"armpit\" between the main stem and a leaf. This keeps the plant to a single stem with maximum fruit size. Bush/determinate varieties: do not remove laterals — they are the fruiting structure.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured and aromatic","details":"Harvest when fully coloured and just yielding to gentle pressure. In cool zones, the season is short — harvest promptly. Green tomatoes picked before frost ripen well on a sunny windowsill. Do not refrigerate tomatoes — it destroys the flavour compounds.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Start indoors September for November transplant
climate_note: Stop setting fruit when night temperatures exceed 30°C or drop below 10°C. Consistent watering prevents blossom end rot and fruit cracking.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant spray","details":"Lime sulfur spray while leafless controls brown rot, leaf curl and shot hole disease. Critical in cool zones where humidity promotes fungal carryover.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after harvest in summer","details":"Apricots are pruned in summer, not winter (to avoid silver leaf disease entry points). Remove crossing branches and open the canopy to light and airflow.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit in spring","details":"Thin to 8-10cm spacing when fruitlets are marble size. Apricots are prone to alternate bearing — hard thinning in productive years reduces the problem.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured","details":"Apricots do not continue to ripen well off the tree. Harvest when fully orange and yield to gentle pressure. Process or eat immediately — shelf life is short.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant in sheltered north-facing aspect to reduce frost risk to blossom
climate_note: Requires 300-900 chill hours. Flowers early — frost damage to blossom is the main risk in cool zones. Insufficient chill hours in zones 11b+.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune to control spread if needed","details":"Sea asparagus can spread via runners in moist conditions. Trim back with shears if it exceeds its intended area. The harvested tips are the most tender part — regular tip harvesting acts as pruning.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Harvest young shoot tips 3-5cm","details":"Snap or cut the bright green young shoot tips (the tips, not the thicker woody stems). Cook briefly (blanch or saute) or eat raw in salads. The salty flavour is intense and distinctive — a little goes a long way.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian coastal native (Sarcocornia/Tecticornia species). Extremely salt-tolerant. Crunchy, salty succulent shoots harvested as a vegetable. Almost no care required once established.

key_activities: [{"timing":7,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings have 2 true leaves. Crowded radish produce small, poorly shaped roots. Thinnings can be eaten as radish sprouts.","category":"planting"},{"timing":22,"activity":"Check root size daily from 20 days","details":"Radish can be ready in 25 days and become pithy within 30-35 days. Begin checking at 20 days by brushing away soil at the base. Harvest when the root reaches 2-3cm diameter — do not wait for them to look \"finished\" above ground.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"This is the most important radish instruction: harvest at correct size (2-3cm). Left even 3-4 days too long, radish becomes pithy, hollow and extremely hot/harsh. Succession sowing is better than trying to extend a single planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fastest vegetable in the garden (25-35 days). Bolts and becomes hot/woody in heat. Harvest promptly at correct size — even 3-4 days too late produces pithy, harsh radish.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Prune after the main February-April harvest. In subtropical zones, figs can crop 2-3 times per year. Moderate pruning maintains manageable size and stimulates new fruiting wood.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":600,"activity":"Check for fruit fly","details":"Queensland fruit fly is the primary pest for figs in subtropical zones. Use exclusion bags over developing fruit clusters, or apply Eco-naturalure bait from fruit development onset. Unmanaged, fruit fly can destroy 80-100% of the crop.","category":"pest"},{"timing":800,"activity":"Harvest at first sign of softening","details":"In subtropical zones figs ripen faster and deteriorate quickly. Harvest immediately when the fruit droops and the base yields to gentle pressure. Process surplus promptly — shelf life in subtropical humidity is only 1-2 days.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very productive — net for fruit fly
climate_note: Extremely drought-tolerant once established. Two crops possible in warm zones: breba (on old wood, Nov) and main (on new wood, Jan-April). Most varieties are self-pollinating.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main fruiting period, remove the oldest and most thorny branches. In tropical zones, finger limes can produce multiple crops per year — time pruning for after the largest crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest ripe fruit — wear thick gloves","details":"The thorns on finger limes are severe. Wear thick leather or cut-resistant gloves. Harvest individual fruit as they colour up and separate freely from the branch. In subtropical zones, harvest may run from April through to October.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian native citrus. Thorny shrub/tree from subtropical rainforest. Grafted varieties fruit from 3-4 years; seed-grown may take 7-10 years. Fruit contains "citrus caviar" vesicles.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Install frost protection","details":"Young avocados are killed at -2°C. Install a frame for frost cloth before first winter. Have cloth ready from May. Remove cloth during the day to prevent overheating.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply avocado fertiliser","details":"Apply zinc-containing complete fertiliser (avocados are very zinc-sensitive) in spring. Use 200-300g per year of tree age. Apply to drip line, not trunk.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune to manageable height","details":"Keep trees to 4-5m for harvesting. Prune after fruiting in autumn. Remove any frost-damaged wood in spring after last frost risk.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest by squeeze test","details":"Avocados do not ripen on the tree — they ripen after picking. Test one fruit; if it softens in 5-7 days on the bench, the crop is ready. Harvest all with a clean cut leaving the stem attached.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires warm, frost-free conditions. Shallow roots are drought-sensitive. Type A and B varieties needed for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut down fern in winter","details":"After fronds yellow in autumn, cut to ground level. Remove and compost debris. Apply potassium-rich fertiliser (sulphate of potash) and top-dress with compost.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Begin harvesting spears","details":"Cut spears when 15-20cm tall with tight tips, using a knife 2-3cm below soil. extra_care: Allow 3 years before first harvest in cold zones
climate_note: Perennial — do not harvest in year 1 (cool zones) or years 1-2 (warm zones). Requires winter dormancy for reliable annual cropping.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Trellis and shade cloth","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not recommended). Erect 1.5m trellis. Shade cloth above may extend the productive window by 1-2 weeks in zone 11.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not recommended). Sulphate of potash at 25g/m² at first flower. No nitrogen.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Begin harvesting young leaves regularly","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not recommended). Harvest pods as soon as plump and snap-crisp — do not wait for full development in warm conditions. Harvest every 1-2 days. Complete harvest before October heat ends the crop.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Thick-walled edible pod (both pod and peas eaten together). Taller vine than snow peas — needs 1.8m support. Same management principles as snow peas and peas.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Remove flowers in the first season","details":"For spring-planted runners, remove all flowers in the first season — this redirects energy into root and crown development and significantly improves the following year's yield.
