climate_note: Grown from runners (not seed). Plant crowns in autumn, harvest spring. Replace plants every 2-3 years — older plants have lower yield. Protect from birds and slugs at fruit set.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Trim to manage spread","details":"In warm zones sea asparagus spreads vigorously. Trim annually to keep within bounds. The trimmed stems are edible.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Begin harvesting young tips","details":"In warm zones sea asparagus is productive year-round. Harvest young shoot tips (3-5cm, bright green and crunchy) at any time. Use sparingly as the salty flavour is intense.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian coastal native (Sarcocornia/Tecticornia species). Extremely salt-tolerant. Crunchy, salty succulent shoots harvested as a vegetable. Almost no care required once established.

key_activities: [{"timing":120,"activity":"Blanch in coolest months","details":"Begin blanching in June-July during the coolest available period. Quality will be below cool-zone standard but acceptable.","category":"planting"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest when mature","details":"Harvest blanched cardoon before September. Quality deteriorates quickly in subtropical warmth.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Grows well but less blanching quality without cool nights
climate_note: Globe artichoke relative grown for the blanched leaf stalks (not the buds). Requires blanching (excluding light for 3-4 weeks) to produce edible, mild-flavoured stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and apply potassium","details":"Eggplant develops to 80-100cm and branches heavily when fruiting. Stake each plant with a 1m stake. Apply sulphate of potash at 40g/m² at first flower. If pressure with a thumbnail shows no resistance, the fruit is overripe — seeds will be brown and flavour bitter. In cool zones harvest promptly at correct size to encourage continued production.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest all before frost","details":"Remove all remaining fruit before first autumn frost. Green eggplant will continue to ripen at room temperature if kept warm. Frost kills plants immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very warm microclimate required — north-facing wall or tunnel
climate_note: Heat-loving crop — needs even more warmth than tomatoes or capsicum. Harvest while skin is glossy and before seeds develop brown inside.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Mulch deeply — critical","details":"Apply 10-15cm of coarse wood chip mulch from trunk (keep 30cm clear) to drip line. Avocado roots are shallow and surface-feeding — mulch protects them from heat and drying. Nitrogen requirement is moderate — excess nitrogen reduces fruit quality. Use avocado-specific formulation.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune for structure and light penetration","details":"Maintain open canopy. Remove skirts (low hanging branches). Prune alternate sides each year to limit tree size. Scaffold branches should angle at 45-60 degrees.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest using oil content or squeeze test","details":"Hass turns black when ready. Fuerte and other green varieties — pick one test fruit, allow to soften at room temperature. If it softens evenly in 5-7 days, harvest the crop. Avoid rough handling — bruising is invisible until ripening.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Mulch heavily to protect shallow roots from temperature extremes
climate_note: Requires warm, frost-free conditions. Shallow roots are drought-sensitive. Type A and B varieties needed for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Apply mulch and install supports","details":"Deep mulch (10cm) and consistent moisture. Stake plants at planting — eggplant branches and heavy fruit cause toppling. In zone 10, eggplant is productive for 5-6 months from one planting.","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash 40g/m² at first flower, repeat every 6 weeks through fruiting. In zone 10, complete fertiliser monthly maintains long-season production.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest consistently when glossy","details":"Harvest every 3-5 days when plants are actively fruiting. Remove any overripe (dull-skinned, spongy) fruit immediately — they reduce production and attract pests.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Overwinter in zone 10b","details":"Cut plants back to a framework of main stems (30-40cm) in April. Mulch heavily. In zone 10b, eggplant reliably re-shoots for a second season from the root system.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Heat-loving crop — needs even more warmth than tomatoes or capsicum. Harvest while skin is glossy and before seeds develop brown inside.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin ruthlessly to 5cm spacing","details":"This is the step gardeners most often skip and most regret. Crowded carrots fork and stay small. Thin in two stages: first to 3cm at 3 weeks, then to 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check progress by brushing away soil","details":"Brush soil from the top of the root at 8-9 weeks. When the shoulder (top of root) reaches 1.5-2cm diameter, full-size roots are approaching maturity. Do not leave in the ground too long — oversize roots become woody.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest after cold for best flavour","details":"Cold temperatures convert carrot starch to sugar — autumn and winter carrots in cool zones are the sweetest. Pull by twisting and pulling steadily, or loosen soil with a fork first to avoid breaking roots.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Autumn and winter crop produces best flavour
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Tropical soils drain quickly. Fortnightly liquid feeding is more effective than granular slow-release in hot, freely-draining tropical conditions.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":49,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Tropical soils drain quickly. Fortnightly liquid feeding is more effective than granular slow-release in hot, freely-draining tropical conditions.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest frequently — complete by October","details":"Harvest every 1-2 days. Complete harvest by October before wet season arrives. Fortnightly liquid feeding is more effective than granular slow-release in hot, freely-draining tropical conditions.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":77,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (4 of 4)","details":"Tropical soils drain quickly. Fortnightly liquid feeding is more effective than granular slow-release in hot, freely-draining tropical conditions.","category":"fertilizing"}]
extra_care: Dry season — spider mite pressure in heat
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Highly productive but affected by powdery mildew. Male and female flowers separate — pollination by bees essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings have 3-4 true leaves. In cool conditions, coriander can be grown at 5cm spacing for leaf harvest. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Succession sow every 2-3 weeks","details":"A single coriander sowing in cool conditions may produce for only 3-4 weeks before bolting. extra_care: Autumn to spring — succession sow monthly
climate_note: Notoriously bolt-prone. Direct sow — resents transplanting. Keep cool and harvest before flower stalks emerge. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² when first flower buds appear. extra_care: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Requires warmth to germinate and fruit. Capsicum and Peppers are the same species (Capsicum annuum) — treated identically.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back to crown after main harvest","details":"After the primary harvest (central heads cut), cut the plant back to 30cm stubs. In cool zones this triggers a second flush of heads in autumn. Clear all old leaf material to prevent fungal disease.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch crowns heavily for winter","details":"After the growing season, cut plants to ground level in cool zones. extra_care: Cut back and mulch crowns heavily in winter
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 120g/m² or ammonium sulfate at 40g/m². Side-dress again at 4 and 8 weeks. Consistent nitrogen drives head development. Any yellowing of leaves signals nitrogen deficiency — correct immediately.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Blanch the curd as it develops","details":"When the curd (head) begins to form (visible white dome 2-3cm across), tie the largest outer leaves over it with a rubber band or soft string. Check twice weekly and apply Bt spray. Caterpillar damage inside tied leaves is not visible until harvest.","category":"pest"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Harvest before curd separates","details":"Cut when the curd is solid, white and compact. Once the surface begins to look \"ricey\" (separated florets) it is past peak. In cool zones cauliflower holds on the plant for 1-2 weeks — in warm conditions it must be harvested immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Summer crop only; Blanch curds by tying outer leaves over the head
climate_note: More cold-sensitive than broccoli. The curd (head) must be blanched by tying outer leaves over it to prevent yellowing and bitterness in sunny conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply low-phosphorus native plant fertiliser","details":"Finger limes are native plants sensitive to high phosphorus. Use native plant fertiliser (marked \"native\" or \"low phosphorus\") in spring. Supplement with trace elements (zinc and iron) if interveinal yellowing appears.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply mulch","details":"Finger limes evolved in moist subtropical rainforest — they need consistent moisture, especially while establishing in cool zones. Deep mulch, regular watering through summer.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove dead wood only","details":"Finger limes are naturally thorny and multi-stemmed. Prune only to remove deadwood and improve access for harvest. Heavy pruning delays fruiting.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fruit is fully coloured","details":"Finger lime fruit (2-8cm elongated cylinders) is ready when it pulls away with a slight twist and the colour matches the variety (green, yellow, red, pink or black depending on cultivar). The interior \"caviar\" should be firm pearls when cut open. Handle carefully — the thorns are sharp.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very marginal — full frost protection required every winter; Container growing recommended
climate_note: Australian native citrus. Thorny shrub/tree from subtropical rainforest. Grafted varieties fruit from 3-4 years; seed-grown may take 7-10 years. Fruit contains "citrus caviar" vesicles.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Harvest any buds before flowering","details":"In tropical zones, harvest buds as small as 5cm — they open to flower (and become inedible) much faster than in temperate zones.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":28,"activity":"Switch to potassium fertiliser","details":"Complete fertiliser at establishment. At first flower, sulphate of potash at 50g/m². High potassium produces firm, thick-skinned pumpkins that store well.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Train vines and support developing fruit","details":"In zone 10 pumpkin vines grow vigorously. Direct vines away from paths and garden beds. For vertically-trained vines, sling fruit in mesh or recycled stockings when it reaches tennis-ball size.","category":"planting"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Harvest at skin hardness and natural cord curing","details":"Harvest when the connecting stem (peduncle) begins to dry and the skin resists a fingernail. In zone 10, leave 15cm of stem on the pumpkin — this significantly improves storage life. Cure in the sun for 10-14 days before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Large vining crop needing 4-6m space or vertical support. Pollination by bees essential — male flowers appear first. Store cured pumpkins in cool dry conditions for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin promptly. In zone 10, afternoon shade extends the harvest window before bolting. Sow more frequently (every 10-14 days) to maintain continuous supply. Harvest brown seed heads and dry. Use seed as spice or for next sowing. Self-sown coriander in zone 10 gardens often fills gaps between sowings.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool season only — bolts immediately in summer heat
climate_note: Notoriously bolt-prone. Direct sow — resents transplanting. Keep cool and harvest before flower stalks emerge. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Check plant for pests and disease","details":"Water weekly for the first 4-6 weeks. After establishment warrigal greens are essentially self-sufficient. No regular fertiliser needed — they evolved in nutrient-poor coastal conditions.","category":"watering"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Begin cut-and-come-again harvest","details":"Harvest young shoot tips and leaves by cutting back stems by 30-40%. The plant regrows vigorously. In cool zones, production slows in winter but rarely stops entirely.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Blanch before eating — mandatory","details":"ALWAYS blanch warrigal greens before eating: boil in a large pot of water for 2 minutes, then drain and refresh in cold water. climate_note: Australian native coastal plant (Tetragonia tetragonioides). Edible leaves MUST be blanched (boiled 2+ minutes) before eating to reduce oxalates. Extremely drought and salt tolerant.

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² at first flower. Okra is a moderate feeder — heavy nitrogen produces lush foliage at the expense of pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days — mandatory","details":"Okra pods become fibrous and inedible within 2-3 days of reaching 5-8cm. In cool zones harvest every 2 days without fail. Wear gloves — okra spines cause skin irritation. Cut with scissors, not pulling.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Remove old pods to maintain production","details":"Any pod allowed to mature beyond harvestable size signals the plant to slow production. Remove all pods including any missed oversize ones to maintain flowering.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant December-January for best results in warm months
climate_note: Heat-loving tropical vegetable. Harvest pods at 5-8cm — older pods become fibrous and tough within 2-3 days of reaching harvestable size.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Select ratoons for continuous production","details":"Allow 2-3 ratoons per plant to develop as replacement plants. Remove excess ratoons. A well-managed pineapple planting can produce continuously for 5-7 years by cycling through ratoon generations.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Protect from fruit fly and mealybug","details":"Pineapple mealybug is the primary pest in tropical zones — it transmits pineapple wilt virus which can devastate a planting. Control ants (which farm mealybugs) by banding trunks with sticky material. Fruit fly: cover developing fruit with paper bags.","category":"pest"},{"timing":548,"activity":"Harvest when base colours and fragrance develops","details":"In tropical conditions pineapple takes 12-18 months from crown to fruit. Each ratoon fruits in 12-14 months. Harvest when the base turns yellow-gold and aroma is strong. Do not leave ripe fruit on the plant in wet season heat — it deteriorates rapidly.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from crowns, ratoons or slips (not seedlings). Takes 18-24 months from crown to fruit in warm zones; up to 3 years in cool zones. Smooth Cayenne and Bethlehem are common varieties.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Check pollination — hand-pollinate if needed","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable — tropical climate). Anna and Dorsett Golden cross-pollinate each other — plant both within 10m for reliable fruit set. Flowering may be irregular in warmer years.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a minimal dormant prune","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable — tropical climate). Remove dead wood and crossing branches only. Low-chill trees have limited dormancy — hard pruning can exhaust the tree.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest when colour develops","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable — tropical climate). Fruit may be smaller and less flavoursome than in cooler zones. Harvest as colour develops — do not wait for full softening in the heat.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 500-1000+ chill hours. Standard varieties fail in zones 11b+. Low-chill varieties (Anna, Dorsett Golden) possible in zone 11a only.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest from 6-8 weeks","details":"Always harvest outer leaves only — leave at least 4-6 central leaves. extra_care: Year-round — summer crop only in coldest zone 8a winters
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 20cm spacing","details":"When seedlings are 5cm tall, thin to 20cm. Thinnings are edible. Crowded parsley produces thin weak stems — give it space.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvest — outer stems first","details":"Cut outer stems at the base of the plant when they reach 15-20cm. Always leave at least 50% of the plant — parsley needs leaf mass to continue producing. Once flower stalks emerge, leaf quality drops immediately. Remove the plant and replace with a new sowing — do not try to harvest from a bolting parsley plant. Scheduled from approximately year undefined after planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Biennial herb (lives 2 years). Very slow germination (3-4 weeks) — pre-soaking in warm water for 24 hours significantly improves germination rate.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Tip-prune following harvest completion","details":"After berry harvest, tip-prune by 30% to encourage bushy, productive growth for the following season. The shrub can be cut back harder (50%) every 3-4 years to rejuvenate it.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest after natural drying on the plant","details":"In warm zones Akudjura berries ripen and dry quickly on the plant. Harvest when fully shrivelled and brown. The caramel-tamarillo flavour is most intense in fully dried berries. Use as a ground spice in marinades, sauces and bread.","category":"harvest"}]

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train a single permanent trunk","details":"Train a single main stem to the top of the trellis. All side shoots are removed in the first 1-2 years. This single-trunk training creates the permanent framework for all future production. Patience here yields decades of production.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune — remove excess growth","details":"Kiwifruit produces prodigious amounts of growth. This is an ongoing summer task.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Do a winter dormant prune — annual reset","details":"In winter while fully dormant, cut all this season's fruited laterals back to 2-3 buds. Remove 1-2 of the oldest permanent arms each year and replace with vigorous new growth. Annual dormant pruning is what makes kiwifruit sustainable.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1825,"activity":"Harvest in late autumn — do not leave in warmth","details":"Harvest in May-June when firmness is correct (firm, not hard, and starch-iodine test shows 6-8% starch remaining). Kiwifruit do not ripen on the vine — they ripen in storage after picking. An ethylene sachet in a sealed bag accelerates ripening.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires male and female plants (1 male per 8 females). Takes 4-5 years from planting to first crop. Requires 600-800 chill hours. Vigorous vine — strong permanent pergola or trellis essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Complete fertiliser with emphasis on nitrogen. Broccoli in zone 10 grows quickly and needs consistent feeding. key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 12-15cm spacing","details":"Thin at 5cm seedling height. They do not develop the same frost-driven sweetness as cool-zone equivalents, but autumn-winter conditions still improve flavour compared to summer production.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Complete harvest before spring warming","details":"Harvest all remaining roots by September-October before spring warmth causes re-shooting and root deterioration.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool season only — bolts in heat
climate_note: Root vegetable that improves dramatically with cold — frost converts starch to sugar. Very slow to germinate (21-28 days). Fresh seed essential — parsnip seed loses viability quickly.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After fruit removal, thin the canopy to improve airflow. Remove water shoots (vigorous vertical epicormic growth from scaffold branches) — they rarely fruit and shade productive outer branches.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured and sweet","details":"Navels ripen June-September. Valencia ripens October-January. In zone 10, flavour is excellent due to the combination of warm summer growth and cool winter ripening. Orange can hold on tree 2-3 months after maturity.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool nights in winter are needed for the best flavour (sugar-acid balance). Valencia ripens later than Navel and is the best variety for warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"When the first flower buds appear, apply sulphate of potash at 40g/m² around plants. Repeat at 6-week intervals through the fruiting period. Potassium is the key nutrient for fruit quality and yield.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Support heavy-fruiting plants","details":"Stake or cage plants as fruit develops — heavy crops can topple unsupported plants. Use soft ties. Check for aphids on new growth and blossom end rot on developing fruit (a calcium deficiency sign — ensure consistent watering).","category":"pest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest at desired colour stage","details":"Zone 10 capsicum will fully ripen to red, orange or yellow (depending on variety) in 3-4 months. climate_note: Warm-season crop. Needs 10°C+ at all times. Pick red for full sweetness — green capsicum is simply unripe.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Check for scale insects and citrus leafminer","details":"Scale insects (brown scale, soft scale) and citrus leafminer are prevalent in warm zones. Apply horticultural oil in winter when fruit is absent. Leafminer: apply oil to new flush growth to reduce larvae. Sooty mould indicates scale — treat the scale.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main harvest, prune for shape and access. Thin the canopy for airflow — this reduces fungal disease pressure in humid subtropical/tropical conditions.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest by taste — colour is unreliable in tropical zones","details":"In tropical zones, mandarin may remain partially green even when fully ripe. Taste is the only reliable indicator — fully sweet fruit with good juice is ready regardless of skin colour.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good production but flavour less intense without cool nights
climate_note: Sweet flavour requires some cool nights in autumn and winter to develop properly. More cold-tolerant than lime or grapefruit. Self-fertile. Satsuma is the most frost-hardy variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Begin harvesting at 10cm height","details":"Cut leaves with scissors 3-4cm above soil when plants reach 10cm. The plant regrows from the cut base 2-3 times before bolting. In cool zones, a single sowing can produce for 4-6 weeks.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":21,"activity":"Check for bolting — remove or allow to set seed","details":"Once flower stalks emerge, leaves become intensely peppery (nearly inedible). Remove bolting plants immediately and resow. Alternatively, allow some to flower and set seed — the seed self-sows readily and produces the next crop.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing salad leaf. Bolts in heat producing very pungent, almost inedible leaves. Succession sow every 10-14 days. Wild rocket (Diplotaxis) is more heat-tolerant than common rocket (Eruca).

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back to crown after main harvest","details":"After the primary harvest (central heads cut), cut the plant back to 30cm stubs. In cool zones this triggers a second flush of heads in autumn. Clear all old leaf material to prevent fungal disease.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch crowns heavily for winter","details":"After the growing season, cut plants to ground level in cool zones. Apply 15cm compost mulch over the crown to protect from hard frosts. The crown overwinters underground and re-shoots in spring.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest central bud before scales open","details":"Cut the central bud (largest) first when it is 8-12cm across and the scales are still tightly closed. climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvesting at pre-flowering stage","details":"In zone 10, oregano grows year-round. Harvest before flowering for maximum flavour. Cut stems to 10cm regularly to prevent woodiness.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Hard prune twice yearly","details":"Cut back hard (to 10cm) in late autumn and early spring. This prevents the plant from becoming an unproductive woody shrub within 2-3 years.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Divide plant","details":"Oregano clumps become woody and less productive after 3-4 years. Divide in spring by digging up the root mass, removing woody central portions, and replanting vigorous outer sections.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Mediterranean perennial. Thrives on neglect — poor, dry soil produces the most aromatic leaves. Do not overwater or over-fertilise.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply mulch","details":"Apply mulch around plants. In windy cool zones, the large leaves catch wind and can rock the plant — a stake at the stem base improves stability. Water 2-3 times weekly.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest at 15-20cm — every 2 days","details":"Harvest zucchini at 15-20cm with a sharp knife. This is the most important management instruction: fruit left beyond 25cm becomes seedy, woody and stops the plant from producing. Harvest every 2 days at peak season. One oversize marrow halves weekly production.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train canes onto trellis","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable). In zone 10a, erect trellis and train canes as per cool zones. Drip irrigation is preferable to overhead — wet foliage in warm conditions promotes botrytis (grey mould) which destroys raspberry crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Potassium emphasis at flowering","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable). In zone 10a where chill hours are marginal, potassium application at first flower is critical for any fruit set to occur. Apply sulphate of potash at 50g per plant. Blood and bone at budburst.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable). Same as cool zones — remove all fruited canes immediately after harvest. This renovation is the foundation of next year's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest quickly in zone 10 warmth","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable). In zone 10, harvest every 1-2 days. Ripe raspberries deteriorate very quickly in warmth. Pick in the early morning when fruit is cool.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 600-900 chill hours. Fruits on second-year canes (summer varieties) or current-year canes (autumn/everbearing varieties). Post-harvest cane removal is the key annual task.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Install drip irrigation and apply mulch","details":"Consistent moisture through drip irrigation. Heavy mulch. In tropical zones, reduce irrigation in the wet season and ensure drainage.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Do a hard winter prune (now or within winter)","details":"Cut to a 30-40cm framework each year in June-July. climate_note: Warm-season crop. Requires warmth to germinate and fruit. Capsicum and Peppers are the same species (Capsicum annuum) — treated identically.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main fruiting period (autumn-winter), remove crossing branches and shape for access. climate_note: Australian native citrus. Thorny shrub/tree from subtropical rainforest. Grafted varieties fruit from 3-4 years; seed-grown may take 7-10 years. Fruit contains "citrus caviar" vesicles.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Remove flower stalks","details":"Rhubarb occasionally sends up a flower stalk (thick round stem with seed head). Remove it immediately at ground level — it diverts energy from leaf stalks and signals the plant to stop producing.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting — pull, do not cut","details":"In spring of year 2 (August-October), harvest stalks by gripping at the base and pulling with a twisting motion. Scheduled from approximately year 2 after planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires cold winters for dormancy and vigorous regrowth. The colder the winter, the better the rhubarb. Only harvest stems — leaves are toxic (contain oxalic acid). Do not harvest in year 1.

key_activities: [{"timing":7,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin at 2 true leaves. In zone 10 warm soil, thinning delay causes crowded, forked roots faster than in cool zones.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Water at pod fill","details":"In zone 10 cool months, dry spells can cause cracking. Water every 2 days in dry weather. Mulch between rows.","category":"watering"},{"timing":22,"activity":"Check from 18 days in zone 10","details":"Zone 10 radish matures faster than cool-zone equivalents. Start checking root size at 18 days. Harvest at 2-3cm before pithy deterioration which comes quickly in warm conditions.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Harvest entire row at once if warm spell approaches","details":"If a warm spell is forecast, harvest all remaining radish regardless of size. A 2-day heat wave can make an entire sowing pithy and unusable.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool season only — bolts rapidly in summer
climate_note: Fastest vegetable in the garden (25-35 days). Bolts and becomes hot/woody in heat. Harvest promptly at correct size — even 3-4 days too late produces pithy, harsh radish.

key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Do not protect from frost — improves head quality","details":"In cool zones, a frost on the developing head triggers the formation of a tighter, less bitter head. Do not protect radicchio from frost — it benefits the crop distinctly.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest outer leaves first — check head firmness","details":"Harvest outer leaves as needed from 8-10 weeks. The central head forms at 10-12 weeks — harvest when it feels firm and compact. The brilliant red and white colouration develops with cold exposure.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut to stump for regrowth","details":"After harvesting the main head, cut the plant to a 5cm stump. climate_note: Italian chicory family. Frost reduces bitterness and tightens the head. Cut back to stump after first head harvest — radicchio regrows and produces again.

key_activities: [{"timing":50,"activity":"Check laterals for disease","details":"Remove laterals on indeterminate varieties. Monitor weekly for early blight (brown spots with yellow halo on lower leaves) and late blight (greasy dark patches) — common in subtropical/tropical humidity. Remove affected leaves immediately and apply copper-based fungicide.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Check for fruit fly — harvest early","details":"Queensland fruit fly is severe in subtropical and tropical zones. Apply Eco-naturalure bait from flowering, refreshing twice weekly. Harvest fruit at the \"breaker\" stage (first colour change) — finish ripening on the bench. This is the only practical approach in high fruit fly pressure zones.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Dry season planting — wet season fruit fly destroys unprotected crop
climate_note: Stop setting fruit when night temperatures exceed 30°C or drop below 10°C. Consistent watering prevents blossom end rot and fruit cracking.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin ruthlessly to 5cm spacing","details":"This is the step gardeners most often skip and most regret. Crowded carrots fork and stay small. Thin in two stages: first to 3cm at 3 weeks, then to 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check progress by brushing away soil","details":"Brush soil from the top of the root at 8-9 weeks. When the shoulder (top of root) reaches 1.5-2cm diameter, full-size roots are approaching maturity. Do not leave in the ground too long — oversize roots become woody.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest after cold for best flavour","details":"Cold temperatures convert carrot starch to sugar — autumn and winter carrots in cool zones are the sweetest. Pull by twisting and pulling steadily, or loosen soil with a fork first to avoid breaking roots.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Apply complete fertiliser at 150g per plant at establishment. Side-dress with blood and bone monthly through the growing season. Cardoon grows rapidly with adequate nutrition.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Blanch stalks for eating — 3-4 weeks before harvest","details":"In late summer-autumn, tie the leaves together in a bundle around each plant and wrap with cardboard, hessian or black plastic to exclude all light. This blanching process renders the otherwise bitter stalks pale, tender and mild.","category":"planting"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Check blanching progress","details":"After 3 weeks, peek inside the wrapping — the inner stalks should be pale yellow-white. If still green, wrap for another week. The outer stalks may still be bitter — focus on the inner pale stalks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Harvest by cutting plant at base","details":"Cut the entire plant at ground level. Remove and discard the outer green leaves. The pale inner stalks are the edible portion — trim to 30-40cm lengths. Use immediately or refrigerate.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Globe artichoke relative grown for the blanched leaf stalks (not the buds). Requires blanching (excluding light for 3-4 weeks) to produce edible, mild-flavoured stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 20cm spacing","details":"When seedlings are 5cm tall, thin to 20cm. Thinnings are edible. Crowded parsley produces thin weak stems — give it space.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvest — outer stems first","details":"Cut outer stems at the base of the plant when they reach 15-20cm. Always leave at least 50% of the plant — parsley needs leaf mass to continue producing. In cool zones parsley is productive for 12-16 months before bolting in its second year.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Remove plant when flowering begins","details":"Parsley bolts in its second year. Once flower stalks emerge, leaf quality drops immediately. Remove the plant and replace with a new sowing — do not try to harvest from a bolting parsley plant. Scheduled from approximately year undefined after planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Biennial herb (lives 2 years). Very slow germination (3-4 weeks) — pre-soaking in warm water for 24 hours significantly improves germination rate.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Remove lateral shoots","details":"Monthly removal of side shoots from the base of the developing root redirects energy. The root should be smooth and rounded — lateral shoots create misshapen, rough roots.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":140,"activity":"Harvest before spring warming","details":"In zone 10, harvest by August-September before spring heat arrives. Roots left in the ground into spring bolt (run to seed) and become hollow. Pull with a fork and use promptly.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season root vegetable. Takes 5-6 months from transplant. One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables — hard frosts improve flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune lightly to encourage bushy growth","details":"Tip-prune stems by 20-30% in late winter to encourage branching and denser fruiting growth. Do not prune heavily — the shrub is slow-growing in cool zones.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest dried berries on the plant","details":"Berries are harvested after they have dried naturally on the plant — they shrivel and turn brown. At this stage the flavour is concentrated and caramel-like. Pick and store in a dry container. Grind before use as a spice.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Needs excellent drainage — semi-arid conditions preferred
climate_note: Australian native desert shrub (Solanum centrale). Extremely drought-tolerant. Berries are dried and used as a spice with caramel-tamarillo flavour. Dislikes wet soils.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train vertically or provide 3–5m run space","details":"Pumpkin vines spread 3-6m. If space is limited, train up a strong trellis and support developing fruit in mesh bags. In cool zones, allow 4-6m per plant in a warm sunny position.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser as side dressing","details":"Apply complete fertiliser at 100g/m² when plants are established and spreading. At first flower, switch to sulphate of potash (50g/m²) — potassium is critical for fruit development and skin cure quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Harvest when skin is hardened — before frost","details":"In cool zones, harvest all pumpkins before first frost regardless of whether fully mature — frost ruins the skin and storage life. Test: push a fingernail into the skin — it should resist. Cure in a warm sunny position for 10-14 days before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Warm-season crop — plant after last frost
climate_note: Large vining crop needing 4-6m space or vertical support. Pollination by bees essential — male flowers appear first. Store cured pumpkins in cool dry conditions for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection — mandatory in zone 10a","details":"Cover with frost cloth when temperatures forecast below 5°C. Remove in the morning. Zone 10a winters can be marginal — the plant may not fruit in its expected timeframe in cold winters.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Select ratoon shoots for next crop","details":"After the main fruit forms and matures, the plant produces \"ratoons\" (side shoots from the base). Allow these to remain — each ratoon becomes the next fruiting plant. Remove all ratoons except the strongest 2-3.","category":"planting"},{"timing":548,"activity":"Harvest when base yellows and fragrance develops","details":"In zone 10, pineapple takes 18-24 months to fruit. Harvest when the base (bottom quarter) turns yellow-gold and the fruit develops a strong sweet aroma. Tap the side — a dull sound indicates full ripeness.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Warm sheltered position — frost protection essential
climate_note: Grown from crowns, ratoons or slips (not seedlings). Takes 18-24 months from crown to fruit in warm zones; up to 3 years in cool zones. Smooth Cayenne and Bethlehem are common varieties.

key_activities: [{"timing":25,"activity":"Harvest as micro-greens or very young","details":"In warm zones harvest spinach as micro-greens (7-10cm) for the best quality. The heat-to-bolt progression is rapid — very young harvest is the only reliable approach.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool dry season only — April to August
climate_note: Most bolt-prone cool-season vegetable. Bolts within days of temperatures exceeding 20°C. Asian (Malabar) spinach is an excellent heat-tolerant substitute in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting when 15cm tall","details":"Cut stems to 5cm above ground when plants reach 15-20cm. This stimulates bushy growth. Harvest regularly — mint not cut back becomes leggy and flavourless. Harvest before flowering for maximum aroma.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Cut back hard before flowering","details":"When flower spikes appear, cut the entire plant back to 5cm. This delays flowering and forces a new flush of aromatic leaves. A plant that flowers loses most of its essential oil content and becomes less flavoursome.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Divide plant","details":"Lift the container, remove the root mass, divide and replant the most vigorous outer sections. Discard the old central root mass — it is woody and less productive.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch roots for winter in zones 8-9","details":"After the plant dies back in autumn, mulch the container or root zone with 5cm of compost. The roots survive winter and re-shoot reliably in spring.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Dies back to roots in winter — regrows strongly in spring
climate_note: Perennial spreading herb — grow in containers to prevent invasive spreading throughout the garden. Regrows from roots even after killing frost.
