key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Mulch deeply — critical","details":"Apply 10-15cm of coarse wood chip mulch from trunk (keep 30cm clear) to drip line. Avocado roots are shallow and surface-feeding — mulch protects them from heat and drying. Renew annually.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply zinc-enriched fertiliser","details":"Apply complete fertiliser with zinc twice yearly (spring and early autumn). Nitrogen requirement is moderate — excess nitrogen reduces fruit quality. Use avocado-specific formulation.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune for structure and light penetration","details":"Maintain open canopy. Remove skirts (low hanging branches). Prune alternate sides each year to limit tree size. Scaffold branches should angle at 45-60 degrees.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest using oil content or squeeze test","details":"Hass turns black when ready. Fuerte and other green varieties — pick one test fruit, allow to soften at room temperature. If it softens evenly in 5-7 days, harvest the crop. Avoid rough handling — bruising is invisible until ripening.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Best zone for avocado production in SE Australia
climate_note: Requires warm, frost-free conditions. Shallow roots are drought-sensitive. Type A and B varieties needed for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Install drip irrigation and apply mulch","details":"Consistent moisture through drip irrigation is ideal. Heavy mulch insulates roots and prevents soil moisture loss in tropical heat.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Begin harvesting regularly","details":"Harvest fruit when glossy and firm. In tropical zones eggplant produces year-round. Monitor for two-spotted mite in dry conditions — stippling on leaves with fine webbing indicates mite presence.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Do a hard winter prune (now or within winter)","details":"Cut to a 30-40cm framework each year in June-July. This restores productive vigour and removes old unproductive wood. New growth emerges within 2-3 weeks and flowers within 6-8 weeks in warm zones.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Heat-loving crop — needs even more warmth than tomatoes or capsicum. Harvest while skin is glossy and before seeds develop brown inside.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 25-30cm spacing","details":"Thin promptly — endive needs space to form a full head. Thinnings are edible (young endive leaves are tender and less bitter than mature).","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Blanch before harvest","details":"10-14 days before harvest, tie the outer leaves loosely over the head with a rubber band, or cover with an upturned pot or plate. Blanching turns the inner leaves pale yellow and dramatically reduces bitterness — this step transforms endive from challenging to genuinely pleasant.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest by cutting at base","details":"Cut the whole plant at the base. In cool zones a frost after blanching improves flavour further. Remove the band or cover before cutting — check for slugs and caterpillars sheltering inside.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Spring and summer crop — excellent in cool conditions
climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Blanching (excluding light for 10-14 days before harvest) is essential to reduce natural bitterness.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvesting","details":"In zone 10, harvest year-round. Flavour is most intense in late spring before flowering and in summer dry conditions when essential oils concentrate.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Hard prune twice yearly","details":"Cut back by 40-50% in August (before summer) and March (after summer). Zone 10 thyme can become a woody mound rapidly without regular cutting.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Replace plant from cuttings","details":"Take spring cuttings from 8cm new growth. Strip lower leaves and insert into coarse sand. Roots form in 3-4 weeks. Replace parent plant every 4 years.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial. Thrives in poor, dry, well-drained conditions. Like oregano — rich soil and overwatering reduce flavour and shorten plant life.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 10-15cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings are 5cm tall — crowded parsnips produce forked, small roots. Thinning is the most commonly skipped and most impactful management step.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Leave in ground after frost for sweetness","details":"Parsnips can be left in the ground until needed. In cool zones, a frost triggers starch-to-sugar conversion — harvest after the first hard frost for the best flavour. This is unique to parsnips and a genuine argument for cool-zone growing.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":140,"activity":"Harvest before plants re-shoot in spring","details":"In the second spring (parsnip is biennial), plants begin to re-shoot and roots become woody and bitter. Harvest all remaining roots before they produce foliage in spring.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Root vegetable that improves dramatically with cold — frost converts starch to sugar. Very slow to germinate (21-28 days). Fresh seed essential — parsnip seed loses viability quickly.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Trellis and shade cloth","details":"Erect 1.2m trellis. 30% shade cloth above can reduce heat stress on flowering plants in marginal cool-season conditions.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at first flower. No nitrogen.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Begin harvesting young pods every 1–2 days","details":"In subtropical zones harvest snow peas very young (the pod is barely full width) and very frequently. Heat causes rapid pod filling and quality drop.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: May-July only — heat causes flower drop
climate_note: Flat edible-pod peas. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Harvest before seeds develop inside the pod. Inoculate with rhizobium.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Lime trees produce prolifically in warm zones and can overcrowd the canopy. After the main harvest, remove crossing branches and thin the canopy to improve airflow. This reduces fungal disease and improves fruit in the following season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting leaves or stems","details":"In warm zones Tahitian lime produces near-continuously. Harvest green for culinary use or allow to turn yellow for higher juice content. Fruit holds on the tree for several weeks — harvest as needed.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good production — Tahitian lime performs very well
climate_note: Least frost-tolerant common citrus. Tahitian (Persian) lime is the standard commercial variety. Kaffir lime grown for leaves. Both are essentially ever-bearing in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Install 1.5m trellis","details":"Snow peas grow vigorously in zone 10 cool conditions. A 1.5m trellis gives maximum cropping space.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 20g/m². Do not add nitrogen. In zone 10, the cool season growing period for snow peas is 8-12 weeks — fertilise precisely at flowering stage.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days","details":"In zone 10, harvest every 2 days when plants are in full production. Pods mature faster than in cool zones. Do not let pods fill with peas — harvest while flat.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Pull before spring heat","details":"Complete harvest by September in zone 10. Rising temperatures cause rapid quality deterioration and flower drop. Pull plants at first sustained warmth.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Flat edible-pod peas. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Harvest before seeds develop inside the pod. Inoculate with rhizobium.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"In tropical and subtropical soils, nutrients leach quickly. Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser is more effective than granular monthly applications.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"In tropical and subtropical soils, nutrients leach quickly. Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser is more effective than granular monthly applications.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting — cut-and-come-again","details":"Harvest outer leaves continuously. In warm zones, silverbeet growth is faster — harvest every 5-7 days rather than weekly. Never remove more than 1/3 of the leaves at once.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"In tropical and subtropical soils, nutrients leach quickly. Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser is more effective than granular monthly applications.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":56,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (4 of 4)","details":"In tropical and subtropical soils, nutrients leach quickly. Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser is more effective than granular monthly applications.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Improve bed drainage before wet season","details":"In the wet season in tropical zones, ensure no waterlogging around the roots. Raise beds if needed. Reduce fertiliser in the wet season — rapid growth in humidity promotes fungal disease.","category":"watering"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Replace plant","details":"Silverbeet in tropical zones has a shorter productive life than in cool zones. Replace plants every 9-12 months as they become large and woody.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings have 3-4 true leaves. In cool conditions, coriander can be grown at 5cm spacing for leaf harvest. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Succession sow every 2-3 weeks","details":"A single coriander sowing in cool conditions may produce for only 3-4 weeks before bolting. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.","category":"planting"},{"timing":21,"activity":"Harvest leaves before flower stalk emerges","details":"Cut leaves regularly from young plants. The moment a central flower stalk begins to rise, leaf quality drops. Harvest the entire plant at this point — stems and leaves are still edible.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":40,"activity":"Leave some plants to flower and set seed","details":"Leave one or two plants to bolt and produce seed (coriander seeds are a spice in themselves). Once seed turns brown, cut the whole stem and dry in a paper bag to collect seeds for cooking or next sowing.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Notoriously bolt-prone. Direct sow — resents transplanting. Keep cool and harvest before flower stalks emerge. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

key_activities: [{"timing":1,"activity":"Transplant deeply and stake firmly","details":"Plant seedlings (raised from Oct-Nov seed) in February-March in cool zones. Firm planting is critical — wind rock causes loose, leafy sprouts instead of tight buttons. Stake each plant with a 60cm stake tied at 3 points. 60cm spacing in rows 75cm apart.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 120g/m² or complete fertiliser with high nitrogen. Repeat at 30-day intervals. Brussels sprouts are very heavy feeders — under-feeding produces small, yellowing plants.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Remove yellowing lower leaves","details":"As the plant grows, strip away yellowing lower leaves regularly. This improves airflow (reducing fungal disease), keeps the planting base clean, and directs energy into sprout development rather than old foliage.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Top the plant to concentrate sprout development","details":"When the plant is 60-70cm tall and sprouts are visible, pinch or cut out the growing tip (the top 10cm). This forces energy into sizing up the existing sprouts rather than growing taller. Results in larger, tighter buttons.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest from base upward","details":"Twist off sprouts from the bottom of the stem first when they reach 2-4cm diameter and are firm. Work up the plant over 4-6 weeks. A frost improves flavour significantly — do not rush harvest in cold zones.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing brassica. Flavour significantly improves after frost. Firm planting prevents wind rock which causes loose sprouts.

key_activities: [{"timing":150,"activity":"Stop watering and fertilising","details":"When approximately half the leaves have yellowed, stop all watering and fertilising. This triggers the final bulb curing process. Premature watering at this stage causes soft, poorly-wrapped bulbs that store poorly.","category":"watering"},{"timing":210,"activity":"Harvest when tops are 50% fallen","details":"Harvest when half the leaves have yellowed and fallen. Do not wait until all leaves die — the outer wrapper splits and bulbs deteriorate. Lift with a fork, not by pulling leaves. Cure in a dry, airy shed for 3-4 weeks before storing or using.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"Blood and bone or urea at 80g/m² when plants reach knee height. Repeat at shoulder height. In zone 10, rapid warm-season growth means the two-feed program must be timed precisely to plant growth stage, not calendar dates.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"In zone 10 warm summers, heat and dry spells at silking are common. Water daily if needed during the 7-10 day silk emergence period. Failure here causes cobs with many missing kernels.","category":"watering"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check silk for harvest readiness","details":"Check from 60-65 days. Brown dry silks = approaching maturity. Pierce a kernel — milky liquid squirts out at peak. Harvest immediately and refrigerate or eat.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Succession sow every 3 weeks for continuous harvest","details":"Plant a new block every 3 weeks from September to December. This staggers the harvest window so not all cobs are ready simultaneously — the \"all at once\" harvest problem is the main frustration with corn.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Pinch out growing tip","details":"Pinch out the central stem tip to the first set of leaves as soon as the plant reaches 15cm. This forces bushy growth and delays flowering. A single pinch doubles leaf yield.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Check for aphids and fungal disease","details":"Cool humid conditions promote basil downy mildew (purple-grey fuzz on leaf undersides). Remove affected leaves. Improve airflow. Apply copper spray if severe. Avoid wetting foliage.","category":"pest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest before flowers open","details":"Harvest by cutting stems to just above a pair of leaves. In cool zones harvest frequently — the season is short. Remove flower buds the moment they appear to extend leaf production.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Do not plant out until after last frost
climate_note: Frost-sensitive annual. Bolts in heat. Best in warm but not extreme conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² when first flowers appear. In subtropical zones multiple flowering flushes occur — fertilise at each flush onset.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Check for fruit fly","details":"Capsicum is highly susceptible to Queensland fruit fly in zones 11-12. Use exclusion bags over individual fruit or apply approved fruit fly bait stations from fruit set. This is the primary pest risk.","category":"pest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Begin harvesting regularly","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, capsicum is productive for 12-18 months if managed as a perennial. Harvest fruit at any colour stage to keep the plant producing. Full red colour takes longest but delivers best flavour.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Needs 10°C+ at all times. Pick red for full sweetness — green capsicum is simply unripe.

key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Begin rinsing and draining twice daily for 7 days","details":"Rinse with cool water through the mesh twice daily (morning and evening). Shake gently and drain completely — standing water causes mould. Keep at 18-22°C. Sprouts grow visibly between rinses.","category":"watering"},{"timing":7,"activity":"Move to light when sprouts reach 3-4cm","details":"When sprouts reach 3-4cm with seed leaves visible, move to indirect light for 1-2 days. This greens the leaves and improves nutritional content. Continue twice-daily rinsing.","category":"planting"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at 4-6cm before roots develop extensively","details":"Harvest when sprouts are 4-6cm and the first true leaves are emerging. Rinse a final time, drain well and refrigerate. Use within 3 days.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Rinse more frequently in warm conditions
climate_note: Indoor crop — grown in a jar or tray, not the garden. Not zone-dependent. The same process applies in all climates.

key_activities: [{"timing":50,"activity":"Remove laterals on indeterminate varieties","details":"Remove side shoots (\"armpit\" growth) from indeterminate varieties weekly. In zone 10, tomatoes grow vigorously and produce many laterals — allow 1 lateral to develop to a second stem on very vigorous varieties for a two-stem system.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Begin harvesting regularly — check for fruit fly","details":"In zone 10, Queensland fruit fly attacks ripe and near-ripe fruit. Apply Eco-naturalure bait from fruit set (not just at ripeness) and refresh weekly. Harvest at first blush of colour (before fully ripe) if fruit fly pressure is high. Never leave fallen fruit on the ground.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — September to April production
climate_note: Stop setting fruit when night temperatures exceed 30°C or drop below 10°C. Consistent watering prevents blossom end rot and fruit cracking.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen when thinning","details":"Liquid fish emulsion or diluted blood and bone after thinning. Spinach is a moderately heavy feeder — nitrogen drives leaf production. One or two applications through the season is sufficient.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest at 20cm height","details":"Harvest outer leaves by cutting at the base when the plant reaches 20cm. Leave the central growing tip intact — the plant regrows for 2-3 more harvests before bolting.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":40,"activity":"Remove at first bolt","details":"Once the central flower stalk begins to elongate, remove the entire plant. Bolted spinach is bitter and unpalatable within hours. Resow immediately from the succession sowing already in place.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most bolt-prone cool-season vegetable. Bolts within days of temperatures exceeding 20°C. Asian (Malabar) spinach is an excellent heat-tolerant substitute in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":0,"activity":"Select variety carefully for chill hours","details":"Zone 9 cherry growing is reliable for 600-800 chill hour varieties. Lapins, Sunburst, and Simone perform well. Check local chill hour accumulation records before selecting variety. Plant two compatible varieties.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray in winter","details":"Apply copper spray while leafless in June-July. Zone 9 humidity in winter can harbour fungal diseases on bark.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune in summer after harvest","details":"Cherry trees are best pruned in summer (January-February in Australia) to reduce silver leaf disease (Chondrostereum purpureum) risk which enters through winter pruning cuts. Remove crossed branches and open the canopy.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Install bird netting structure","details":"Permanent netting frames over cherry trees are a sound investment in zone 9 where commercial cherry growing is common (Huon Valley, Stanthorpe region). Install before fruit colour develops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Harvest at peak ripeness","details":"Ripe cherries are deep red (or yellow for Golden Queen), firm and sweet. Taste before picking — colour alone is not a reliable indicator in zone 9 where ripening can be slow. Handle gently — bruises are invisible but cause rapid deterioration.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Marginal in zone 9b — select lowest-chill standard varieties
climate_note: Requires 700-1000+ chill hours for most varieties. Among the most chill-demanding fruit trees. Needs a pollination partner (most varieties). Net for birds before harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Check for aphids — repeat weekly for 4 weeks","details":"In zone 10, green peach aphid colonises lettuce heads. Check centres of developing heads weekly. Pyrethrum spray in the evening, or cold water blast. Row covers prevent aphid entry entirely.","category":"pest"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Harvest before temperatures rise","details":"In zone 10, lettuce holds quality for only 1-2 weeks past optimum harvest — rising spring temperatures cause rapid bolting. Harvest whole heads promptly. Leaf lettuce: harvest continuously with cut-and-come-again.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Bolts (goes to seed) when temperatures exceed 25°C or day length increases beyond 14 hours. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.

key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Begin rinsing and draining twice daily for 7 days","details":"Rinse with cool water through the mesh twice daily (morning and evening). Shake gently and drain completely — standing water causes mould. Keep at 18-22°C. Sprouts grow visibly between rinses.","category":"watering"},{"timing":7,"activity":"Move to light when sprouts reach 3-4cm","details":"When sprouts reach 3-4cm with seed leaves visible, move to indirect light for 1-2 days. This greens the leaves and improves nutritional content. Continue twice-daily rinsing.","category":"planting"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at 4-6cm before roots develop extensively","details":"Harvest when sprouts are 4-6cm and the first true leaves are emerging. Rinse a final time, drain well and refrigerate. Use within 3 days.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Indoor crop — grown in a jar or tray, not the garden. Not zone-dependent. The same process applies in all climates.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Remove flower stalks","details":"In zone 10, rhubarb may produce more flower stalks than in cool zones. Remove all immediately at ground level.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Begin harvesting in cooler months","details":"In zone 10, rhubarb harvesting is best confined to August-October when stalks are at their best. Summer heat significantly reduces quality. Harvest by pulling, not cutting. Do not overharvest in zone 10 — the plant needs every leaf to sustain itself through the warm season.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Marginal — poor winter chilling reduces stem colour and size
climate_note: Requires cold winters for dormancy and vigorous regrowth. The colder the winter, the better the rhubarb. Only harvest stems — leaves are toxic (contain oxalic acid). Do not harvest in year 1.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train onto trellis — direct young shoots upward","details":"Sugar snap peas produce vigorous growth. Direct shoots to the trellis in the first 2 weeks. Once climbing is established they self-direct.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 25g/m² at first flower. No nitrogen — peas fix their own. Potassium drives pod wall development — important for sugar snaps where the thick pod wall is the premium eating part.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Water at pod fill","details":"Consistent moisture at pod fill prevents shrivelled peas inside the pod. Water deeply every 2-3 days when plants are actively flowering and filling pods.","category":"watering"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest when pod is plump but snap-crisp","details":"Sugar snap peas are ready when the pod is rounded and full but still snaps cleanly when bent — not soft or yielding. The peas inside should be round but not hard. Harvest every 2-3 days. Overmature pods become tough and stringy.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Thick-walled edible pod (both pod and peas eaten together). Taller vine than snow peas — needs 1.8m support. Same management principles as snow peas and peas.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply potassium at bulbing","details":"Sulphate of potash at 30g/m² when bulbs begin to swell. In zone 10, the switch from nitrogen to potassium must be made earlier than in cool zones because spring warming arrives sooner.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Stop watering","details":"Stop irrigation at 40-50% top yellowing — in zone 10 the curing process is faster than in cool zones due to warmer conditions. Letting the bulbs dry in the ground for a week before lifting is beneficial.","category":"watering"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest October-November and cure quickly","details":"Lift in October-November in zone 10. Cure in a warm airy shed for 2-3 weeks. In zone 10, do not leave in the ground past November — spring heat deteriorates the bulbs rapidly.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted from individual bulbs — each divides into a cluster of 4-8 new bulbs at harvest. Same day-length sensitivity as onions. Cure thoroughly before storage.

key_activities: [{"timing":75,"activity":"Check for powdery mildew — treat if needed","details":"Powdery mildew typically appears by midsummer on squash in zone 10. Apply sulfur spray at first signs (white powder on leaf surfaces). Mildew does not spread to the fruit but defoliates the plant, reducing final fruit quality.","category":"pest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest at skin hardness — long stem essential","details":"Harvest when skin resists a fingernail and the stem connection point has dried (corky texture). Leave 10cm of stem. Cure for 10-14 days before storage. Zone 10 storage life of well-cured squash: 4-6 months.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Same principles as pumpkin. Harvest at full maturity with hard skin — unlike summer squash. Cures to 3-6 months storage. Needs bees for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin and harvest simultaneously","details":"Thin plants to 5cm spacing, eating thinnings immediately. In warm zones, thinning itself can trigger bolt in remaining plants — be gentle.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Harvest very young for best flavour","details":"In subtropical and tropical conditions, harvest leaves very young (2-3 true leaves stage). Older leaves in warm conditions are still edible but aroma diminishes rapidly.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Collect seed","details":"Allow all bolted plants to set seed in a paper bag. Dry and store. Use as spice or re-sow in the following cool season.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Notoriously bolt-prone. Direct sow — resents transplanting. Keep cool and harvest before flower stalks emerge. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After fruit removal, remove crossing branches and manage height for easy picking. Remove any dead wood or diseased material. Zone 10 mandarins grow vigorously — annual size management is important.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at colour change and taste test","details":"Each variety has a different harvest window. Colour changes to orange-red when ready. Taste regularly near the expected harvest period — sweetness and juice confirm readiness. Mandarin holds on tree for 4-6 weeks without quality loss.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Sweet flavour requires some cool nights in autumn and winter to develop properly. More cold-tolerant than lime or grapefruit. Self-fertile. Satsuma is the most frost-hardy variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser with trace elements","details":"Complete citrus fertiliser (including zinc and iron) in September. In cool zones, one application per year is appropriate. Late-season feeding stimulates soft frost-vulnerable new growth.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection for young trees","details":"Cover young trees (under 4-5 years) when frost is forecast. Established Satsuma trees can withstand -6°C. Young trees are more vulnerable — protect below -2°C.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a light annual prune","details":"After main harvest in autumn-winter, remove dead wood and crossing branches. Do not prune heavily — mandarins form on the outer canopy and heavy pruning reduces next season's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at full colour — Satsuma ripens before most citrus","details":"Satsuma ripens April-June in cool zones — one of the earliest mandarins. Satsumas can be fully ripe while still slightly green in cool zones — taste to confirm. Mandarins are the best indicator of correct harvest — taste, don't just look at colour.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Sweet flavour requires some cool nights in autumn and winter to develop properly. More cold-tolerant than lime or grapefruit. Self-fertile. Satsuma is the most frost-hardy variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting when 15cm tall","details":"Cut stems to 5cm above ground when plants reach 15-20cm. This stimulates bushy growth. Harvest regularly — mint not cut back becomes leggy and flavourless. Harvest before flowering for maximum aroma.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Cut back hard before flowering","details":"When flower spikes appear, cut the entire plant back to 5cm. This delays flowering and forces a new flush of aromatic leaves. A plant that flowers loses most of its essential oil content and becomes less flavoursome.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Divide plant","details":"Lift the container, remove the root mass, divide and replant the most vigorous outer sections. Discard the old central root mass — it is woody and less productive.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch roots for winter in zones 8-9","details":"After the plant dies back in autumn, mulch the container or root zone with 5cm of compost. The roots survive winter and re-shoot reliably in spring.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Perennial spreading herb — grow in containers to prevent invasive spreading throughout the garden. Regrows from roots even after killing frost.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at first true leaf stage","details":"In warm zones, harvest rocket as micro-greens (at first true leaf, 7-10cm) before heat accelerates bolting. This very young harvest has the best flavour in warm conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing salad leaf. Bolts in heat producing very pungent, almost inedible leaves. Succession sow every 10-14 days. Wild rocket (Diplotaxis) is more heat-tolerant than common rocket (Eruca).

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 100g/m² at planting. Side-dress with complete fertiliser at 4 weeks. Water in thoroughly after each application.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Check for cabbage white butterflies","details":"Check every 2-3 days from transplant. Bt spray is the safest and most effective control. Fine insect mesh (exclusion netting) over the bed eliminates butterfly damage entirely.","category":"pest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check head tightness","details":"A tight, domed head of uniform small florets is ready for harvest. In zone 9 autumn crops, heads develop slowly and stay tight longer in cool conditions — excellent quality.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest and continue for side shoots","details":"Cut the central head. Leave plants for side shoot production over 4-6 weeks. Autumn-harvested broccoli produces exceptional side shoots in zone 9 conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season brassica. Cut the central head before flowers open. Side shoots continue producing after central head harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":28,"activity":"Begin harvesting young tips","details":"In zone 10, harvest watercress tips at 8-10cm — younger than in cool zones — before heat intensifies the pungency beyond palatability. Harvest in the cool of the morning.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Refresh plant from cuttings","details":"Zone 10 watercress becomes woody and unproductive faster than in cool zones. Refresh with new cuttings every 4-6 months.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Partial shade and constantly wet conditions
climate_note: Aquatic or semi-aquatic plant. Grows in cool running water or in pots sat in trays of water. Bolts and becomes pungent in heat. Wild-harvested watercress is a liver fluke risk — only consume cultivated plant.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant spray","details":"Lime sulfur spray while leafless controls brown rot, leaf curl and shot hole disease. Critical in cool zones where humidity promotes fungal carryover.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after harvest in summer","details":"Apricots are pruned in summer, not winter (to avoid silver leaf disease entry points). Remove crossing branches and open the canopy to light and airflow.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit in spring","details":"Thin to 8-10cm spacing when fruitlets are marble size. Apricots are prone to alternate bearing — hard thinning in productive years reduces the problem.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured","details":"Apricots do not continue to ripen well off the tree. Harvest when fully orange and yield to gentle pressure. Process or eat immediately — shelf life is short.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 300-900 chill hours. Flowers early — frost damage to blossom is the main risk in cool zones. Insufficient chill hours in zones 11b+.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Erect support trellis or peasticks","details":"Even \"dwarf\" peas benefit from support. Tall climbing varieties reach 1.8-2m. Push in peasticks (bushy twigs) immediately after sowing — peas send out tendrils within 2 weeks and need something to grip. Climbing varieties on a wire trellis.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium — no nitrogen needed","details":"Peas fix their own nitrogen — adding nitrogen fertiliser produces lush foliage and poor pod set. Apply sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at first flower. This improves pod fill and yield significantly.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Water at pod fill","details":"Irregular watering at pod-fill stage causes peas to shrivel inside the pod (\"blind\" pods). Consistent moisture from first flower through harvest is the most important management step for peas. Mulch well.","category":"watering"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest every 2-3 days","details":"Pick peas when the pod is well-filled but the peas inside still feel round (not lumpy). Harvest every 2-3 days — pods left too long become starchy and tough. Picking stimulates continued flowering and extends the harvest by 2-3 weeks.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — peas resent root disturbance. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation. Pod quality drops rapidly in heat — harvest every 2-3 days.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant spray","details":"Lime sulfur spray while leafless controls brown rot, leaf curl and shot hole disease. Critical in cool zones where humidity promotes fungal carryover.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after harvest in summer","details":"Apricots are pruned in summer, not winter (to avoid silver leaf disease entry points). Remove crossing branches and open the canopy to light and airflow.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit in spring","details":"Thin to 8-10cm spacing when fruitlets are marble size. Apricots are prone to alternate bearing — hard thinning in productive years reduces the problem.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured","details":"Apricots do not continue to ripen well off the tree. Harvest when fully orange and yield to gentle pressure. Process or eat immediately — shelf life is short.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 300-900 chill hours. Flowers early — frost damage to blossom is the main risk in cool zones. Insufficient chill hours in zones 11b+.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Copper spray while leafless to control fungal diseases including pear scab. Pear scab (Venturia pirina) is the main foliar disease — dormant spraying followed by a post-petal-fall spray controls it in most years.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune to central leader or modified leader in winter","details":"Pears are pruned more lightly than apples — they fruit on long-lived spurs that are removed only when unproductive. Maintain the central leader. Remove crossing branches and vigorous vertical water shoots. Do not heavily prune — pears can produce excessive vegetative growth called \"woolly butt\" if over-stimulated.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit lightly — 10-15cm spacing","details":"Thin to one fruit per cluster at 2-3cm fruitlet size. Pears thin naturally to some extent — supplement the natural drop to 10-15cm final spacing.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Harvest hard and ripen off the tree","details":"This is the most important pear-specific instruction: do not wait for pears to soften on the tree. Pick when the fruit separates cleanly with an upward twist but still feels firm. Ripen in a cool area (15-18°C) for 1-2 weeks. Beurre Bosc: harvest April-May; Williams: February-March; Packham: May-June.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires more chill hours than apple (600-1500+ hours depending on variety). Needs a cross-pollination partner. Pears are picked hard (before soft) and ripened off the tree — unlike most fruit.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Check plant for pests and disease","details":"Water weekly for the first 4-6 weeks. After establishment warrigal greens are essentially self-sufficient. No regular fertiliser needed — they evolved in nutrient-poor coastal conditions.","category":"watering"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Begin cut-and-come-again harvest","details":"Harvest young shoot tips and leaves by cutting back stems by 30-40%. The plant regrows vigorously. In cool zones, production slows in winter but rarely stops entirely.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Blanch before eating — mandatory","details":"ALWAYS blanch warrigal greens before eating: boil in a large pot of water for 2 minutes, then drain and refresh in cold water. This removes oxalates that cause kidney problems if eaten raw. After blanching, treat like spinach in any recipe.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut back hard annually","details":"Once per year, cut back hard to 15cm above ground. This renovation stimulates fresh, productive growth and prevents the plant from becoming a sprawling, unmanageable mound.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Australian native coastal plant (Tetragonia tetragonioides). Edible leaves MUST be blanched (boiled 2+ minutes) before eating to reduce oxalates. Extremely drought and salt tolerant.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 20cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings are 5cm tall. In zone 10, thin to the lower end (15cm) — plants grow faster and thicker in warmth, and spacing prevents fungal disease.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvesting outer stems regularly","details":"Cut from the outside regularly. In zone 10, consistent harvesting delays bolting. As soon as flower stems emerge, harvest the entire plant and resow.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Replace seasonally","details":"Zone 10 parsley rarely achieves the 12-16 month lifespan of cool-zone plants. Plan for 2-3 plantings per year rather than one long-lived plant.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Bolts in peak summer — spring and autumn emphasis
climate_note: Biennial herb (lives 2 years). Very slow germination (3-4 weeks) — pre-soaking in warm water for 24 hours significantly improves germination rate.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Switch to potassium at bulbing","details":"When bulbs are visibly swelling, stop nitrogen and apply sulphate of potash (30g/m²). This firms the bulb layers and improves storage quality and flavour.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Stop watering when tops yellow","details":"Stop all irrigation when 50-60% of tops have yellowed and flopped. This triggers the final curing of the neck — premature watering at this point causes soft-necked bulbs with poor storage life.","category":"watering"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest and cure — 3-4 weeks","details":"Lift when tops are fully yellowed. Lay in a dry, airy shed for 3-4 weeks. Separate the bulb clusters once tops are fully dry. In cool zones, shallots store for 6-12 months in cool, dry, dark conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted from individual bulbs — each divides into a cluster of 4-8 new bulbs at harvest. Same day-length sensitivity as onions. Cure thoroughly before storage.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Prune and space plants to maximise airflow","details":"Plant in open, well-ventilated positions. In subtropical zones even dry season humidity promotes powdery mildew. Avoid enclosed beds.","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Preventive sulfur spray from 40 days","details":"Apply sulfur-based fungicide from 40 days as a preventive measure in subtropical and tropical zones. Powdery mildew appears earlier and spreads faster in warm conditions.","category":"pest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest daily in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat, zucchini grows even faster than in temperate zones. Harvest every day or two. A missed harvest in tropical heat produces an enormous marrow within 72 hours.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Dry season planting for disease management
climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 30cm spacing","details":"Thin at 3-4 true leaves. Apply liquid fertiliser after thinning.","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Blanch for 10 days","details":"Blanching is even more important in zone 10 than cool zones — heat increases baseline bitterness. 10 days under cover or with tied leaves significantly improves palatability.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"In zone 10, endive overmatured by only 1-2 weeks becomes very bitter. Harvest when the centre is pale and well-blanched regardless of overall head size.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Blanching (excluding light for 10-14 days before harvest) is essential to reduce natural bitterness.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"Blood and bone or urea at 80g/m² when plants reach knee height. Repeat at shoulder height. In zone 10, rapid warm-season growth means the two-feed program must be timed precisely to plant growth stage, not calendar dates.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"In zone 10 warm summers, heat and dry spells at silking are common. Water daily if needed during the 7-10 day silk emergence period. Failure here causes cobs with many missing kernels.","category":"watering"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check silk for harvest readiness","details":"Check from 60-65 days. Brown dry silks = approaching maturity. Pierce a kernel — milky liquid squirts out at peak. Harvest immediately and refrigerate or eat.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Succession sow every 3 weeks for continuous harvest","details":"Plant a new block every 3 weeks from September to December. This staggers the harvest window so not all cobs are ready simultaneously — the \"all at once\" harvest problem is the main frustration with corn.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Excellent warm season crop — multiple plantings possible
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser","details":"One application of complete citrus fertiliser (including zinc and iron trace elements) in September. In cool zones, avoid late-season feeding that stimulates frost-vulnerable new growth flushes.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install winter frost protection — mandatory in zone 9","details":"Protect all bare-ground lime trees below 2°C with frost cloth. Young trees below 5°C. Container trees: move to a frost-free but light position. Remove protection during daylight.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune lightly following harvest","details":"Remove dead wood and crossing branches in spring after the coldest period. Avoid heavy pruning — lime trees in cool zones are slow to recover.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest when green-yellow and aromatic","details":"Tahitian lime is technically ripe when yellow but is conventionally harvested green for market appearance. Test by squeezing — ripe lime yields slightly. In cool zones lime production is limited but quality is usually good.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Least frost-tolerant common citrus. Tahitian (Persian) lime is the standard commercial variety. Kaffir lime grown for leaves. Both are essentially ever-bearing in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":150,"activity":"Reduce then stop water","details":"When 30-40% of leaves yellow, reduce watering. When 50% yellow, stop completely. Earlier water reduction in zone 10 compared to cooler zones because spring warming arrives sooner.","category":"watering"},{"timing":210,"activity":"Harvest October-November","details":"In zone 10, harvest typically October-November — earlier than cool zones. Lift carefully with a fork. Cure in a well-ventilated dry shed for 2-3 weeks. Do not leave in wet ground as spring rains begin.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest by cutting stems — avoid woody sections","details":"Cut stems 5-10cm long — always cut into the green, leafy growth and never into the old grey woody stems (they do not regenerate). Harvest year-round in zones 8-10. The highest essential oil content occurs just before flowering.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back hard after flowering — twice yearly","details":"Cut the entire plant back by 40-50% twice per year (spring and after summer flowering). This prevents thyme from becoming an unproductive woody mound within 2-3 years. Do not cut into the grey woody base.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Replace plant from cuttings","details":"Even well-managed thyme becomes woody and less productive after 4-5 years. Take cuttings from current-season growth in spring, root in coarse sand, and replace the old plant. Named varieties (English, French, lemon) must be propagated this way — they do not come true from seed.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial. Thrives in poor, dry, well-drained conditions. Like oregano — rich soil and overwatering reduce flavour and shorten plant life.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Support climbing varieties","details":"Erect 2m trellis or individual stakes before sowing. Train stems upward from 20cm height. Climbing varieties in zone 10 can produce for 8-10 weeks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Side-dress with potassium","details":"Apply sulphate of potash at 20g/m² when plants begin to flower. Beans fix nitrogen — supplemental nitrogen causes foliage at the expense of pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Pick at snap stage","details":"Harvest when pods are 10-15cm, bright green and snap cleanly. Pick every 2 days to maximise production. Beans left to mature on the plant signal the plant to stop producing.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — beans resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Do winter pruning","details":"Even in subtropical zones, grapes go partly dormant in winter. Prune in June-July to 2-bud spurs. Subtropical grapes may not fully lose all leaves — prune regardless.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply gypsum and potassium","details":"In subtropical soils, calcium (as gypsum) and potassium are often the limiting nutrients for grape quality. Apply gypsum at 500g per vine and sulphate of potash at 60g per vine at bunch formation.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":240,"activity":"Check for Queensland fruit fly","details":"Fruit fly is the major risk for grapes in subtropical zones. Begin Eco-naturalure bait applications from veraison (when colour change begins) through to harvest. Without management, the crop can be lost entirely.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest early to beat fruit fly","details":"Harvest bunches as they reach eating ripeness — do not leave ripe bunches on the vine in zone 11 subtropical heat as fruit fly, wasps and mould cause rapid deterioration.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Table grapes only — wine grapes lack acid without cool nights; Muscat varieties perform well
climate_note: Dormant pruning is essential — prune to 2-bud spurs each winter. Grapes fruit on current season growth from last year's wood. Requires chill hours for dormancy and reliable fruiting.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Check swollen stem size regularly","details":"Start checking at 40 days — the bulb can go from ideal to woody and split within a week in growing conditions. Harvest at 5-8cm diameter while skin is still smooth.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"This is the most important instruction for kohlrabi: harvest at the correct size (5-8cm). Left too long it becomes woody, fibrous and inedible. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing brassica. Harvest when bulb (swollen stem) reaches 5-8cm — do not wait or it becomes woody and splits. Quicker to harvest than most brassicas.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"While tree is leafless spray with Bordeaux mixture or copper hydroxide to prevent fungal diseases including brown rot and leaf curl. Cover all bark and buds thoroughly.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do formative pruning in winter","details":"In the first and second winter, prune to an open-vase or central-leader shape. Remove crossing branches. Keep cuts clean and angled. Do not remove more than 25% of canopy in one season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruitlets in spring","details":"When fruitlets reach marble size (2-3cm), thin to one fruit per cluster and space remaining fruit 15-20cm apart. Heavy thinning improves size and prevents biennial bearing. Scheduled from approximately year 2 after planting.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Harvest when mature","details":"Pick when fruit separates easily with a slight upward twist. Cool temperate apples (Granny Smith, Jonathon) ripen April-June. Store in cool conditions immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Apply dormant copper spray; Protect blossom from late frost
climate_note: Requires 500-1000+ chill hours. Standard varieties fail in zones 11b+. Low-chill varieties (Anna, Dorsett Golden) possible in zone 11a only.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train canes onto trellis","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). In zone 10a, erect trellis and train canes as per cool zones. Drip irrigation is preferable to overhead — wet foliage in warm conditions promotes botrytis (grey mould) which destroys raspberry crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Potassium emphasis at flowering","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). In zone 10a where chill hours are marginal, potassium application at first flower is critical for any fruit set to occur. Apply sulphate of potash at 50g per plant. Blood and bone at budburst.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Same as cool zones — remove all fruited canes immediately after harvest. This renovation is the foundation of next year's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest quickly in zone 10 warmth","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). In zone 10, harvest every 1-2 days. Ripe raspberries deteriorate very quickly in warmth. Pick in the early morning when fruit is cool.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 600-900 chill hours. Fruits on second-year canes (summer varieties) or current-year canes (autumn/everbearing varieties). Post-harvest cane removal is the key annual task.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Begin harvesting at 10cm height","details":"Cut leaves with scissors 3-4cm above soil when plants reach 10cm. The plant regrows from the cut base 2-3 times before bolting. In cool zones, a single sowing can produce for 4-6 weeks.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":21,"activity":"Check for bolting — remove or allow to set seed","details":"Once flower stalks emerge, leaves become intensely peppery (nearly inedible). Remove bolting plants immediately and resow. Alternatively, allow some to flower and set seed — the seed self-sows readily and produces the next crop.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing salad leaf. Bolts in heat producing very pungent, almost inedible leaves. Succession sow every 10-14 days. Wild rocket (Diplotaxis) is more heat-tolerant than common rocket (Eruca).

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser with trace elements","details":"Complete citrus fertiliser (including zinc and iron) in September. In cool zones, one application per year is appropriate. Late-season feeding stimulates soft frost-vulnerable new growth.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection for young trees","details":"Cover young trees (under 4-5 years) when frost is forecast. Established Satsuma trees can withstand -6°C. Young trees are more vulnerable — protect below -2°C.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a light annual prune","details":"After main harvest in autumn-winter, remove dead wood and crossing branches. Do not prune heavily — mandarins form on the outer canopy and heavy pruning reduces next season's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at full colour — Satsuma ripens before most citrus","details":"Satsuma ripens April-June in cool zones — one of the earliest mandarins. Satsumas can be fully ripe while still slightly green in cool zones — taste to confirm. Mandarins are the best indicator of correct harvest — taste, don't just look at colour.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Sweet flavour requires some cool nights in autumn and winter to develop properly. More cold-tolerant than lime or grapefruit. Self-fertile. Satsuma is the most frost-hardy variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Earth up progressively","details":"Mound soil around the shaft as it grows. Zone 10 leeks benefit from 2-3 earthing operations through their growing season (May-August). Keep soil loose for easy earthing.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Begin harvest when shaft reaches 2cm","details":"In zone 10, leeks reach harvestable size faster than in cool zones. Start harvesting the largest from July onwards. All leeks should be harvested before spring warmth triggers bolting.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Complete harvest before spring","details":"In zone 10, leeks left in the ground past August-September begin to bolt (run to flower), becoming tough and unusable. Harvest all remaining leeks by September.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season allium. Deep planting and earthing up blanches the white shaft — the primary eating part. More cold-tolerant than onions.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Stop nitrogen — switch to potassium","details":"When bulbs begin to swell (visible at the soil surface), stop nitrogen fertilising and apply sulphate of potash (40g/m²). This is the critical transition — nitrogen at this stage produces soft necks with poor storage life.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Stop watering when tops begin to fall","details":"When 50-70% of tops have flopped over, stop all watering. This triggers neck curing. Premature watering at this stage causes soft-necked onions that store poorly and rot within weeks.","category":"watering"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest and cure in dry conditions","details":"Lift onions when tops are fully fallen and yellowed. Lay in a single layer in a dry, airy location for 3-4 weeks. In cool zones, a dry shed or under cover is ideal. Cure until the necks are completely dry before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Identify and thin to hermaphrodite plant","details":"Hermaphrodite papaya produces fruit without a pollinator. Identify by flower type when first flowers appear (4-5 months): hermaphrodite flowers emerge directly from trunk. Remove all males immediately. Keep one hermaphrodite.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune to keep height below 2.5m","details":"When trunk reaches 2m, cut back to encourage branching and maintain accessible harvest height. Suckers from the base can replace aging main trunks. Replace trees after 3-4 years when trunk becomes tall and production declines.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest when 20-30% yellow — ripen off tree","details":"In tropical zones papaya is produced year-round. Harvest individual fruit when skin starts to colour (20-30% yellow). In tropical heat the fruit completes ripening within 3-5 days at room temperature. Do not leave fully ripe fruit on the tree in wet season heat — it ferments quickly.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing tropical/subtropical tree. Short-lived (3-5 years productive). May include hermaphrodite, male or female plants from seed — hermaphrodite produces best fruit. Water-sensitive — do not waterlog.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Remove side shoots from the root","details":"As the root swells, it produces small shoots (tillers) from its sides. Remove these monthly — they divert energy from root development. Reach into the base of the plant and snap them off.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":140,"activity":"Harvest when root reaches 8-12cm diameter","details":"Brush away soil to check root size. Celeriac roots store well in the ground in cool zones — can be left until needed through winter. Lift with a fork, trim leaves to 2-3cm above root.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: One of the best cool-temperate vegetables
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season root vegetable. Takes 5-6 months from transplant. One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables — hard frosts improve flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"When corn reaches knee height (30-40cm), apply blood and bone at 100g/m² or pelleted nitrogen fertiliser alongside the row. This is the critical \"knee-high by holiday\" feed that drives cob development. Repeat at shoulder height.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"Never allow soil to dry at silking (when the silks emerge from the cob tips). Moisture stress at silking causes unfilled kernels — the single most common cause of poor corn. Daily watering if needed during silk emergence.","category":"watering"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check silk browning — harvest test","details":"When silk turns brown and dry, the cobs are approaching maturity. Pull back the husk and pierce a kernel — if milky liquid squirts out, harvest immediately. Clear liquid = too early; no liquid (doughy) = too late. The milky stage lasts only 2-3 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest at peak sweetness","details":"Pick at milky stage. Twist and pull downward to detach from the stem. In cool zones, boil or refrigerate within 30 minutes of harvest — sugars convert to starch rapidly after picking. Supersweet varieties are more forgiving.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Net when colour begins","details":"Bird pressure in subtropical zones is high. Net completely before any colour development.","category":"pest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Check for botrytis and spider mites","details":"Subtropical conditions promote both grey mould (in humid periods) and spider mite (in dry heat). Manage drainage for botrytis; forceful water sprays on leaf undersides for mites.","category":"pest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Harvest September-October before heat returns","details":"In zone 11, the harvest window is September-October. Harvest daily. Once sustained temperatures above 28°C arrive, production effectively ends. Pull plants in December and compost — replant runners the following June.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant May-June — limited production in subtropical heat
climate_note: Grown from runners (not seed). Plant crowns in autumn, harvest spring. Replace plants every 2-3 years — older plants have lower yield. Protect from birds and slugs at fruit set.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray — essential","details":"Apply copper oxychloride or Bordeaux mixture while leafless. Nectarines are extremely susceptible to leaf curl and brown rot which overwinter on bark. Thorough dormant spraying is the single most effective disease management step.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune to open vase shape","details":"Prune in summer (January-February) after harvest — not winter. Winter pruning leaves entry wounds for silver leaf disease. Remove inward-facing shoots. Open vase structure admits light and air to reduce brown rot.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit heavily in spring","details":"When fruitlets are 1-2cm, thin to one fruit per 10-15cm of branch. Heavy thinning seems counterintuitive but dramatically increases final fruit size and reduces brown rot pressure from crowded touching fruit.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured and fragrant","details":"Nectarines picked even one day early are disappointing — they do not ripen further off the tree. Harvest when the background colour changes from green to yellow and the fruit yields to gentle palm pressure. The aroma intensifies as ripeness is reached.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Smooth-skinned peach variant with identical chill hour requirements. Brown rot at harvest is the main management challenge. Harvest timing is critical — nectarines do not improve after picking.

key_activities: [{"timing":300,"activity":"Remove excess suckers — keep 3-stem system","details":"Maintain mother plant + one follower + one replacement sucker. Remove all others. This provides continuous annual production from the same mat.","category":"planting"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Bag and harvest bunch","details":"When the flower (bell) appears and the first hands of fruit set, bag the bunch with a slitted blue banana bag to protect from sunburn, insects and birds. Harvest 10-14 weeks after bagging when fruit is full and rounded.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent growing conditions — protect from strong winds
climate_note: Grows from suckers/rhizomes, not seedlings. Needs 10-12 months of warmth to fruit. Frost kills foliage; sustained frost kills the rhizome.

key_activities: [{"timing":7,"activity":"Thin to 5cm","details":"Thin at 2 true leaves. In warm zones overcrowding causes even faster deterioration.","category":"planting"},{"timing":20,"activity":"Check from 15 days — harvest small","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones radish matures even faster than in zone 10. Start checking at 15 days. Harvest at 1.5-2cm diameter — smaller than cool zone radish but less likely to be pithy.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":25,"activity":"Harvest all before wet season or heat returns","details":"Do not leave radish in the ground as temperatures rise. Harvest all plants by September. Wet season humidity causes immediate root rot.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fastest vegetable in the garden (25-35 days). Bolts and becomes hot/woody in heat. Harvest promptly at correct size — even 3-4 days too late produces pithy, harsh radish.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin promptly. In zone 10, afternoon shade extends the harvest window before bolting. Even light shade (30%) significantly delays bolting in warm conditions.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Succession sow every 10-14 days","details":"In zone 10, bolt-to-seed time is very fast in warm months. Sow more frequently (every 10-14 days) to maintain continuous supply. Use slow-bolt varieties (Leisure, Santos).","category":"planting"},{"timing":21,"activity":"Harvest before bolt","details":"Monitor plants daily in zone 10. Harvest entire plant at first sign of the central flower stalk elongating. Young coriander has the best leaf aroma and flavour.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Collect seed for replanting","details":"Allow one plant to go to seed each cycle. Harvest brown seed heads and dry. Use seed as spice or for next sowing. Self-sown coriander in zone 10 gardens often fills gaps between sowings.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Grow in cool months — autumn to spring
climate_note: Notoriously bolt-prone. Direct sow — resents transplanting. Keep cool and harvest before flower stalks emerge. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"When corn reaches knee height (30-40cm), apply blood and bone at 100g/m² or pelleted nitrogen fertiliser alongside the row. This is the critical \"knee-high by holiday\" feed that drives cob development. Repeat at shoulder height.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"Never allow soil to dry at silking (when the silks emerge from the cob tips). Moisture stress at silking causes unfilled kernels — the single most common cause of poor corn. Daily watering if needed during silk emergence.","category":"watering"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check silk browning — harvest test","details":"When silk turns brown and dry, the cobs are approaching maturity. Pull back the husk and pierce a kernel — if milky liquid squirts out, harvest immediately. Clear liquid = too early; no liquid (doughy) = too late. The milky stage lasts only 2-3 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest at peak sweetness","details":"Pick at milky stage. Twist and pull downward to detach from the stem. In cool zones, boil or refrigerate within 30 minutes of harvest — sugars convert to starch rapidly after picking. Supersweet varieties are more forgiving.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant after last frost — October at earliest
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 20cm spacing","details":"Thin at 3-4 true leaves. Harvest thinnings as salad greens.","category":"planting"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Harvest young to avoid bitterness","details":"Zone 10 chicory becomes bitter faster than in cool zones. Begin harvesting outer leaves at 30-35 days when young and tender. Do not let plants mature fully before harvest.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Remove before heat returns","details":"If approaching summer, harvest all remaining plants before temperatures rise — heat converts palatable leaves to very bitter inedible ones within days.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Avoid summer — bolts rapidly in heat
climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Leaf quality deteriorates rapidly in heat — becomes tough and very bitter. Forcing chicory for chicons is a separate process requiring root lifting.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Apply complete fertiliser with nitrogen at transplant. Follow with liquid fish fertiliser every 3 weeks. Consistent nitrogen is the single biggest driver of solid head formation.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Install exclusion netting for caterpillars","details":"In zone 10, cabbage white butterfly is active most of the year. Fine insect mesh over the bed at transplant is the most effective approach. Remove only for maintenance.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check for early splitting in warm spells","details":"In zone 10, sudden warmth after cool development can cause heads to split as they resume rapid growth. Harvest immediately if cracks appear at the crown.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":85,"activity":"Harvest at full size","details":"Heads should feel solid and heavy for their size. In zone 10, autumn-planted cabbage can reach 1-2kg. Cut at the base and compost the stump.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season brassica. Heavy feeder — needs consistent nitrogen. Firm planting prevents splitting.

key_activities: [{"timing":150,"activity":"Stop water early","details":"Stop watering when 30-40% of leaves yellow — this arrives sooner in subtropical zones as temperatures warm more rapidly.","category":"watering"},{"timing":210,"activity":"Harvest September-October","details":"Harvest when tops fall regardless of size. Subtropical garlic bulbs will be smaller than cool zone equivalents. Cure in a dry, airy position for 2-3 weeks. Use within 4-6 months — storage life shorter than cool zone garlic.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant June only — results less reliable
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main fruiting flush, cut all fruited branches back to the main framework wires. Collect fruit when it falls (fully ripe) or when the skin begins to wrinkle on the vine. Replace vines after 4-5 years as production naturally declines — plan the replacement crop 1-2 years ahead.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very productive — check rootstock compatibility with Fusarium wilt
climate_note: Vigorous perennial vine needing a strong trellis. Self-fertile but bee pollination improves fruit set. Fusarium crown rot is the main killer — plant grafted varieties in zones 10-11.

key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Transplant firmly","details":"Raise seedlings in trays, transplant at 4-6 true leaves when 10-15cm tall. If still soft, leave another 2-3 weeks. Leave the outer wrapper leaves for transport protection. In cool zones a light frost after heading actually improves sweetness.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season brassica. Heavy feeder — needs consistent nitrogen. Firm planting prevents splitting.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Erect trellis","details":"Snow peas are climbing plants (1-1.5m). Net or string trellis works well.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at first flower. Peas fix their own nitrogen — do not add nitrogen fertiliser. Potassium drives pod fill and overall yield.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Harvest when flat and pods are full","details":"Pick snow peas when the pod is flat and full width but before the peas inside begin to bulge. key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune lightly to encourage bushy growth","details":"Tip-prune stems by 20-30% in late winter to encourage branching and denser fruiting growth. Do not prune heavily — the shrub is slow-growing in cool zones.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest dried berries on the plant","details":"Berries are harvested after they have dried naturally on the plant — they shrivel and turn brown. climate_note: Australian native desert shrub (Solanum centrale). Extremely drought-tolerant. Berries are dried and used as a spice with caramel-tamarillo flavour. Dislikes wet soils.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Install drip irrigation and apply mulch","details":"Consistent moisture through drip irrigation. Heavy mulch. In tropical zones, reduce irrigation in the wet season and ensure drainage.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Do a hard winter prune (now or within winter)","details":"Cut to a 30-40cm framework each year in June-July. Stimulates vigorous new fruiting growth. extra_care: Year-round perennial — monitor for mites in dry conditions
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Requires warmth to germinate and fruit. Capsicum and Peppers are the same species (Capsicum annuum) — treated identically.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After fruit removal (August-September in cool zones; timing varies in tropical zones), remove crossing branches and any dead wood. Grapefruit does not need heavy pruning — mostly size management for access.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when skin colour develops","details":"Grapefruit turns yellow when mature. In warmer zones (11-12) fruit may remain partially green even when ripe — taste is a better guide than colour. Fruit holds on the tree for months — harvest as needed.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Least cold-tolerant of commercial citrus. Requires warm nights to develop balanced acidity and sweetness. Self-fertile but large tree — allow 6m spacing.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Remove side shoots","details":"As with cool zones, remove lateral shoots monthly for best root development.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest small roots by September","details":"Do not wait for large roots in warm zones — harvest whatever size has developed before heat returns. Small celeriac roots still have excellent flavour.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season root vegetable. Takes 5-6 months from transplant. One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables — hard frosts improve flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 20cm — space for airflow","details":"Good spacing reduces fungal leaf disease risk in humid subtropical conditions.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvesting young leaves regularly","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones harvest young leaves frequently and early — older leaves in warm conditions become tougher. climate_note: Biennial herb (lives 2 years). Very slow germination (3-4 weeks) — pre-soaking in warm water for 24 hours significantly improves germination rate.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Begin harvesting young tips","details":"Harvest young shoot tips year-round. Cut stems back by 30-40% to stimulate regrowth. Annual hard pruning to 15-20cm keeps the plant compact and productive. The cut material is edible (blanch first).","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Australian native coastal plant (Tetragonia tetragonioides). Edible leaves MUST be blanched (boiled 2+ minutes) before eating to reduce oxalates. Extremely drought and salt tolerant.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Change water regularly — daily in warm periods","details":"If growing in a container, change the water daily in warm weather to prevent stagnation and mosquito breeding. In cool zones, changing water every 2-3 days in winter is sufficient. extra_care: Needs running or frequently refreshed water — shallow stream ideal
climate_note: Aquatic or semi-aquatic plant. Grows in cool running water or in pots sat in trays of water. Bolts and becomes pungent in heat. Wild-harvested watercress is a liver fluke risk — only consume cultivated plant.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 10-15cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings are 5cm tall — crowded parsnips produce forked, small roots. Harvest all remaining roots before they produce foliage in spring.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Root vegetable that improves dramatically with cold — frost converts starch to sugar. Very slow to germinate (21-28 days). Fresh seed essential — parsnip seed loses viability quickly.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Remove lower leaves regularly","details":"More frequent removal needed in warm humid conditions — fungal disease (especially black rot) spreads quickly in zone 11+ without good airflow around the base.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Top early to force development","details":"Top at 50-60cm height — earlier than cool zones.
