key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Apply mulch and install supports","details":"Deep mulch (10cm) and consistent moisture. Perennial plants in subtropical/tropical zones produce prolifically over years — they need consistent feeding to maintain yield.","category":"fertilizing"}]

climate_note: Warm-season crop that thrives in heat. Can be treated as a perennial in frost-free zones (10b-12). Extended ripening produces full colour and maximum heat.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin seedlings and apply liquid fertiliser","details":"Thin to 20cm when seedlings have 3-4 true leaves. Thinnings are edible. climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Leaf quality deteriorates rapidly in heat — becomes tough and very bitter. Forcing chicory for chicons is a separate process requiring root lifting.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply potassium at bulbing","details":"As bulbs start to swell (visible above the soil), apply sulphate of potash at 30g/m². Stop all nitrogen. The warm dry season climate in subtropical zones assists natural curing.","category":"watering"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest and store in warm dry conditions","details":"In tropical zones, bulbs left in the ground after tops fall deteriorate rapidly. Harvest promptly. Cure in a warm, well-ventilated covered area for 2 weeks. Shelf life is shorter in warm humid zones than in cool-zone equivalents.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

Papaya leaves die at 0°C; the growing tip (crown) is killed below -1°C. Loss of the crown kills the tree entirely.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest when yellow blush develops","details":"In zone 9b papaya may fruit only in warm years. Harvest when 20-30% of the skin has turned yellow. The fruit continues to ripen at room temperature.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing tropical/subtropical tree. Short-lived (3-5 years productive). May include hermaphrodite, male or female plants from seed — hermaphrodite produces best fruit. Water-sensitive — do not waterlog.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Remove lateral shoots","details":"Monthly removal of side shoots from the base of the developing root redirects energy. The root should be smooth and rounded — lateral shoots create misshapen, rough roots.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":140,"activity":"Harvest before spring warming","details":"In zone 10, harvest by August-September before spring heat arrives. Roots left in the ground into spring bolt (run to seed) and become hollow. Pull with a fork and use promptly.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season root vegetable. Takes 5-6 months from transplant. One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables — hard frosts improve flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen when thinning","details":"Liquid fish emulsion or diluted blood and bone after thinning. Spinach is a moderately heavy feeder — nitrogen drives leaf production. One or two applications through the season is sufficient.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest at 20cm height","details":"Harvest outer leaves by cutting at the base when the plant reaches 20cm. Leave the central growing tip intact — the plant regrows for 2-3 more harvests before bolting.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":40,"activity":"Remove at first bolt","details":"Once the central flower stalk begins to elongate, remove the entire plant. Bolted spinach is bitter and unpalatable within hours. Resow immediately from the succession sowing already in place.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent cool season — year-round except winter peak cold

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Apply copper while leafless. In zone 10 with higher humidity, dormant sprays followed by petal-fall sprays are both important for brown rot control.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after harvest in summer — critical","details":"Prune in summer immediately after harvest. This is even more important in zone 10 than cool zones — the longer growing season allows wound healing before winter and reduces silver leaf disease risk.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit — especially important in warm zones","details":"In zone 10, warm temperatures drive rapid fruit development. Thin to 10-12cm between fruit. In warm conditions, crowded touching fruit develops brown rot rapidly before harvest.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at peak ripeness — do not delay","details":"In zone 10, nectarines move from ready to overripe quickly. Harvest in morning when fruit is cool. Brown rot can develop overnight on ripe fruit in warm humid conditions — harvest entire tree at ripeness and refrigerate immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Low-chill varieties: Snow Queen, Arctic Star
climate_note: Smooth-skinned peach variant with identical chill hour requirements. Brown rot at harvest is the main management challenge. Harvest timing is critical — nectarines do not improve after picking.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Prune and space plants to maximise airflow","details":"Plant in open, well-ventilated positions. In subtropical zones even dry season humidity promotes powdery mildew. Avoid enclosed beds.","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Preventive sulfur spray from 40 days","details":"Apply sulfur-based fungicide from 40 days as a preventive measure in subtropical and tropical zones. Powdery mildew appears earlier and spreads faster in warm conditions.","category":"pest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest daily in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat, zucchini grows even faster than in temperate zones. Harvest every day or two. A missed harvest in tropical heat produces an enormous marrow within 72 hours.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Remove flower stalks","details":"Rhubarb occasionally sends up a flower stalk (thick round stem with seed head). Remove it immediately at ground level — it diverts energy from leaf stalks and signals the plant to stop producing.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting — pull, do not cut","details":"In spring of year 2 (August-October), harvest stalks by gripping at the base and pulling with a twisting motion. Never cut — cutting leaves a stub that can rot into the crown. Take no more than 1/3 of the stalks at any time. Stop harvesting by November to allow the plant to rebuild. Scheduled from approximately year 2 after planting.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Outstanding zone — cold winters produce largest, most colourful stalks
climate_note: Requires cold winters for dormancy and vigorous regrowth. The colder the winter, the better the rhubarb. Only harvest stems — leaves are toxic (contain oxalic acid). Do not harvest in year 1.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 20cm spacing","details":"When seedlings are 5cm tall, thin to 20cm. Thinnings are edible. Crowded parsley produces thin weak stems — give it space.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvest — outer stems first","details":"Cut outer stems at the base of the plant when they reach 15-20cm. Always leave at least 50% of the plant — parsley needs leaf mass to continue producing. In cool zones parsley is productive for 12-16 months before bolting in its second year.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Remove plant when flowering begins","details":"Parsley bolts in its second year. Once flower stalks emerge, leaf quality drops immediately. Remove the plant and replace with a new sowing — do not try to harvest from a bolting parsley plant. Scheduled from approximately year undefined after planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Biennial herb (lives 2 years). Very slow germination (3-4 weeks) — pre-soaking in warm water for 24 hours significantly improves germination rate.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin ruthlessly to 5cm spacing","details":"This is the step gardeners most often skip and most regret. Crowded carrots fork and stay small. Thin in two stages: first to 3cm at 3 weeks, then to 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check progress by brushing away soil","details":"Brush soil from the top of the root at 8-9 weeks. When the shoulder (top of root) reaches 1.5-2cm diameter, full-size roots are approaching maturity. Do not leave in the ground too long — oversize roots become woody.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest after cold for best flavour","details":"Cold temperatures convert carrot starch to sugar — autumn and winter carrots in cool zones are the sweetest. Pull by twisting and pulling steadily, or loosen soil with a fork first to avoid breaking roots.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Autumn and winter crop produces best flavour
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 10-15cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings are 5cm tall — crowded parsnips produce forked, small roots. Thinning is the most commonly skipped and most impactful management step.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Leave in ground after frost for sweetness","details":"Parsnips can be left in the ground until needed. In cool zones, a frost triggers starch-to-sugar conversion — harvest after the first hard frost for the best flavour. This is unique to parsnips and a genuine argument for cool-zone growing.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":140,"activity":"Harvest before plants re-shoot in spring","details":"In the second spring (parsnip is biennial), plants begin to re-shoot and roots become woody and bitter. Harvest all remaining roots before they produce foliage in spring.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Outstanding zone — cold converts starch to sugar for excellent flavour; Harvest after frost for best sweetness
climate_note: Root vegetable that improves dramatically with cold — frost converts starch to sugar. Very slow to germinate (21-28 days). Fresh seed essential — parsnip seed loses viability quickly.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Install wind and frost protection","details":"Bananas shred in wind, reducing photosynthesis. Erect shade cloth windbreak on south and west. Add organic matter monthly.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Remove all suckers but one follower","details":"As the main plant grows, it throws suckers. extra_care: Ornamental use only — fruiting unreliable; Heavy mulching to protect rhizome
climate_note: Grows from suckers/rhizomes, not seedlings. Needs 10-12 months of warmth to fruit. Frost kills foliage; sustained frost kills the rhizome.

key_activities: [{"timing":120,"activity":"Blanch before spring warmth arrives","details":"In zone 10, begin blanching in July-August — earlier than in cool zones. climate_note: Globe artichoke relative grown for the blanched leaf stalks (not the buds). Requires blanching (excluding light for 3-4 weeks) to produce edible, mild-flavoured stalks.

climate_note: Warm-season crop. Highly productive but affected by powdery mildew. Male and female flowers separate — pollination by bees essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Switch to potassium at bulb swell","details":"Apply sulphate of potash (40g/m²) when bulbs first become visible. This firms up the bulb layers and improves storage quality. Heavy nitrogen at this stage causes thick necks and short shelf life.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Stop watering — allow curing to begin","details":"Stop watering when tops begin to fall over. climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 10cm — thinnings are edible","details":"Thin at 3-4cm seedling height. Thinnings make excellent salad greens. Crowded turnips produce small deformed roots.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Check root size from 35 days","details":"Begin checking by pulling a test root at 35 days. Succession sow every 3 weeks for continuous supply of young, sweet turnips.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast cool-season root crop. Harvest small (5-8cm) — older turnips become pithy and peppery. Leaves are also edible (turnip greens). Frost improves sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train vertically or provide 3–5m run space","details":"Winter squash vines spread extensively. Allow 3-5m per plant or erect a strong trellis and support developing fruit in mesh bags. Vertical growing produces cleaner fruit and is practical in cool zones with limited space.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser and potassium at fruit set","details":"Complete fertiliser at establishment. High potassium produces thick, hard skin essential for long storage.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Check fruit maturity with skin test","details":"Begin checking at 90 days. Press a fingernail firmly into the skin — it should resist completely without marking. Soft skin means the squash needs more time. In cool zones, harvest all squash before first frost even if skin test says incomplete.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest with long stem and cure thoroughly","details":"Cut with 10cm of stem — this is essential for storage. Cure in a warm (25-30°C) sunny position for 10-14 days. Curing hardens the skin and seals the stem scar, enabling 3-6 months storage in cool, dry, dark conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Same principles as pumpkin. Harvest at full maturity with hard skin — unlike summer squash. Cures to 3-6 months storage. Needs bees for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply azalea/camellia fertiliser","details":"Never use standard NPK fertiliser — it raises pH and kills blueberries. Scheduled from approximately year 3 after planting.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Soil pH 4.5-5.5 is critical — most Australian soils need acidification. Needs cross-pollination from a second variety. Chill hour requirements vary dramatically by variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to strongest seedling","details":"When seedlings reach 5cm, thin to one per cluster (8-10cm final spacing). climate_note: Cool-season root crop. Bolts (runs to seed prematurely) in heat. Best grown in autumn, winter and spring.

key_activities: [{"timing":28,"activity":"Harvest very young — before heat makes it unpalatable","details":"In subtropical zones, harvest watercress at 5-8cm — micro-herb stage. Older growth in warm conditions is intensely pungent and often unpalatable.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Shade essential — flows to cool running water position if possible
climate_note: Aquatic or semi-aquatic plant. Grows in cool running water or in pots sat in trays of water. Bolts and becomes pungent in heat. Wild-harvested watercress is a liver fluke risk — only consume cultivated plant.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After fruit removal (August-September in cool zones; timing varies in tropical zones), remove crossing branches and any dead wood. climate_note: Least cold-tolerant of commercial citrus. Requires warm nights to develop balanced acidity and sweetness. Self-fertile but large tree — allow 6m spacing.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin carefully","details":"Thin to 8cm spacing. In warm climates bolt risk increases with crowding. Thinnings are edible — use as baby salad greens.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply seaweed fertiliser with trace elements","details":"In zone 10, focus on trace elements (boron, manganese). extra_care: Avoid summer sowing — bolts in heat
climate_note: Cool-season root crop. Bolts (runs to seed prematurely) in heat. Best grown in autumn, winter and spring.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Blanch curds in zone 10","details":"Zone 10 sunshine is intense. Check every second day once the head is blanched. Harvest when solid and white — before any separation of florets.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: More cold-sensitive than broccoli. The curd (head) must be blanched by tying outer leaves over it to prevent yellowing and bitterness in sunny conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Check bulb size daily in warm conditions","details":"In zone 10, the window between \"ready\" and \"too late\" is only 3-5 days in warm weather. Check daily from 35-40 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Succession sow for continuous harvest","details":"Plant a new row every 2-3 weeks through the cool season to avoid having all plants ready simultaneously.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing brassica. Harvest when bulb (swollen stem) reaches 5-8cm — do not wait or it becomes woody and splits. Quicker to harvest than most brassicas.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting outer leaves — cut-and-come-again","details":"Harvest outer leaves only. In zone 10 with year-round warmth, a single plant produces for 12+ months with cut-and-come-again management.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 3)","details":"Blood and bone at 80g/m² at planting. Monthly liquid fish emulsion maintains production. Zone 10 silverbeet grows vigorously — consistent feeding sustains this.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 3)","details":"Blood and bone at 80g/m² at planting. Monthly liquid fish emulsion maintains production. Zone 10 silverbeet grows vigorously — consistent feeding sustains this.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Replace at first bolt","details":"Remove and replace at first sign of a central flower stalk. Monthly liquid fish emulsion maintains production. Zone 10 silverbeet grows vigorously — consistent feeding sustains this.","category":"fertilizing"}]
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":28,"activity":"Begin harvesting young tips","details":"In zone 10, harvest watercress tips at 8-10cm — younger than in cool zones — before heat intensifies the pungency beyond palatability. Harvest in the cool of the morning.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Refresh plant from cuttings","details":"Zone 10 watercress becomes woody and unproductive faster than in cool zones. Refresh with new cuttings every 4-6 months.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Shade and constant moisture — bolts in heat
climate_note: Aquatic or semi-aquatic plant. Grows in cool running water or in pots sat in trays of water. Bolts and becomes pungent in heat. Wild-harvested watercress is a liver fluke risk — only consume cultivated plant.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply low-phosphorus native plant fertiliser","details":"Finger limes are native plants sensitive to high phosphorus. Use native plant fertiliser (marked \"native\" or \"low phosphorus\") in spring. Supplement with trace elements (zinc and iron) if interveinal yellowing appears.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply mulch","details":"Finger limes evolved in moist subtropical rainforest — they need consistent moisture, especially while establishing in cool zones. extra_care: Plant in warmest sheltered position — north-facing against brick wall
climate_note: Australian native citrus. Thorny shrub/tree from subtropical rainforest. Grafted varieties fruit from 3-4 years; seed-grown may take 7-10 years. Fruit contains "citrus caviar" vesicles.

climate_note: Most frost-tolerant citrus. Compact tree suitable for container growing. Self-fruitful. Fruit is eaten whole — skin is sweet, flesh is tart.

climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Pinch tips","details":"In warm zones basil bolts very quickly. Pinch the growing tip as soon as the plant is established (15-20cm). key_activities: [{"timing":7,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings have 2 true leaves. Crowded radish produce small, poorly shaped roots. Harvest when the root reaches 2-3cm diameter — do not wait for them to look \"finished\" above ground.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"This is the most important radish instruction: harvest at correct size (2-3cm). extra_care: Spring and autumn crop — excellent in cool conditions

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Install trellis and train main stem","details":"Train one main stem upward to the top of the trellis. key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Pinch out growing tip","details":"Pinch out the central stem tip to the first set of leaves as soon as the plant reaches 15cm. This forces bushy growth and delays flowering. In cool zones harvest frequently — the season is short. Remove flower buds the moment they appear to extend leaf production.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Grow indoors or in glasshouse — frost kills immediately
climate_note: Frost-sensitive annual. Bolts in heat. Best in warm but not extreme conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest from 6-8 weeks","details":"Always harvest outer leaves only — leave at least 4-6 central leaves. This cut-and-come-again method allows a single planting to produce for 12-18 months in cool zones.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Remove any yellowing leaves","details":"Remove yellowing or damaged outer leaves at the base. Once a central flower stalk appears, the plant is finished — remove and replace with a new sowing. Scheduled from approximately year undefined after planting.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after fruiting","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Light prune to maintain shape. Spray copper at petal fall and repeat weekly during fruit development in humid weather.","category":"pest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when mature","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). climate_note: Requires 300-900 chill hours. Flowers early — frost damage to blossom is the main risk in cool zones. Insufficient chill hours in zones 11b+.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser","details":"Use a citrus fertiliser containing nitrogen, trace elements (zinc, iron, manganese) in September-October when growth resumes. Apply at label rates to drip line. Do not apply late in season — new soft growth in autumn is frost-vulnerable.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Bring container plants indoors in severe winters","details":"In zone 8a, move container cumquats to a frost-free shed or sunroom in June-July if hard frosts (below -5°C) are forecast. Fruit turns deep orange when ripe and softens slightly. Can be left on the tree for several months without quality loss.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Most cold-tolerant citrus but zone 8a winters may be too severe — grow in container
climate_note: Most frost-tolerant citrus. Compact tree suitable for container growing. Self-fruitful. Fruit is eaten whole — skin is sweet, flesh is tart.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Check swollen stem size regularly","details":"Start checking at 40 days — the bulb can go from ideal to woody and split within a week in growing conditions. Harvest at 5-8cm diameter while skin is still smooth.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"This is the most important instruction for kohlrabi: harvest at the correct size (5-8cm). Left too long it becomes woody, fibrous and inedible. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing brassica. Harvest when bulb (swollen stem) reaches 5-8cm — do not wait or it becomes woody and splits. Quicker to harvest than most brassicas.

key_activities: [{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium after complete fertiliser","details":"Same nutritional program as other zones: complete at establishment, potassium at flowering.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check for powdery mildew — treat if needed","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, apply sulfur fungicide at the first sign of powdery mildew (white powder on leaf surfaces). extra_care: October-February planting — avoid wet season in tropics
climate_note: Large vining crop needing 4-6m space or vertical support. Pollination by bees essential — male flowers appear first. Store cured pumpkins in cool dry conditions for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvesting at pre-flowering stage","details":"In zone 10, oregano grows year-round. Harvest before flowering for maximum flavour. Cut stems to 10cm regularly to prevent woodiness.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Hard prune twice yearly","details":"Cut back hard (to 10cm) in late autumn and early spring. climate_note: Mediterranean perennial. Thrives on neglect — poor, dry soil produces the most aromatic leaves. Do not overwater or over-fertilise.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train onto trellis — direct young shoots upward","details":"Sugar snap peas produce vigorous growth. Direct shoots to the trellis in the first 2 weeks. climate_note: Thick-walled edible pod (both pod and peas eaten together). Taller vine than snow peas — needs 1.8m support. Same management principles as snow peas and peas.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Install plant supports","details":"Erect supports before planting. climate_note: Direct sow — beans resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Check for scale insects and citrus leafminer","details":"Scale insects (brown scale, soft scale) and citrus leafminer are prevalent in warm zones. climate_note: Sweet flavour requires some cool nights in autumn and winter to develop properly. More cold-tolerant than lime or grapefruit. Self-fertile. Satsuma is the most frost-hardy variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser with trace elements","details":"Complete citrus fertiliser (with zinc, iron and manganese) in September. Do not prune heavily — oranges fruit on new season shoots and over-pruning reduces next season's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest by taste — colour not reliable in cool zones","details":"In cool zones, Washington Navels ripen May-August. Taste for sweetness and juice — in cool zones colour development can precede full flavour by several weeks. Orange holds on the tree for months without quality loss in cool conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool nights in winter are needed for the best flavour (sugar-acid balance). Valencia ripens later than Navel and is the best variety for warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 10-15cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings are 5cm tall — crowded parsnips produce forked, small roots. Thinning is the most commonly skipped and most impactful management step.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Leave in ground after frost for sweetness","details":"Parsnips can be left in the ground until needed. This is unique to parsnips and a genuine argument for cool-zone growing.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":140,"activity":"Harvest before plants re-shoot in spring","details":"In the second spring (parsnip is biennial), plants begin to re-shoot and roots become woody and bitter. Harvest all remaining roots before they produce foliage in spring.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very good — autumn and winter crop
climate_note: Root vegetable that improves dramatically with cold — frost converts starch to sugar. Very slow to germinate (21-28 days). Fresh seed essential — parsnip seed loses viability quickly.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Switch to potassium at bulb swell","details":"Apply sulphate of potash (40g/m²) when bulbs first become visible. This firms up the bulb layers and improves storage quality. climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"In tropical and subtropical soils, nutrients leach quickly. climate_note: Cool-season brassica. Heavy feeder — needs consistent nitrogen. Firm planting prevents splitting.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and support plants","details":"In cool zones wind can be damaging. Stake each plant to a 60cm stake at transplant. Apply potassium-rich fertiliser (sulphate of potash at 40g/m²) at flowering — potassium drives fruit development.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest green or wait for full colour","details":"In cool zones the season may end before capsicum fully ripen. Harvest green if frost threatens. Red capsicum is the same fruit — simply allowed to fully ripen — and is sweeter with higher vitamin C.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Warm microclimate essential — against a north-facing wall
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Needs 10°C+ at all times. Pick red for full sweetness — green capsicum is simply unripe.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune lightly to encourage bushy growth","details":"Tip-prune stems by 20-30% in late winter to encourage branching and denser fruiting growth. Do not prune heavily — the shrub is slow-growing in cool zones.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest dried berries on the plant","details":"Berries are harvested after they have dried naturally on the plant — they shrivel and turn brown. extra_care: Dry, well-drained position — dislikes wet winters
climate_note: Australian native desert shrub (Solanum centrale). Extremely drought-tolerant. Berries are dried and used as a spice with caramel-tamarillo flavour. Dislikes wet soils.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser in warm zones. Granular slow-release is less effective in warm, freely-draining tropical soils.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser in warm zones. Granular slow-release is less effective in warm, freely-draining tropical soils.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Harvest very young leaves","details":"In warm zones, harvest kale leaves very young (15-20cm) before they become tough and bitter. Do not wait for large leaf development.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser in warm zones. Granular slow-release is less effective in warm, freely-draining tropical soils.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Net for caterpillar control","details":"Multiple caterpillar species attack brassicas in warm climates. Wet season conditions cause immediate disease collapse in brassicas.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables. Frost dramatically improves sweetness. Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves only to extend production for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Check for powdery mildew — treat if needed","details":"Powdery mildew is universal on zone 10 zucchini by midsummer. Apply sulfur spray at first signs. Remove badly affected leaves. The plant typically outlasts mildew for 4-6 weeks if managed.","category":"pest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days without exception","details":"In zone 10 warmth, zucchini grows 3-5cm per day. A 20cm zucchini today is a 40cm marrow in 4 days. Harvest every 2 days. Any fruit allowed to grow large signals the plant to slow production. This instruction is not optional.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 30cm spacing","details":"Thin to final spacing when seedlings have 3-4 leaves. Do not delay thinning — crowded fennel bolts prematurely.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Hill up soil around the base","details":"When the swollen stem (the bulb) begins to develop at the base, hill up soil around it to 5cm depth. This blanches the bulb, making it whiter and sweeter. Repeat as the bulb grows.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest before bolt or when bolting","details":"Cut the whole plant at soil level when the bulb is 8-12cm across and firm. If flower stems emerge from the centre, harvest immediately — once flowering starts the bulb becomes fibrous.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Florence fennel (bulb type) is grown for the swollen stem base. Herb fennel is more adaptable. Both bolt readily in heat. Do not plant near dill or coriander — cross-pollination affects flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray — prevents leaf curl","details":"Apply copper while leafless. Leaf curl in zone 10 is severe if not treated — a warm humid autumn following harvest creates perfect conditions for overwintering spores. No exceptions to this spray.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune for airflow","details":"Open vase form. After harvest (December-January in zone 10), prune for airflow. Brown rot in the humid summer conditions of zone 10 requires maximum airflow through the canopy as a preventive measure.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin hard — essential in warm zones","details":"Thin to 12-15cm spacing. In zone 10, thinning is even more important than in cool zones — crowded fruit in warm conditions develops brown rot faster. Fruit touching any surface or another fruit is a disease vector.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest before brown rot develops","details":"In zone 10, the harvest window is very tight. A warm humid week at harvest time can destroy the entire crop with brown rot. Harvest at first sign of ripeness (background colour change, slight softness) and refrigerate immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very marginal — ultra-low chill varieties only
climate_note: Like nectarine — requires winter chilling. Most productive and best flavour in zones with 500-1000 chill hours. Brown rot at harvest is the primary management challenge.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 100g/m² at planting. Monthly liquid fish fertiliser maintains production through the cool season. Stop heavy feeding as spring warms — promotes soft frost-susceptible growth.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Begin harvesting outer leaves regularly","details":"Cut-and-come-again from 5-6 weeks. In zone 10, consistent harvesting of outer leaves delays bolting and extends productive life. Leave the growing centre intact.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Install exclusion netting","details":"Cabbage white butterfly is active throughout the cool season in zone 10. Fine mesh applied at transplant is the most effective and practical solution.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Succession sow for continuous supply","details":"A new kale planting every 6-8 weeks in cool months ensures continuous supply. As one planting begins to bolt, the next is coming into production.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables. Frost dramatically improves sweetness. Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves only to extend production for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply potassium at bulbing","details":"Sulphate of potash at 30g/m² when bulbs begin to swell. In zone 10, the switch from nitrogen to potassium must be made earlier than in cool zones because spring warming arrives sooner.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Stop watering","details":"Stop irrigation at 40-50% top yellowing — in zone 10 the curing process is faster than in cool zones due to warmer conditions. Letting the bulbs dry in the ground for a week before lifting is beneficial.","category":"watering"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest October-November and cure quickly","details":"Lift in October-November in zone 10. Cure in a warm airy shed for 2-3 weeks. In zone 10, do not leave in the ground past November — spring heat deteriorates the bulbs rapidly.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted from individual bulbs — each divides into a cluster of 4-8 new bulbs at harvest. Same day-length sensitivity as onions. Cure thoroughly before storage.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin to 5cm","details":"Thin as soon as seedlings are identifiable. In warm zones overcrowding is even more damaging than in cool zones — thinning to 5cm spacing is essential for any root development.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Begin harvesting small leaves regularly","details":"In warm zones carrots mature faster and stay at peak quality for a shorter window. Start tasting at 10 weeks (smaller, sweeter). Do not leave in the ground into the wet season.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Complete harvest before wet season","details":"Harvest all remaining carrots by September in tropical zones before monsoon rains waterlog the bed. Small roots are fine — better than leaving them to rot.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool season crop — April to September
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train new canes to trellis wires","details":"Tie new primocanes to the trellis as they grow through spring and summer. Summer-bearing varieties: these canes will fruit next year. Autumn/everbearing varieties: these canes will fruit at their tips in autumn of the same year.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest — critical annual task","details":"For summer varieties: immediately after harvest, cut all floricanes (the canes that fruited) to ground level. Tie the new primocanes neatly to the trellis. For autumn varieties: cut all canes to the ground in winter — they re-shoot and fruit on the new canes.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest every 2-3 days at peak season","details":"Ripe raspberries separate from the core (receptacle) cleanly, leaving behind the hollow cone shape. They are fragile — pick into shallow containers and refrigerate immediately. Harvest every 2-3 days to prevent waste from overripe fruit.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 600-900 chill hours. Fruits on second-year canes (summer varieties) or current-year canes (autumn/everbearing varieties). Post-harvest cane removal is the key annual task.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train onto trellis — direct young shoots upward","details":"Sugar snap peas produce vigorous growth. Direct shoots to the trellis in the first 2 weeks. Once climbing is established they self-direct.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 25g/m² at first flower. No nitrogen — peas fix their own. Potassium drives pod wall development — important for sugar snaps where the thick pod wall is the premium eating part.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Water at pod fill","details":"Consistent moisture at pod fill prevents shrivelled peas inside the pod. Water deeply every 2-3 days when plants are actively flowering and filling pods.","category":"watering"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest when pod is plump but snap-crisp","details":"Sugar snap peas are ready when the pod is rounded and full but still snaps cleanly when bent — not soft or yielding. The peas inside should be round but not hard. Harvest every 2-3 days. Overmature pods become tough and stringy.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Thick-walled edible pod (both pod and peas eaten together). Taller vine than snow peas — needs 1.8m support. Same management principles as snow peas and peas.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin seedlings to final spacing","details":"Thin to 8-10cm. Use thinnings as salad greens.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Harvest very small — 3-5cm","details":"In warm zones harvest turnips very small (3-5cm) and young. They develop sweetness at a smaller size than in cool zones and the pithiness window arrives earlier.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Complete harvest before wet season","details":"All turnips should be harvested by September in tropical zones. Wet season conditions cause immediate root rot.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool dry season — April to August
climate_note: Fast cool-season root crop. Harvest small (5-8cm) — older turnips become pithy and peppery. Leaves are also edible (turnip greens). Frost improves sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Install wind and frost protection","details":"Bananas shred in wind, reducing photosynthesis. Erect shade cloth windbreak on south and west. Have frost cloth ready for any nights below 4°C — foliage browns but regrows.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Bananas are very heavy feeders. Add organic matter monthly.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Remove all suckers but one follower","details":"As the main plant grows, it throws suckers. climate_note: Grows from suckers/rhizomes, not seedlings. Needs 10-12 months of warmth to fruit. Frost kills foliage; sustained frost kills the rhizome.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Erect support stakes","details":"Tall varieties (Aquadulce) reach 1.2m and fall over in wind and rain. Drive stakes at row ends and run string every 30cm of height as plants grow. This prevents lodging which causes disease and reduces yield.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply potassium fertiliser","details":"Apply sulphate of potash at 30g/m² when plants reach 40cm. Phosphorus at sowing (superphosphate 40g/m²) improves root development.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Pinch out growing tips when pods set","details":"When the lowest pods are visible, pinch out the soft growing tips (the top 10cm of each stem). This is critical — it deters black bean aphid colonies which colonise the tips, and it redirects energy into pod filling.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest pods when plump","details":"Harvest pods when the beans inside create visible bumps in the pod wall. Do not wait until the pod turns black — beans become starchy. Double-pod varieties: harvest outer pods first. Pick from the bottom up.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season crop. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium. Do not grow where temperatures regularly exceed 21°C at flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection in first 3 winters","details":"Young grapefruit are vulnerable to frost damage. Cover with frost cloth when temperatures are forecast below 1°C. Remove cloth during the day to prevent overheating.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune minimally — dead wood only","details":"Remove dead wood and crossing branches after fruit removal (August-September). In cool zones, avoid any pruning that stimulates new growth before winter.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest from July onward","details":"Grapefruit holds exceptionally well on the tree — it can be harvested over a 4-6 month window. In cool zones (9a/b), fruit may not develop full sweetness — early harvests will be more tart. Taste before picking.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Sheltered position — less cold-tolerant than lemon/orange
climate_note: Least cold-tolerant of commercial citrus. Requires warm nights to develop balanced acidity and sweetness. Self-fertile but large tree — allow 6m spacing.

key_activities: [{"timing":28,"activity":"Switch to potassium fertiliser","details":"Complete fertiliser at establishment. At first flower, sulphate of potash at 50g/m². High potassium produces firm, thick-skinned pumpkins that store well.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Train vines and support developing fruit","details":"In zone 10 pumpkin vines grow vigorously. Direct vines away from paths and garden beds. For vertically-trained vines, sling fruit in mesh or recycled stockings when it reaches tennis-ball size.","category":"planting"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Harvest at skin hardness and natural cord curing","details":"Harvest when the connecting stem (peduncle) begins to dry and the skin resists a fingernail. In zone 10, leave 15cm of stem on the pumpkin — this significantly improves storage life. Cure in the sun for 10-14 days before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Large vining crop needing 4-6m space or vertical support. Pollination by bees essential — male flowers appear first. Store cured pumpkins in cool dry conditions for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest by cutting stems to 10cm","details":"Cut stems back to 10cm when the plant reaches 20cm. This stimulates bushy growth and prevents the plant from becoming woody. In cool zones, harvest runs from spring through autumn — the plant dies back in winter.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back hard before or at first flowering","details":"When flower buds form, the essential oil in leaves is at its peak. Harvest heavily at this point — cut the whole plant back to 10cm. Dry the harvest in a warm airy place. The essential oil content is highest just before full flowering.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch roots lightly for winter in zone 8","details":"After the plant dies back to the ground in zone 8 winters, apply a light mulch of gravel or coarse sand over the crown. This prevents water sitting on the crown in winter which can rot the roots. The plant re-shoots reliably in spring.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Excellent — Mediterranean herb thrives in cool dry conditions; Dies back in winter but regrows from roots
climate_note: Mediterranean perennial. Thrives on neglect — poor, dry soil produces the most aromatic leaves. Do not overwater or over-fertilise.

key_activities: [{"timing":120,"activity":"Blanch in coolest months","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Begin blanching in June-July during the coolest available period. Quality will be below cool-zone standard but acceptable.","category":"planting"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest when mature","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Harvest blanched cardoon before September. Quality deteriorates quickly in subtropical warmth.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Globe artichoke relative grown for the blanched leaf stalks (not the buds). Requires blanching (excluding light for 3-4 weeks) to produce edible, mild-flavoured stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Calcium-rich soil amendment and potassium at first flower","details":"Apply dolomite lime (100g per plant) around the drip zone to prevent blossom end rot (calcium deficiency). At first flower, apply sulphate of potash (60g per plant). Consistent calcium and potassium are the two most important nutrients for fruit quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Remove laterals (side shoots) on indeterminate varieties","details":"For tall/indeterminate varieties: remove all side shoots (laterals) growing in the \"armpit\" between the main stem and a leaf. This keeps the plant to a single stem with maximum fruit size. Bush/determinate varieties: do not remove laterals — they are the fruiting structure.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured and aromatic","details":"Harvest when fully coloured and just yielding to gentle pressure. In cool zones, the season is short — harvest promptly. Green tomatoes picked before frost ripen well on a sunny windowsill. Do not refrigerate tomatoes — it destroys the flavour compounds.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost
climate_note: Stop setting fruit when night temperatures exceed 30°C or drop below 10°C. Consistent watering prevents blossom end rot and fruit cracking.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest by cutting stems — avoid woody sections","details":"Cut stems 5-10cm long — always cut into the green, leafy growth and never into the old grey woody stems (they do not regenerate). Harvest year-round in zones 8-10. The highest essential oil content occurs just before flowering.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back hard after flowering — twice yearly","details":"Cut the entire plant back by 40-50% twice per year (spring and after summer flowering). This prevents thyme from becoming an unproductive woody mound within 2-3 years. Do not cut into the grey woody base.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Replace plant from cuttings","details":"Even well-managed thyme becomes woody and less productive after 4-5 years. Take cuttings from current-season growth in spring, root in coarse sand, and replace the old plant. Named varieties (English, French, lemon) must be propagated this way — they do not come true from seed.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial. Thrives in poor, dry, well-drained conditions. Like oregano — rich soil and overwatering reduce flavour and shorten plant life.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Train main stem and begin lateral framework","details":"Train the main stem to the top of the trellis, then allow it to branch. Train laterals (side branches) horizontally along the wires to form the permanent fruiting framework. Fruiting occurs on new growth from this framework.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main harvest (April-June in zone 10), cut all fruited branches back to 30cm from the main framework wires. This removes old unproductive wood and stimulates a flush of new fruiting laterals. The vine looks drastically reduced immediately after this prune but recovers within 6-8 weeks.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":540,"activity":"Harvest fallen or shrivelled fruit","details":"In zone 10, passionfruit ripens March-July. Collect fallen fruit daily — it is ripe when it falls. Alternatively pick when the skin begins to wrinkle on the vine. Fully ripe fruit has a rich, intensely aromatic pulp.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Vigorous perennial vine needing a strong trellis. Self-fertile but bee pollination improves fruit set. Fusarium crown rot is the main killer — plant grafted varieties in zones 10-11.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Tip-prune following harvest completion","details":"After berry harvest, tip-prune by 30% to encourage bushy, productive growth for the following season. The shrub can be cut back harder (50%) every 3-4 years to rejuvenate it.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest after natural drying on the plant","details":"In warm zones Akudjura berries ripen and dry quickly on the plant. Harvest when fully shrivelled and brown. The caramel-tamarillo flavour is most intense in fully dried berries. Use as a ground spice in marinades, sauces and bread.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good zone — Mediterranean-type dry summers suit well
climate_note: Australian native desert shrub (Solanum centrale). Extremely drought-tolerant. Berries are dried and used as a spice with caramel-tamarillo flavour. Dislikes wet soils.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Check chill hour accumulation","details":"Track minimum overnight temperatures June-August. If temperatures stay above 7°C consistently, the plant will not set fruit well the following season. Warm winters are the primary limiting factor in zone 11.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a light annual prune","details":"Remove any dead or crossing wood. Minimal pruning in subtropical zones — plants grow vigorously but need energy directed to fruiting. Do not remove more than 20% of canes per year.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest early in the morning","details":"Fruit matures quickly in subtropical warmth. Harvest every 2-3 days. Refrigerate immediately. Net before any colour develops — birds locate fruit before visible ripeness.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Rabbiteye or low-chill varieties — Sunshine Blue, Powder Blue
climate_note: Soil pH 4.5-5.5 is critical — most Australian soils need acidification. Needs cross-pollination from a second variety. Chill hour requirements vary dramatically by variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 100g/m² at planting. Monthly liquid fish fertiliser maintains production through the cool season. Stop heavy feeding as spring warms — promotes soft frost-susceptible growth.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Begin harvesting outer leaves regularly","details":"Cut-and-come-again from 5-6 weeks. In zone 10, consistent harvesting of outer leaves delays bolting and extends productive life. Leave the growing centre intact.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Install exclusion netting","details":"Cabbage white butterfly is active throughout the cool season in zone 10. Fine mesh applied at transplant is the most effective and practical solution.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Succession sow for continuous supply","details":"A new kale planting every 6-8 weeks in cool months ensures continuous supply. As one planting begins to bolt, the next is coming into production.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables. Frost dramatically improves sweetness. Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves only to extend production for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Apply copper while leafless. In zone 10 with higher humidity, dormant sprays followed by petal-fall sprays are both important for brown rot control.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after harvest in summer — critical","details":"Prune in summer immediately after harvest. This is even more important in zone 10 than cool zones — the longer growing season allows wound healing before winter and reduces silver leaf disease risk.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit — especially important in warm zones","details":"In zone 10, warm temperatures drive rapid fruit development. Thin to 10-12cm between fruit. In warm conditions, crowded touching fruit develops brown rot rapidly before harvest.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at peak ripeness — do not delay","details":"In zone 10, nectarines move from ready to overripe quickly. Harvest in morning when fruit is cool. Brown rot can develop overnight on ripe fruit in warm humid conditions — harvest entire tree at ripeness and refrigerate immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Smooth-skinned peach variant with identical chill hour requirements. Brown rot at harvest is the main management challenge. Harvest timing is critical — nectarines do not improve after picking.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to final spacing","details":"Thin to 12cm. Daily watering in dry conditions. Mulch well.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Harvest small roots","details":"In subtropical zones harvest at whatever size develops by August-September before temperatures rise. Small parsnips still have acceptable flavour.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Complete harvest by September","details":"Do not leave roots in the ground past September in subtropical zones.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Root vegetable that improves dramatically with cold — frost converts starch to sugar. Very slow to germinate (21-28 days). Fresh seed essential — parsnip seed loses viability quickly.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser. In warm zone soils, nutrients flush through quickly — regular light feeding is more effective than one heavy application.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":24,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser. In warm zone soils, nutrients flush through quickly — regular light feeding is more effective than one heavy application.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Check for aphids and leaf-mining flies","details":"In warm zones, additional pests including lettuce leaf-mining flies appear. Fine insect mesh is the most practical control.","category":"pest"},{"timing":38,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser. In warm zone soils, nutrients flush through quickly — regular light feeding is more effective than one heavy application.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Harvest young — cut-and-come-again is best strategy","details":"In warm zones, harvest leaves young and continuously — do not wait for full head development. Full head lettuce in subtropical and tropical zones bolts before achieving commercial size. Cut individual leaves from the outside every few days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":52,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (4 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser. In warm zone soils, nutrients flush through quickly — regular light feeding is more effective than one heavy application.","category":"fertilizing"}]
extra_care: Cool dry season only — April to September
climate_note: Bolts (goes to seed) when temperatures exceed 25°C or day length increases beyond 14 hours. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). Apply copper while leafless (June-July). Brown rot is the primary disease challenge in zone 10 — preventive spraying is essential.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune for airflow","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). Prune after harvest in December-January. Open vase form. In zone 10, canopy airflow is the most important structural factor for brown rot prevention.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit — critical in warm zones","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). Thin to 8-10cm spacing when fruitlets are 1-2cm. In zone 10 warm conditions, crowded fruit touching each other spreads brown rot rapidly before harvest.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when ripe","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). In zone 10, plums move from ripe to overripe very quickly. Monitor daily as harvest approaches (November-December). Harvest in the morning when fruit is cool. Brown rot can destroy an entire crop overnight in warm humid conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Japanese plums (Santa Rosa, Mariposa) have lower chill requirements than European (600-800 hrs). Most varieties need cross-pollination. Summer prune to avoid silver leaf disease.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Provide afternoon shade if possible","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). In subtropical zones, afternoon shade during the coolest months slightly extends the pod-setting window. Sow on the south side of taller crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply light fertiliser","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Light application of balanced fertiliser at sowing only. Plants in subtropical zones have a short season — heavy feeding is unnecessary and can promote leafy growth over pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Pinch tips when pods appear","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Black bean aphid colonises rapidly in subtropical warmth. Pinch growing tips as soon as lowest pods form. Apply neem oil spray if aphid colonies appear.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest early at 4–5cm","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Harvest begins September-October in zone 11a. Pick as soon as pods are full — rising spring temperatures rapidly end the season. Process or freeze immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season crop. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium. Do not grow where temperatures regularly exceed 21°C at flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and apply potassium","details":"Eggplant develops to 80-100cm and branches heavily when fruiting. Stake each plant with a 1m stake. Apply sulphate of potash at 40g/m² at first flower. In cool zones, maximise nutrient support to make the most of the short season.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest before seeds show brown","details":"Cut (do not pull) fruit when the skin is glossy and firm. If pressure with a thumbnail shows no resistance, the fruit is overripe — seeds will be brown and flavour bitter. In cool zones harvest promptly at correct size to encourage continued production.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest all before frost","details":"Remove all remaining fruit before first autumn frost. Green eggplant will continue to ripen at room temperature if kept warm. Frost kills plants immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost
climate_note: Heat-loving crop — needs even more warmth than tomatoes or capsicum. Harvest while skin is glossy and before seeds develop brown inside.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Erect trellis and train shoots","details":"Vertical growing maximises yield, improves airflow (reducing powdery mildew), and makes harvest easier. Train the main stem vertically and tie at 20cm intervals. Pinch laterals at 2 leaves.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply potassium at fruiting","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² when first fruit set. Repeat every 4-5 weeks. In cool zones fertilise every 3 weeks due to shorter growing window.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest daily when fruiting begins","details":"Once cucumber production starts it is relentless. Harvest every 1-2 days — cucumbers left too long on the vine signal the plant to stop producing. Pull or cut with clean hands. Yellow cucumbers are overripe and bitter.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Warm season crop — October to March
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Highly productive but affected by powdery mildew. Male and female flowers separate — pollination by bees essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply mulch","details":"Apply mulch around plants. In windy cool zones, the large leaves catch wind and can rock the plant — a stake at the stem base improves stability. Water 2-3 times weekly.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest at 15-20cm — every 2 days","details":"Harvest zucchini at 15-20cm with a sharp knife. This is the most important management instruction: fruit left beyond 25cm becomes seedy, woody and stops the plant from producing. Harvest every 2 days at peak season. One oversize marrow halves weekly production.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Short season — start indoors; Quick-maturing varieties
climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":1,"activity":"Transplant deeply and stake firmly","details":"Plant seedlings (raised from Oct-Nov seed) in February-March in cool zones. Firm planting is critical — wind rock causes loose, leafy sprouts instead of tight buttons. Stake each plant with a 60cm stake tied at 3 points. 60cm spacing in rows 75cm apart.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 120g/m² or complete fertiliser with high nitrogen. Repeat at 30-day intervals. Brussels sprouts are very heavy feeders — under-feeding produces small, yellowing plants.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Remove yellowing lower leaves","details":"As the plant grows, strip away yellowing lower leaves regularly. This improves airflow (reducing fungal disease), keeps the planting base clean, and directs energy into sprout development rather than old foliage.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Top the plant to concentrate sprout development","details":"When the plant is 60-70cm tall and sprouts are visible, pinch or cut out the growing tip (the top 10cm). This forces energy into sizing up the existing sprouts rather than growing taller. Results in larger, tighter buttons.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest from base upward","details":"Twist off sprouts from the bottom of the stem first when they reach 2-4cm diameter and are firm. Work up the plant over 4-6 weeks. A frost improves flavour significantly — do not rush harvest in cold zones.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing brassica. Flavour significantly improves after frost. Firm planting prevents wind rock which causes loose sprouts.

Have frost cloth ready for any nights below 4°C — foliage browns but regrows.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Bananas are very heavy feeders. Add organic matter monthly.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Remove all suckers but one follower","details":"As the main plant grows, it throws suckers. Repeat annually.","category":"planting"},{"timing":480,"activity":"Harvest bunch before full ripeness","details":"Harvest when fruits plump up and lose their angular shape. Cut the whole bunch. Hang to ripen at room temperature. Do not refrigerate unripe bananas.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grows from suckers/rhizomes, not seedlings. Needs 10-12 months of warmth to fruit. Frost kills foliage; sustained frost kills the rhizome.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After fruit removal, remove crossing branches and manage height for easy picking. Remove any dead wood or diseased material. Zone 10 mandarins grow vigorously — annual size management is important.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at colour change and taste test","details":"Each variety has a different harvest window. Colour changes to orange-red when ready. Taste regularly near the expected harvest period — sweetness and juice confirm readiness. Mandarin holds on tree for 4-6 weeks without quality loss.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Premium mandarin zone — Murcott, Ellendale, Imperial
climate_note: Sweet flavour requires some cool nights in autumn and winter to develop properly. More cold-tolerant than lime or grapefruit. Self-fertile. Satsuma is the most frost-hardy variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser with trace elements","details":"Complete citrus fertiliser (including zinc and iron) in September. In cool zones, one application per year is appropriate. Late-season feeding stimulates soft frost-vulnerable new growth.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection for young trees","details":"Cover young trees (under 4-5 years) when frost is forecast. Established Satsuma trees can withstand -6°C. Young trees are more vulnerable — protect below -2°C.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a light annual prune","details":"After main harvest in autumn-winter, remove dead wood and crossing branches. Do not prune heavily — mandarins form on the outer canopy and heavy pruning reduces next season's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at full colour — Satsuma ripens before most citrus","details":"Satsuma ripens April-June in cool zones — one of the earliest mandarins. Satsumas can be fully ripe while still slightly green in cool zones — taste to confirm. Mandarins are the best indicator of correct harvest — taste, don't just look at colour.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Marginal — container growing recommended; Satsuma variety most cold-tolerant
climate_note: Sweet flavour requires some cool nights in autumn and winter to develop properly. More cold-tolerant than lime or grapefruit. Self-fertile. Satsuma is the most frost-hardy variety.

key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Begin rinsing and draining 3 times daily for 7 days","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, rinse sprouts 3 times per day (morning, midday, evening) to prevent mould growth that warm temperatures accelerate. Complete drainage between rinses is critical.","category":"watering"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at 4-5cm","details":"In warm climates, harvest at 4-5cm before the sprouts begin to deteriorate. Refrigerate immediately after a final rinse. Use within 2 days (shorter shelf life in warm climates).","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Grow in air-conditioned environment in peak tropical heat
climate_note: Indoor crop — grown in a jar or tray, not the garden. Not zone-dependent. The same process applies in all climates.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a structural prune","details":"Prune after the main harvest to maintain access height. In humid subtropical zones, thin the canopy to improve airflow and reduce fungal disease pressure.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Check fruit maturity with oil test","details":"Tropical avocados can produce year-round depending on variety. Sharwil, Reed and Monroe perform well in subtropical zones. Harvest when skin turns colour (Hass) or when flesh oil content exceeds 8% (confirm by picking a test fruit).","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent conditions — manage Phytophthora with well-drained soil
climate_note: Requires warm, frost-free conditions. Shallow roots are drought-sensitive. Type A and B varieties needed for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Check swollen stem size regularly","details":"Start checking at 40 days — the bulb can go from ideal to woody and split within a week in growing conditions. Harvest at 5-8cm diameter while skin is still smooth.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"This is the most important instruction for kohlrabi: harvest at the correct size (5-8cm). Left too long it becomes woody, fibrous and inedible. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing brassica. Harvest when bulb (swollen stem) reaches 5-8cm — do not wait or it becomes woody and splits. Quicker to harvest than most brassicas.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Complete fertiliser with emphasis on nitrogen. Broccoli in zone 10 grows quickly and needs consistent feeding. key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Remove lower leaves regularly","details":"More frequent removal needed in warm humid conditions — fungal disease (especially black rot) spreads quickly in zone 11+ without good airflow around the base.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Top early to force development","details":"Top at 50-60cm height — earlier than cool zones. key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Pinch growing tip","details":"Pinch the main stem tip when plants reach 15cm. extra_care: Pinch tips regularly to prevent flowering
climate_note: Frost-sensitive annual. Bolts in heat. Best in warm but not extreme conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":25,"activity":"Harvest as micro-greens or very young","details":"In warm zones harvest spinach as micro-greens (7-10cm) for the best quality. The heat-to-bolt progression is rapid — very young harvest is the only reliable approach.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most bolt-prone cool-season vegetable. Bolts within days of temperatures exceeding 20°C. Asian (Malabar) spinach is an excellent heat-tolerant substitute in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Install plant supports","details":"Peas send out tendrils within 10-14 days of germination. Have trellis or peasticks in place before germination. Every-2-day harvesting is essential as the season warms. At first sign of pod yellowing, harvest everything remaining immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool season only — avoid summer; Two crops: autumn and late winter
climate_note: Direct sow — peas resent root disturbance. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation. Pod quality drops rapidly in heat — harvest every 2-3 days.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin to 5-8cm spacing","details":"Thin twice: 3cm at 3 weeks, 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinning is the most important and most skipped step. key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Support and shade cloth if needed","details":"In zone 11+, 30% shade cloth reduces heat stress on developing peas. key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train new canes","details":"Tie new primocanes vertically to the trellis wires as they grow. extra_care: Use thornless varieties for ease of harvest
climate_note: Requires 200-700 chill hours. Grown from canes or root divisions, not seedlings. Fruits on second-year canes (floricanes).

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 25-30cm spacing","details":"Thin promptly — endive needs space to form a full head. key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply mulch","details":"Apply mulch around plants. One oversize marrow halves weekly production.","category":"harvest"}]

climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid fish emulsion or complete fertiliser. key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Check for scale insects and leafminer","details":"Scale insects and citrus leafminer are common in warm zones. key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Do not protect from frost — improves head quality","details":"In cool zones, a frost on the developing head triggers the formation of a tighter, less bitter head. climate_note: Italian chicory family. Frost reduces bitterness and tightens the head. Cut back to stump after first head harvest — radicchio regrows and produces again.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Thin to 12-15cm spacing","details":"Thin at 5cm seedling height. Do not delay — crowding produces forked roots that are difficult to use.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Harvest as they reach size","details":"In zone 10, parsnips are ready from July-October. They do not develop the same frost-driven sweetness as cool-zone equivalents, but autumn-winter conditions still improve flavour compared to summer production.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Complete harvest before spring warming","details":"Harvest all remaining roots by September-October before spring warmth causes re-shooting and root deterioration.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Root vegetable that improves dramatically with cold — frost converts starch to sugar. Very slow to germinate (21-28 days). Fresh seed essential — parsnip seed loses viability quickly.

key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Begin rinsing and draining 3 times daily for 7 days","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, rinse sprouts 3 times per day (morning, midday, evening) to prevent mould growth that warm temperatures accelerate. Refrigerate immediately after a final rinse. Use within 2 days (shorter shelf life in warm climates).","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Rinse 3x daily in humid conditions — mould risk
climate_note: Indoor crop — grown in a jar or tray, not the garden. Not zone-dependent. The same process applies in all climates.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut down fern in winter","details":"After fronds yellow in autumn, cut to ground level. Remove and compost debris. Apply potassium-rich fertiliser (sulphate of potash) and top-dress with compost.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Begin harvesting spears","details":"Cut spears when 15-20cm tall with tight tips, using a knife 2-3cm below soil. Cool-zone harvest runs August-October. Stop harvesting after 6-8 weeks to allow crown recovery. Scheduled from approximately year 3 after planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Perennial — do not harvest in year 1 (cool zones) or years 1-2 (warm zones). Requires winter dormancy for reliable annual cropping.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser","details":"Use a citrus fertiliser containing nitrogen, trace elements (zinc, iron, manganese) in September-October when growth resumes. Apply at label rates to drip line. extra_care: Container growing or sheltered wall position
climate_note: Most frost-tolerant citrus. Compact tree suitable for container growing. Self-fruitful. Fruit is eaten whole — skin is sweet, flesh is tart.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest from 6-8 weeks","details":"Always harvest outer leaves only — leave at least 4-6 central leaves. Once a central flower stalk appears, the plant is finished — remove and replace with a new sowing. Scheduled from approximately year undefined after planting.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Switch to potassium at bulb swell","details":"Apply sulphate of potash (40g/m²) when bulbs first become visible. Harvest every 1-2 days at snap stage.","category":"harvest"}]

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Earth up as plants grow","details":"As leeks grow, mound soil progressively around the shaft every 3-4 weeks.
