Each earthing up must cover all previously exposed green growth.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Check shaft thickness","details":"Leeks are harvestable from 1.5cm shaft diameter but best at 2.5-4cm. If the soil is hard, loosen with a fork first. Trim roots and outer leaves. Leeks left in the ground in cool zones continue growing and hold quality for months.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant deeply and blanch shaft — best zone for leeks
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season allium. Deep planting and earthing up blanches the white shaft — the primary eating part. More cold-tolerant than onions.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Mulch root zone heavily","details":"Deep mulch (15cm) protects roots in cool zone winters. Complete drainage between rinses is critical.","category":"watering"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at 4-5cm","details":"In warm climates, harvest at 4-5cm before the sprouts begin to deteriorate. Refrigerate immediately after a final rinse. Use within 2 days (shorter shelf life in warm climates).","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Rinse 3x daily — keep in air-conditioned environment if possible
climate_note: Indoor crop — grown in a jar or tray, not the garden. Not zone-dependent. The same process applies in all climates.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Erect support trellis or peasticks","details":"Even \"dwarf\" peas benefit from support. Tall climbing varieties reach 1.8-2m. Push in peasticks (bushy twigs) immediately after sowing — peas send out tendrils within 2 weeks and need something to grip. Climbing varieties on a wire trellis.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium — no nitrogen needed","details":"Peas fix their own nitrogen — adding nitrogen fertiliser produces lush foliage and poor pod set. Apply sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at first flower. This improves pod fill and yield significantly.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Water at pod fill","details":"Irregular watering at pod-fill stage causes peas to shrivel inside the pod (\"blind\" pods). Consistent moisture from first flower through harvest is the most important management step for peas. Mulch well.","category":"watering"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest every 2-3 days","details":"Pick peas when the pod is well-filled but the peas inside still feel round (not lumpy). Harvest every 2-3 days — pods left too long become starchy and tough. Picking stimulates continued flowering and extends the harvest by 2-3 weeks.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent cool-season crop — autumn sowing produces spring harvest
climate_note: Direct sow — peas resent root disturbance. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation. Pod quality drops rapidly in heat — harvest every 2-3 days.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 120g/m² or ammonium sulfate at 40g/m². Side-dress again at 4 and 8 weeks. Consistent nitrogen drives head development. Any yellowing of leaves signals nitrogen deficiency — correct immediately.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Blanch the curd as it develops","details":"When the curd (head) begins to form (visible white dome 2-3cm across), tie the largest outer leaves over it with a rubber band or soft string. This protects from sunlight which yellows and bitters the curd — blanching keeps it white and mild.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check for caterpillars under leaf cover","details":"Cabbage white caterpillars hide in the outer leaves. Check twice weekly and apply Bt spray. Caterpillar damage inside tied leaves is not visible until harvest.","category":"pest"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Harvest before curd separates","details":"Cut when the curd is solid, white and compact. Once the surface begins to look \"ricey\" (separated florets) it is past peak. In cool zones cauliflower holds on the plant for 1-2 weeks — in warm conditions it must be harvested immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: More cold-sensitive than broccoli. The curd (head) must be blanched by tying outer leaves over it to prevent yellowing and bitterness in sunny conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply light fertiliser","details":"Very light application of blood and bone. In warm zones excess nitrogen dramatically increases bitterness.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":40,"activity":"Harvest young outer leaves — head may not form","details":"In subtropical zones a tight head may not develop. Harvest young individual outer leaves (less bitter than mature) as cut-and-come-again greens. This is a more realistic outcome than expecting a full tight head.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest any head that forms","details":"If a head does form, harvest immediately — warm conditions cause rapid deterioration and the head opens quickly into a loose, very bitter mass.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Italian chicory family. Frost reduces bitterness and tightens the head. Cut back to stump after first head harvest — radicchio regrows and produces again.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply acidic fertiliser","details":"Pineapple prefers slightly acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5). Use azalea/camellia fertiliser or ericaceous fertiliser. Monthly application from spring to autumn.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install full frost protection in winter","details":"Move container indoors or to a frost-free shed at any temperature below 5°C. Pineapple leaves are damaged below 5°C and the plant is killed below 1°C.","category":"planting"},{"timing":540,"activity":"Harvest when base turns yellow-gold","details":"In zone 9b pineapple takes up to 3 years to fruit. If it fruits at all, harvest when the base of the fruit begins to yellow. Do not wait for full surface yellowing — overripe pineapple ferments quickly on the plant.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from crowns, ratoons or slips (not seedlings). Takes 18-24 months from crown to fruit in warm zones; up to 3 years in cool zones. Smooth Cayenne and Bethlehem are common varieties.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest by cutting stems — avoid woody sections","details":"Cut stems 5-10cm long — always cut into the green, leafy growth and never into the old grey woody stems (they do not regenerate). Harvest year-round in zones 8-10. The highest essential oil content occurs just before flowering.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back hard after flowering — twice yearly","details":"Cut the entire plant back by 40-50% twice per year (spring and after summer flowering). This prevents thyme from becoming an unproductive woody mound within 2-3 years. Do not cut into the grey woody base.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Replace plant from cuttings","details":"Even well-managed thyme becomes woody and less productive after 4-5 years. Take cuttings from current-season growth in spring, root in coarse sand, and replace the old plant. Named varieties (English, French, lemon) must be propagated this way — they do not come true from seed.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial. Thrives in poor, dry, well-drained conditions. Like oregano — rich soil and overwatering reduce flavour and shorten plant life.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply light fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 50g/m² after shoots establish. One application only — excess nutrition in warm zones produces soft poorly-stored shallots.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply potassium at bulbing","details":"Sulphate of potash at 25g/m² when bulbs visibly swell. Stop nitrogen immediately.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Stop water when tops yellow","details":"Stop watering promptly. In subtropical zones the curing period is shorter — the warm dry air cures the neck quickly.","category":"watering"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest September — store in cool dry conditions","details":"Harvest in September before heat returns. Cure for 2 weeks. In subtropical zones shallots store for 3-6 months (shorter than cool-zone equivalents).","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted from individual bulbs — each divides into a cluster of 4-8 new bulbs at harvest. Same day-length sensitivity as onions. Cure thoroughly before storage.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Apply complete fertiliser with nitrogen at transplant. Follow with liquid fish fertiliser every 3 weeks. Consistent nitrogen is the single biggest driver of solid head formation.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Install exclusion netting for caterpillars","details":"In zone 10, cabbage white butterfly is active most of the year. Fine insect mesh over the bed at transplant is the most effective approach. Remove only for maintenance.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check for early splitting in warm spells","details":"In zone 10, sudden warmth after cool development can cause heads to split as they resume rapid growth. Harvest immediately if cracks appear at the crown.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":85,"activity":"Harvest at full size","details":"Heads should feel solid and heavy for their size. In zone 10, autumn-planted cabbage can reach 1-2kg. Cut at the base and compost the stump.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season brassica. Heavy feeder — needs consistent nitrogen. Firm planting prevents splitting.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train new canes","details":"Tie new primocanes vertically to the trellis wires as they grow. First-year canes (primocanes) will not fruit — they develop into next year's fruiting floricanes.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after fruiting","details":"In summer after harvest, cut all floricanes (old canes that fruited) to ground level. Tie the new primocanes to the trellis horizontally — they will fruit next season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest when fully black","details":"Fruit is ready when it pulls free with almost no resistance and is fully black (not red). Taste — fully ripe blackberries are sweet, not tart. Pick every 2-3 days during the harvest window.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 200-700 chill hours. Grown from canes or root divisions, not seedlings. Fruits on second-year canes (floricanes).

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 30cm spacing","details":"Thin to final spacing when seedlings have 3-4 leaves. Do not delay thinning — crowded fennel bolts prematurely.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Hill up soil around the base","details":"When the swollen stem (the bulb) begins to develop at the base, hill up soil around it to 5cm depth. This blanches the bulb, making it whiter and sweeter. Repeat as the bulb grows.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest before bolt or when bolting","details":"Cut the whole plant at soil level when the bulb is 8-12cm across and firm. If flower stems emerge from the centre, harvest immediately — once flowering starts the bulb becomes fibrous.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Spring and summer crop only in cool zones
climate_note: Florence fennel (bulb type) is grown for the swollen stem base. Herb fennel is more adaptable. Both bolt readily in heat. Do not plant near dill or coriander — cross-pollination affects flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Mulch heavily — soil warmth is critical","details":"Apply black plastic mulch (plant through holes) or 10cm of straw mulch over the mounds. Soil warmth drives sweet potato growth — cool soils massively reduce yield. Black plastic mulch raises soil temperature by 3-5°C.","category":"planting"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Harvest before first frost","details":"Dig carefully with a fork before first autumn frost. In cool zones the tubers will be smaller than in tropical zones but perfectly good quality. Cure in a warm (25-30°C) humid position for 10-14 days — this converts starches to sugars and heals any wounds in the skin.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from slips (vine cuttings), not true seedlings or seed. Needs 4-5 frost-free months minimum. Harvest triggers the development of sweetness — cure for 1-2 weeks after harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a winter structural prune","details":"Remove crossing branches and deadwood. Select 3-5 main scaffold branches. In zone 10, figs can become large — manage height to 3-4m by removing dominant leaders. Apply sulphate of potash (60g per tree) in late winter to promote fruit development.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":600,"activity":"Leave breba fruit on plant","details":"In zone 10, the early breba crop (November) can partially ripen. Leave it on the tree. The main crop follows in February-April and is substantially larger.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":800,"activity":"Harvest in morning before fruit softens","details":"Ripe figs are fragile — pick in the cool of the morning. In zone 10, figs ripen from February-April. A large established tree can produce 50+ kg. Process excess into jam or dry in the sun.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Extremely drought-tolerant once established. Two crops possible in warm zones: breba (on old wood, Nov) and main (on new wood, Jan-April). Most varieties are self-pollinating.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Prune in dry season to force dormancy","details":"In tropical zones grapes must be forced into dormancy by hard pruning in the dry season (June-July) and withholding water. This artificial stress substitutes for the natural cold dormancy that tropical climates do not provide.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Resume watering and fertilising after pruning","details":"After 4-6 weeks of dry \"dormancy\", resume irrigation and apply complete fertiliser. Shoot emergence and flowering should follow within 3-4 weeks.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":240,"activity":"Check for fruit fly and disease","details":"Both Queensland fruit fly and fungal diseases (powdery mildew, downy mildew) are severe in tropical zones. Sulfur sprays from budburst and Eco-naturalure bait from bunch formation are the minimum management program.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest quickly when ripe","details":"Tropical climate grapes deteriorate rapidly at ripeness. Harvest individual bunches at first eating ripeness and refrigerate. Do not expect the storage life of cool-zone grapes.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very marginal — specialty tropical varieties only
climate_note: Dormant pruning is essential — prune to 2-bud spurs each winter. Grapes fruit on current season growth from last year's wood. Requires chill hours for dormancy and reliable fruiting.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Erect trellis","details":"Snow peas are climbing plants (1-1.5m). Have trellis or peasticks in position before germination — they begin sending out tendrils very early. Net or string trellis works well.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 20g/m² at first flower. Peas fix their own nitrogen — do not add nitrogen fertiliser. Potassium drives pod fill and overall yield.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Harvest when flat and pods are full","details":"Pick snow peas when the pod is flat and full width but before the peas inside begin to bulge. Once peas swell visibly inside the pod, the eating quality drops (they become starchy). Harvest every 2-3 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Clear plants at end of season and compost","details":"At season end, pull plants and compost. Snow pea roots fix nitrogen — leave roots in the soil for 2-3 weeks before digging in. This is a genuine soil improvement benefit.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Flat edible-pod peas. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Harvest before seeds develop inside the pod. Inoculate with rhizobium.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Install 1.5m trellis","details":"Snow peas grow vigorously in zone 10 cool conditions. A 1.5m trellis gives maximum cropping space.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 20g/m². Do not add nitrogen. In zone 10, the cool season growing period for snow peas is 8-12 weeks — fertilise precisely at flowering stage.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days","details":"In zone 10, harvest every 2 days when plants are in full production. Pods mature faster than in cool zones. Do not let pods fill with peas — harvest while flat.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Pull before spring heat","details":"Complete harvest by September in zone 10. Rising temperatures cause rapid quality deterioration and flower drop. Pull plants at first sustained warmth.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Flat edible-pod peas. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Harvest before seeds develop inside the pod. Inoculate with rhizobium.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train canes onto trellis","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). In zone 10a, erect trellis and train canes as per cool zones. Drip irrigation is preferable to overhead — wet foliage in warm conditions promotes botrytis (grey mould) which destroys raspberry crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Potassium emphasis at flowering","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). In zone 10a where chill hours are marginal, potassium application at first flower is critical for any fruit set to occur. Apply sulphate of potash at 50g per plant. Blood and bone at budburst.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). Same as cool zones — remove all fruited canes immediately after harvest. This renovation is the foundation of next year's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest quickly in zone 10 warmth","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). In zone 10, harvest every 1-2 days. Ripe raspberries deteriorate very quickly in warmth. Pick in the early morning when fruit is cool.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 600-900 chill hours. Fruits on second-year canes (summer varieties) or current-year canes (autumn/everbearing varieties). Post-harvest cane removal is the key annual task.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant spray","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). Copper spray in June-July while leafless. Brown rot is a serious risk in zone 10 where humidity can be higher than in cool growing regions.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune to open vase form","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). Keep trees small (under 3m) for easy netting. Summer prune after harvest. Shade cloth can be used to provide some temperature reduction during fruit development.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Net at petal fall","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). In zone 10 marginal areas, the crop is small and precious. Net from petal fall (not just at colour) to protect any fruit that sets.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Begin harvesting fruit when ripe","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Not suitable — insufficient chill hours). Fruiting may be erratic in zone 10a. Harvest any fruit that develops at first sign of colour change — leaving fruit too long in warm conditions causes rapid deterioration.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 700-1000+ chill hours for most varieties. Among the most chill-demanding fruit trees. Needs a pollination partner (most varieties). Net for birds before harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings have 3-4 true leaves. In cool conditions, coriander can be grown at 5cm spacing for leaf harvest. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Succession sow every 2-3 weeks","details":"A single coriander sowing in cool conditions may produce for only 3-4 weeks before bolting. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.","category":"planting"},{"timing":21,"activity":"Harvest leaves before flower stalk emerges","details":"Cut leaves regularly from young plants. The moment a central flower stalk begins to rise, leaf quality drops. Harvest the entire plant at this point — stems and leaves are still edible.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":40,"activity":"Leave some plants to flower and set seed","details":"Leave one or two plants to bolt and produce seed (coriander seeds are a spice in themselves). Once seed turns brown, cut the whole stem and dry in a paper bag to collect seeds for cooking or next sowing.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Notoriously bolt-prone. Direct sow — resents transplanting. Keep cool and harvest before flower stalks emerge. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Install drip irrigation and apply mulch","details":"Consistent moisture through drip irrigation is ideal. Heavy mulch insulates roots and prevents soil moisture loss in tropical heat.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Begin harvesting regularly","details":"Harvest fruit when glossy and firm. In tropical zones eggplant produces year-round. Monitor for two-spotted mite in dry conditions — stippling on leaves with fine webbing indicates mite presence.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Do a hard winter prune (now or within winter)","details":"Cut to a 30-40cm framework each year in June-July. This restores productive vigour and removes old unproductive wood. New growth emerges within 2-3 weeks and flowers within 6-8 weeks in warm zones.","category":"pruning"}]
extra_care: Year-round potential — short dry season rest improves production
climate_note: Heat-loving crop — needs even more warmth than tomatoes or capsicum. Harvest while skin is glossy and before seeds develop brown inside.

key_activities: [{"timing":7,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings have 2 true leaves. Crowded radish produce small, poorly shaped roots. Thinnings can be eaten as radish sprouts.","category":"planting"},{"timing":22,"activity":"Check root size daily from 20 days","details":"Radish can be ready in 25 days and become pithy within 30-35 days. Begin checking at 20 days by brushing away soil at the base. Harvest when the root reaches 2-3cm diameter — do not wait for them to look \"finished\" above ground.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"This is the most important radish instruction: harvest at correct size (2-3cm). Left even 3-4 days too long, radish becomes pithy, hollow and extremely hot/harsh. Succession sowing is better than trying to extend a single planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fastest vegetable in the garden (25-35 days). Bolts and becomes hot/woody in heat. Harvest promptly at correct size — even 3-4 days too late produces pithy, harsh radish.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Straw mulch in winter","details":"Apply straw mulch around plants in June-July to insulate roots in any mild frosts and to protect developing fruit later in spring.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Net before colour — birds move quickly","details":"In zone 10, lorikeets and waxeyes are major strawberry predators. Net the bed before any colour development. Net to ground level — birds will walk under loose netting.","category":"pest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Check for botrytis in humid spring","details":"In zone 10 humid spring weather, grey mould (botrytis) develops in packed fruit. Ensure good airflow through the planting. Remove any affected fruit immediately. Apply registered fungicide if severe.","category":"pest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Harvest every day at peak season","details":"Zone 10 strawberries ripen rapidly in spring warmth. Harvest daily at peak. After 3-4 weeks the main flush is over — plants produce a smaller trickle until summer heat ends production.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from runners (not seed). Plant crowns in autumn, harvest spring. Replace plants every 2-3 years — older plants have lower yield. Protect from birds and slugs at fruit set.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant spray","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable). Copper spray in June-July while leafless. Brown rot is a serious risk in zone 10 where humidity can be higher than in cool growing regions.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune to open vase form","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable). Keep trees small (under 3m) for easy netting. Summer prune after harvest. Shade cloth can be used to provide some temperature reduction during fruit development.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Net at petal fall","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable). In zone 10 marginal areas, the crop is small and precious. Net from petal fall (not just at colour) to protect any fruit that sets.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Begin harvesting fruit when ripe","details":"Adapted for zone 11a (Not suitable). Fruiting may be erratic in zone 10a. Harvest any fruit that develops at first sign of colour change — leaving fruit too long in warm conditions causes rapid deterioration.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires 700-1000+ chill hours for most varieties. Among the most chill-demanding fruit trees. Needs a pollination partner (most varieties). Net for birds before harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Select hermaphrodite plant","details":"Once plants begin to flower (4-5 months), identify: male has thin stems with clusters of small flowers; female has large solitary flowers; hermaphrodite has flowers directly on the trunk — keep this plant. Remove males once identified.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Remove low suckers to manage height","details":"Papaya produces suckers at the base. Allow 1-2 low suckers to grow as replacements. When the main trunk reaches 2m, cut it back to 1m — the trunk will branch and produce a new growing tip at a manageable height.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest when 30-50% yellow","details":"Zone 10 papaya ripens slower than tropical equivalents. Harvest when 30-50% of the skin has turned yellow-orange. Ripen at room temperature — refrigerate only after cutting. Replace trees after 3-4 years as production declines.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good production in warm sheltered sites
climate_note: Fast-growing tropical/subtropical tree. Short-lived (3-5 years productive). May include hermaphrodite, male or female plants from seed — hermaphrodite produces best fruit. Water-sensitive — do not waterlog.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Install plant supports","details":"Erect stake-and-string support when plants reach 30cm. Zone 10 broad beans can produce tall crops — good support prevents wind damage.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Pinch out tips — black aphid control","details":"Pinch out growing tips when 4-6 pods are visible on the stem. Black bean aphid infests broad bean tips in zone 10 and spreads rapidly in warm conditions. Pinching out removes the primary colony site.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest before heat returns","details":"In zone 10, the window before warming spring temperatures closes the harvest is short. Pick when pods are full but green. Process or freeze quickly — pods deteriorate rapidly in warm conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Sow April-July — avoid spring sowing (heat causes poor pod set)
climate_note: Cool-season crop. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium. Do not grow where temperatures regularly exceed 21°C at flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back to crown after main harvest","details":"After the primary harvest (central heads cut), cut the plant back to 30cm stubs. In cool zones this triggers a second flush of heads in autumn. Clear all old leaf material to prevent fungal disease.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch crowns heavily for winter","details":"After the growing season, cut plants to ground level in cool zones. Apply 15cm compost mulch over the crown to protect from hard frosts. The crown overwinters underground and re-shoots in spring.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest central bud before scales open","details":"Cut the central bud (largest) first when it is 8-12cm across and the scales are still tightly closed. A small gap between scales indicates the bud is past prime. Cut with 15cm of stem for ease of eating. Side buds follow.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Mulch mounded rows","details":"Heavy mulch (10cm sugar cane or straw) over mounds retains moisture through the dry season and reduces weed competition. In the wet season, the mulch also moderates soil temperature.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Begin partial harvest from one end of row","details":"In tropical zones, sweet potato can be partially harvested (digging from one end of the mound) while leaving the remainder to continue growing. This staged approach is common in tropical food gardens.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Cure for sweetness","details":"Even in tropical zones, cure harvested tubers for 7-10 days in a warm (25-30°C) dry position before eating. Curing dramatically improves sweetness and texture. Store in a cool, dry, dark position — not the refrigerator.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from slips (vine cuttings), not true seedlings or seed. Needs 4-5 frost-free months minimum. Harvest triggers the development of sweetness — cure for 1-2 weeks after harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Check plant for pests and disease","details":"Water weekly for the first 4-6 weeks. After establishment warrigal greens are essentially self-sufficient. No regular fertiliser needed — they evolved in nutrient-poor coastal conditions.","category":"watering"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Begin cut-and-come-again harvest","details":"Harvest young shoot tips and leaves by cutting back stems by 30-40%. The plant regrows vigorously. In cool zones, production slows in winter but rarely stops entirely.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Blanch before eating — mandatory","details":"ALWAYS blanch warrigal greens before eating: boil in a large pot of water for 2 minutes, then drain and refresh in cold water. This removes oxalates that cause kidney problems if eaten raw. After blanching, treat like spinach in any recipe.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut back hard annually","details":"Once per year, cut back hard to 15cm above ground. This renovation stimulates fresh, productive growth and prevents the plant from becoming a sprawling, unmanageable mound.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Australian native coastal plant (Tetragonia tetragonioides). Edible leaves MUST be blanched (boiled 2+ minutes) before eating to reduce oxalates. Extremely drought and salt tolerant.

key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Do not protect from frost — improves head quality","details":"In cool zones, a frost on the developing head triggers the formation of a tighter, less bitter head. Do not protect radicchio from frost — it benefits the crop distinctly.","category":"planting"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest outer leaves first — check head firmness","details":"Harvest outer leaves as needed from 8-10 weeks. The central head forms at 10-12 weeks — harvest when it feels firm and compact. The brilliant red and white colouration develops with cold exposure.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut to stump for regrowth","details":"After harvesting the main head, cut the plant to a 5cm stump. New heads will grow from the base over the following 4-6 weeks — often more than one per stump. Second-growth radicchio is typically milder than the first harvest.","category":"pruning"}]
extra_care: Excellent cool-season crop — frost reduces bitterness
climate_note: Italian chicory family. Frost reduces bitterness and tightens the head. Cut back to stump after first head harvest — radicchio regrows and produces again.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin outer-leaf harvest from 6-8 weeks","details":"Always harvest outer leaves only — leave at least 4-6 central leaves. This cut-and-come-again method allows a single planting to produce for 12-18 months in cool zones.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Remove any yellowing leaves","details":"Remove yellowing or damaged outer leaves at the base. This keeps the planting clean, prevents fungal disease and redirects plant energy to new growth.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Replace plant at bolting","details":"Silverbeet bolts (runs to seed) in its second year or after exposure to heat. Once a central flower stalk appears, the plant is finished — remove and replace with a new sowing. Scheduled from approximately year undefined after planting.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Mulch root zone heavily","details":"Deep mulch (15cm) protects roots in cool zone winters. Figs are deciduous — they die back to woody structure in winter and re-shoot strongly in spring.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune in winter while leafless","details":"In winter, remove crossing branches, dead wood and any vigorous vertical growth (epicormic shoots). In cool zones keep the tree to a manageable size — 2-3m ensures good fruit ripening. Remove some of the oldest branches each winter to stimulate new productive wood.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin breba crop in cool zones","details":"The early breba crop (on previous season wood) rarely ripens in cool zones — remove breba fruit in September to direct energy into the main crop which follows in late summer/autumn.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":800,"activity":"Harvest when skin softens and splits at neck","details":"Ripe figs droop from their attachment point, the skin softens and the neck may split slightly. Gently push against the base — if it yields it is ripe. In cool zones, ripening can be extended by placing a clear plastic bag over individual fruit clusters.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Hardy but tops may die back in severe winters — mulch root zone heavily; Brown Turkey and Black Genoa are the most cold-tolerant
climate_note: Extremely drought-tolerant once established. Two crops possible in warm zones: breba (on old wood, Nov) and main (on new wood, Jan-April). Most varieties are self-pollinating.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Mulch for moisture retention","details":"Apply 8cm mulch after establishment. Okra is surprisingly drought-tolerant once established but consistent moisture improves pod quality and reduces fibrous texture.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash 40g/m² at first flower. Complete fertiliser monthly through the long growing season in zone 10.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days — this is critical","details":"Zone 10 summer heat causes rapid pod development. A pod that is 5cm today will be 12cm and fibrous in 3 days. Harvest every 2 days without exception. Use scissors and gloves.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Heat-loving tropical vegetable. Harvest pods at 5-8cm — older pods become fibrous and tough within 2-3 days of reaching harvestable size.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 100g/m² after transplanting or thinning. Kale is a heavy feeder — nitrogen drives leaf production. Repeat every 4-6 weeks for continuous production.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Begin cut-and-come-again harvest","details":"Harvest outer leaves only — always leave at least 4-6 central leaves. Kale harvested this way from one planting can produce for 6-12 months in cool zones. Younger, smaller leaves are most tender.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Check for caterpillars and aphids","details":"Cabbage white butterfly caterpillars and grey cabbage aphid are the primary pests. Bt spray for caterpillars, forceful water spray for aphids. Fine insect mesh (exclusion netting) eliminates both without spraying.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest young leaves for best flavour","details":"Young kale leaves (20-30cm) have the best flavour. After frost, taste older leaves — they will have sweetened significantly. Harvest large leaves for cooking, young leaves for salads.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — frost improves sweetness dramatically; Year-round crop with succession sowing
climate_note: One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables. Frost dramatically improves sweetness. Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves only to extend production for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 10cm — thinnings are edible","details":"Thin at 3-4cm seedling height. Thinnings make excellent salad greens. Crowded turnips produce small deformed roots.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Check root size from 35 days","details":"Begin checking by pulling a test root at 35 days. Harvest at 5-7cm diameter — the sweet spot for texture and flavour. Cold temperatures convert turnip starch to sugar (same as parsnip and carrot) — autumn and winter turnips in cool zones are excellent quality.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Harvest before bolting or overgrowth","details":"Do not leave turnips beyond 60-70 days — they become large, hollow and very hot-flavoured. Succession sow every 3 weeks for continuous supply of young, sweet turnips.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast cool-season root crop. Harvest small (5-8cm) — older turnips become pithy and peppery. Leaves are also edible (turnip greens). Frost improves sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main fruiting period (autumn-winter), remove crossing branches and shape for access. The thorns make gloves essential.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest as individual fruit mature","details":"Finger limes fruit over an extended period (March-August in zone 10). Harvest individual fruit as they reach colour and separate with a slight twist. Some trees produce two flushes per year in zone 10.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian native citrus. Thorny shrub/tree from subtropical rainforest. Grafted varieties fruit from 3-4 years; seed-grown may take 7-10 years. Fruit contains "citrus caviar" vesicles.

key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Harvest early — at 4-5cm","details":"In warm zones harvest smaller than in cool zones (4-5cm diameter). The texture is better at smaller size and the window before becoming woody is narrower.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Succession sow every 3 weeks","details":"Stagger sowings for continuous supply through the dry season.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing brassica. Harvest when bulb (swollen stem) reaches 5-8cm — do not wait or it becomes woody and splits. Quicker to harvest than most brassicas.

key_activities: [{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest small and use as herb","details":"Do not expect commercial-sized celery in tropical conditions. Harvest young stalks and use as a fresh herb in cooking — the flavour is more intense and useful in small quantities.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Complete harvest by October","details":"Harvest all plants before monsoon rains begin. Wet season humidity and waterlogging kill celery within days.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow crop needing consistent moisture and cool but not cold conditions. Blanching by excluding light produces milder, less bitter stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Artichokes produce abundant foliage in zone 10. Monthly complete fertiliser (150g per plant) through the growing season keeps production going. Sulphate of potash applied at head development improves quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Artichokes produce abundant foliage in zone 10. Monthly complete fertiliser (150g per plant) through the growing season keeps production going. Sulphate of potash applied at head development improves quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"Artichokes produce abundant foliage in zone 10. Monthly complete fertiliser (150g per plant) through the growing season keeps production going. Sulphate of potash applied at head development improves quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Reduce water during summer dormancy","details":"In zone 10, artichokes go semi-dormant in summer. Cut back to 30cm stubs in January-February. Apply compost mulch. The plants re-shoot vigorously in autumn and produce the main crop in winter-spring.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser (4 of 4)","details":"Artichokes produce abundant foliage in zone 10. Monthly complete fertiliser (150g per plant) through the growing season keeps production going. Sulphate of potash applied at head development improves quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Check for artichoke aphid","details":"Artichoke aphid (Capitophorus elaeagni) can colonise developing buds in zone 10. Check buds when small (2-3cm). Apply pyrethrum spray or release parasitoid wasps. Aphid-infested heads are inedible.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest central then side buds","details":"Cut central buds first at 8-12cm, tight scales. In zone 10 the harvest runs July-November with excellent quality. Side buds are smaller but numerous — pick them at 5-7cm for the best flavour.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Remove side shoots from the root","details":"As the root swells, it produces small shoots (tillers) from its sides. Remove these monthly — they divert energy from root development. Reach into the base of the plant and snap them off.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":140,"activity":"Harvest when root reaches 8-12cm diameter","details":"Brush away soil to check root size. Celeriac roots store well in the ground in cool zones — can be left until needed through winter. Lift with a fork, trim leaves to 2-3cm above root.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season root vegetable. Takes 5-6 months from transplant. One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables — hard frosts improve flavour.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection — mandatory in zone 10a","details":"Cover with frost cloth when temperatures forecast below 5°C. Remove in the morning. Zone 10a winters can be marginal — the plant may not fruit in its expected timeframe in cold winters.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Select ratoon shoots for next crop","details":"After the main fruit forms and matures, the plant produces \"ratoons\" (side shoots from the base). Allow these to remain — each ratoon becomes the next fruiting plant. Remove all ratoons except the strongest 2-3.","category":"planting"},{"timing":548,"activity":"Harvest when base yellows and fragrance develops","details":"In zone 10, pineapple takes 18-24 months to fruit. Harvest when the base (bottom quarter) turns yellow-gold and the fruit develops a strong sweet aroma. Tap the side — a dull sound indicates full ripeness.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from crowns, ratoons or slips (not seedlings). Takes 18-24 months from crown to fruit in warm zones; up to 3 years in cool zones. Smooth Cayenne and Bethlehem are common varieties.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash 40g/m² at first flower and again at first fruit set. Zone 10 chillies can produce for 6-8 months from one planting. High potassium maintains this extended production.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest green or red at preference","details":"Harvest at any stage — green chillies are fresh and grassy; fully red are sweeter and hotter. Continuous picking extends production dramatically. Leave some to ripen fully for seed saving.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Overwinter in zone 10b","details":"In zone 10b, chilli plants can survive winter if cut back to 30cm and mulched heavily. They re-shoot in spring, producing a larger plant in year 2. This is the most productive approach for zone 10b gardens.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Warm-season crop that thrives in heat. Can be treated as a perennial in frost-free zones (10b-12). Extended ripening produces full colour and maximum heat.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Apply copper while leafless (June-July). Brown rot is the primary disease challenge in zone 10 — preventive spraying is essential.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune for airflow","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Prune after harvest in December-January. Open vase form. In zone 10, canopy airflow is the most important structural factor for brown rot prevention.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit — critical in warm zones","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Thin to 8-10cm spacing when fruitlets are 1-2cm. In zone 10 warm conditions, crowded fruit touching each other spreads brown rot rapidly before harvest.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when ripe","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). In zone 10, plums move from ripe to overripe very quickly. Monitor daily as harvest approaches (November-December). Harvest in the morning when fruit is cool. Brown rot can destroy an entire crop overnight in warm humid conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Japanese plums (Santa Rosa, Mariposa) have lower chill requirements than European (600-800 hrs). Most varieties need cross-pollination. Summer prune to avoid silver leaf disease.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply copper spray in winter — prevents brown rot","details":"Apply copper during the minimal dormancy period. In subtropical zones brown rot pressure is severe — chemical management is essential.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune for airflow","details":"Open canopy essential in zone 11a — airflow reduces brown rot which is the primary production challenge in subtropical conditions.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit aggressively","details":"In subtropical conditions crowded fruit is particularly vulnerable to brown rot. Thin to one fruit every 15cm minimum.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest early at 4–5cm","details":"In zone 11a harvest at first colour change — do not wait for full softness. Brown rot can destroy an entire crop within 48 hours in subtropical heat. Refrigerate immediately.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very marginal — Anzac or similar ultra-low chill varieties only
climate_note: Smooth-skinned peach variant with identical chill hour requirements. Brown rot at harvest is the main management challenge. Harvest timing is critical — nectarines do not improve after picking.

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Pinch out growing tip","details":"Pinch out the central stem tip to the first set of leaves as soon as the plant reaches 15cm. This forces bushy growth and delays flowering. A single pinch doubles leaf yield.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Check for aphids and fungal disease","details":"Cool humid conditions promote basil downy mildew (purple-grey fuzz on leaf undersides). Remove affected leaves. Improve airflow. Apply copper spray if severe. Avoid wetting foliage.","category":"pest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest before flowers open","details":"Harvest by cutting stems to just above a pair of leaves. In cool zones harvest frequently — the season is short. Remove flower buds the moment they appear to extend leaf production.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Frost-sensitive annual. Bolts in heat. Best in warm but not extreme conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin ruthlessly to 5cm spacing","details":"This is the step gardeners most often skip and most regret. Crowded carrots fork and stay small. Thin in two stages: first to 3cm at 3 weeks, then to 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check progress by brushing away soil","details":"Brush soil from the top of the root at 8-9 weeks. When the shoulder (top of root) reaches 1.5-2cm diameter, full-size roots are approaching maturity. Do not leave in the ground too long — oversize roots become woody.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest after cold for best flavour","details":"Cold temperatures convert carrot starch to sugar — autumn and winter carrots in cool zones are the sweetest. Pull by twisting and pulling steadily, or loosen soil with a fork first to avoid breaking roots.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply copper spray during minimal dormancy","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Apply copper during the brief semi-dormancy period (June-July). Leaf curl in warm zones can be severe — spray thoroughly.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Summer prune for maximum airflow. In zone 11a, brown rot management through canopy airflow is critical.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit aggressively","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). Any remaining fruit after natural drop should be thinned to 15cm+. Small crops in warm zones must be individually protected from brown rot.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest at first colour change — do not delay","details":"Adapted for zone 12b (Not suitable). In zone 11a, harvest promptly at first ripeness signs. Brown rot can destroy a ripe peach overnight in subtropical warmth. Refrigerate immediately after picking.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Like nectarine — requires winter chilling. Most productive and best flavour in zones with 500-1000 chill hours. Brown rot at harvest is the primary management challenge.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest very young — 8-10cm","details":"In zone 10, harvest rocket younger than in cool zones — at 8-10cm before heat intensifies the pepper. Young rocket is milder and more palatable.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":21,"activity":"Succession sow every 7-10 days","details":"In zone 10, the bolt-to-flower time is faster than in cool zones. Sow more frequently (every 7-10 days) to maintain continuous supply.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Fast-growing salad leaf. Bolts in heat producing very pungent, almost inedible leaves. Succession sow every 10-14 days. Wild rocket (Diplotaxis) is more heat-tolerant than common rocket (Eruca).

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune to control spread if needed","details":"Sea asparagus can spread via runners in moist conditions. Trim back with shears if it exceeds its intended area. The harvested tips are the most tender part — regular tip harvesting acts as pruning.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Harvest young shoot tips 3-5cm","details":"Snap or cut the bright green young shoot tips (the tips, not the thicker woody stems). Cook briefly (blanch or saute) or eat raw in salads. The salty flavour is intense and distinctive — a little goes a long way.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Tolerates cold — coastal and saline conditions preferred
climate_note: Australian coastal native (Sarcocornia/Tecticornia species). Extremely salt-tolerant. Crunchy, salty succulent shoots harvested as a vegetable. Almost no care required once established.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train vertically or provide 3–5m run space","details":"Winter squash vines spread extensively. Allow 3-5m per plant or erect a strong trellis and support developing fruit in mesh bags. Vertical growing produces cleaner fruit and is practical in cool zones with limited space.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser and potassium at fruit set","details":"Complete fertiliser at establishment. When fruit first sets (marble to golf-ball size), apply sulphate of potash at 50g/m². High potassium produces thick, hard skin essential for long storage.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Check fruit maturity with skin test","details":"Begin checking at 90 days. Press a fingernail firmly into the skin — it should resist completely without marking. Soft skin means the squash needs more time. In cool zones, harvest all squash before first frost even if skin test says incomplete.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest with long stem and cure thoroughly","details":"Cut with 10cm of stem — this is essential for storage. Cure in a warm (25-30°C) sunny position for 10-14 days. Curing hardens the skin and seals the stem scar, enabling 3-6 months storage in cool, dry, dark conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Short season — quick-maturing varieties (Butternut, Red Kuri); Start indoors 3-4 weeks before last frost
climate_note: Same principles as pumpkin. Harvest at full maturity with hard skin — unlike summer squash. Cures to 3-6 months storage. Needs bees for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone or urea at 100g/m² at knee height. Repeat at shoulder height. In tropical zones, rapid growth means both feeds may be needed within 3-4 weeks of each other.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest quickly in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat the milky stage passes even faster than in temperate zones. Once silks brown, check daily by piercing a kernel. Harvest at milky stage and refrigerate immediately — sugars convert to starch extremely rapidly in tropical heat.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Check for corn earworm","details":"Corn earworm (Helicoverpa armigera) is a major pest in subtropical and tropical zones. Apply Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) into the silk when it first emerges — before the husk closes. Repeat every 5 days until silks brown.","category":"pest"}]
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Lime trees produce prolifically in warm zones and can overcrowd the canopy. After the main harvest, remove crossing branches and thin the canopy to improve airflow. This reduces fungal disease and improves fruit in the following season.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting leaves or stems","details":"In warm zones Tahitian lime produces near-continuously. Harvest green for culinary use or allow to turn yellow for higher juice content. Fruit holds on the tree for several weeks — harvest as needed.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Least frost-tolerant common citrus. Tahitian (Persian) lime is the standard commercial variety. Kaffir lime grown for leaves. Both are essentially ever-bearing in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin seedlings to final spacing","details":"Thin at first true leaf. In zone 10, crowding accelerates bolting in warm autumn conditions.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Harvest small and young","details":"In zone 10, harvest turnips at 4-6cm diameter — slightly smaller than cool-zone equivalents. The window from \"ready\" to \"pithy and overgrown\" is shorter in warmer conditions.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Succession sow every 3 weeks","details":"Keep successive sowings going through the cool season. This prevents the \"harvest glut\" problem common with turnips and maintains steady supply of young, sweet roots.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast cool-season root crop. Harvest small (5-8cm) — older turnips become pithy and peppery. Leaves are also edible (turnip greens). Frost improves sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train new canes to trellis wires","details":"Tie new primocanes to the trellis as they grow through spring and summer. Summer-bearing varieties: these canes will fruit next year. Autumn/everbearing varieties: these canes will fruit at their tips in autumn of the same year.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest — critical annual task","details":"For summer varieties: immediately after harvest, cut all floricanes (the canes that fruited) to ground level. Tie the new primocanes neatly to the trellis. For autumn varieties: cut all canes to the ground in winter — they re-shoot and fruit on the new canes.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest every 2-3 days at peak season","details":"Ripe raspberries separate from the core (receptacle) cleanly, leaving behind the hollow cone shape. They are fragile — pick into shallow containers and refrigerate immediately. Harvest every 2-3 days to prevent waste from overripe fruit.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — Heritage and autumn-bearing varieties ideal
climate_note: Requires 600-900 chill hours. Fruits on second-year canes (summer varieties) or current-year canes (autumn/everbearing varieties). Post-harvest cane removal is the key annual task.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install winter frost protection — essential","details":"Frost kills mango trees under 3-4 years old outright. Cover completely with frost cloth below 4°C. Remove immediately when temperatures rise — heat under frost cloth is also damaging.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Reduce watering in winter — allow dry rest period","details":"Do not irrigate in June-August — the cool dry period triggers flowering. Premature flowering from an irrigated warm tree produces inferior small crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fruit colours and smells aromatic","details":"In zone 9b, mango may produce only in warm years. Fruit ripens November-January. Pick when the fruit colours up, has a sweet aroma and yields slightly to pressure at the tip.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Tropical/subtropical tree requiring a warm dry period to trigger flowering. Frost kills young trees. Most varieties need 8-10 weeks of cool/dry weather to induce flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"When corn reaches knee height (30-40cm), apply blood and bone at 100g/m² or pelleted nitrogen fertiliser alongside the row. This is the critical \"knee-high by holiday\" feed that drives cob development. Repeat at shoulder height.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"Never allow soil to dry at silking (when the silks emerge from the cob tips). Moisture stress at silking causes unfilled kernels — the single most common cause of poor corn. Daily watering if needed during silk emergence.","category":"watering"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check silk browning — harvest test","details":"When silk turns brown and dry, the cobs are approaching maturity. Pull back the husk and pierce a kernel — if milky liquid squirts out, harvest immediately. Clear liquid = too early; no liquid (doughy) = too late. The milky stage lasts only 2-3 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest at peak sweetness","details":"Pick at milky stage. Twist and pull downward to detach from the stem. In cool zones, boil or refrigerate within 30 minutes of harvest — sugars convert to starch rapidly after picking. Supersweet varieties are more forgiving.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Short season — quick-maturing varieties (Honey & Pearl); Start indoors 3-4 weeks before last frost
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting from 15cm height","details":"Cut back to 5-10cm when plants reach 20cm. In zone 10, this cycle repeats every 4-6 weeks year-round. Regular cutting is both harvest and maintenance — uncut mint becomes woody and aromatic oils concentrate in flowers rather than leaves.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Cut back hard twice yearly","details":"Cut the entire plant to 5cm in January and July. After cutting, apply a small amount of complete fertiliser and water in. New growth emerges in 10-14 days and is the most aromatic stage.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Check for rust disease","details":"Mint rust (orange powdery pustules on leaf undersides) is common in zone 10. Remove and bin (do not compost) affected stems. Apply a registered copper fungicide. Improve airflow by thinning dense growth. Persistent rust: replace with new healthy plants.","category":"pest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Divide plant","details":"Divide container plants annually — remove the pot, extract the root mass, divide and replant vigorous sections in fresh potting mix. This maintains productivity and prevents pot-binding.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Very vigorous — always grow in pots or contained beds
climate_note: Perennial spreading herb — grow in containers to prevent invasive spreading throughout the garden. Regrows from roots even after killing frost.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Mulch mounded rows","details":"Apply 8-10cm straw or sugar cane mulch over mounds. In zone 10, this retains moisture and moderates soil temperature through the summer growing season.","category":"planting"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Harvest when leaves begin to yellow","details":"In zone 10, harvest in February-April when vine leaves begin to yellow. Dig carefully with a fork. Cure in a warm dry shed for 10-14 days to develop sweetness and seal skin wounds.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good warm-season crop — October to March
climate_note: Grown from slips (vine cuttings), not true seedlings or seed. Needs 4-5 frost-free months minimum. Harvest triggers the development of sweetness — cure for 1-2 weeks after harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"When corn reaches knee height (30-40cm), apply blood and bone at 100g/m² or pelleted nitrogen fertiliser alongside the row. This is the critical \"knee-high by holiday\" feed that drives cob development. Repeat at shoulder height.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"Never allow soil to dry at silking (when the silks emerge from the cob tips). Moisture stress at silking causes unfilled kernels — the single most common cause of poor corn. Daily watering if needed during silk emergence.","category":"watering"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check silk browning — harvest test","details":"When silk turns brown and dry, the cobs are approaching maturity. Pull back the husk and pierce a kernel — if milky liquid squirts out, harvest immediately. Clear liquid = too early; no liquid (doughy) = too late. The milky stage lasts only 2-3 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest at peak sweetness","details":"Pick at milky stage. Twist and pull downward to detach from the stem. In cool zones, boil or refrigerate within 30 minutes of harvest — sugars convert to starch rapidly after picking. Supersweet varieties are more forgiving.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After fruit removal (August-September in cool zones; timing varies in tropical zones), remove crossing branches and any dead wood. Grapefruit does not need heavy pruning — mostly size management for access.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when skin colour develops","details":"Grapefruit turns yellow when mature. climate_note: Least cold-tolerant of commercial citrus. Requires warm nights to develop balanced acidity and sweetness. Self-fertile but large tree — allow 6m spacing.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Mulch root zone heavily","details":"Deep mulch (15cm) protects roots in cool zone winters. Figs are deciduous — they die back to woody structure in winter and re-shoot strongly in spring.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune in winter while leafless","details":"In winter, remove crossing branches, dead wood and any vigorous vertical growth (epicormic shoots). Remove some of the oldest branches each winter to stimulate new productive wood.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin breba crop in cool zones","details":"The early breba crop (on previous season wood) rarely ripens in cool zones — remove breba fruit in September to direct energy into the main crop which follows in late summer/autumn.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":800,"activity":"Harvest when skin softens and splits at neck","details":"Ripe figs droop from their attachment point, the skin softens and the neck may split slightly. Gently push against the base — if it yields it is ripe. In cool zones, ripening can be extended by placing a clear plastic bag over individual fruit clusters.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Extremely drought-tolerant once established. Two crops possible in warm zones: breba (on old wood, Nov) and main (on new wood, Jan-April). Most varieties are self-pollinating.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Blanch curds in zone 10","details":"Zone 10 sunshine is intense. Blanch the curd as soon as it reaches 3-4cm across by folding outer leaves over and securing. Check regularly — the curd can reach harvest size in as little as 2-3 weeks in mild warm conditions.","category":"planting"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Harvest when mature","details":"In zone 10 the transition from \"ready\" to \"overblown\" takes only days in warm spells. Check every second day once the head is blanched. Harvest when solid and white — before any separation of florets.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Blanch curds if growing coloured varieties in full sun
climate_note: More cold-sensitive than broccoli. The curd (head) must be blanched by tying outer leaves over it to prevent yellowing and bitterness in sunny conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply light fertiliser","details":"Very light application of blood and bone. In warm zones excess nitrogen dramatically increases bitterness.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":40,"activity":"Harvest young outer leaves — head may not form","details":"In subtropical zones a tight head may not develop. Harvest young individual outer leaves (less bitter than mature) as cut-and-come-again greens. This is a more realistic outcome than expecting a full tight head.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest any head that forms","details":"If a head does form, harvest immediately — warm conditions cause rapid deterioration and the head opens quickly into a loose, very bitter mass.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Italian chicory family. Frost reduces bitterness and tightens the head. Cut back to stump after first head harvest — radicchio regrows and produces again.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting outer leaves — cut-and-come-again","details":"Harvest outer leaves only. In zone 10 with year-round warmth, a single plant produces for 12+ months with cut-and-come-again management.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 3)","details":"Blood and bone at 80g/m² at planting. Monthly liquid fish emulsion maintains production. Zone 10 silverbeet grows vigorously — consistent feeding sustains this.","category":"fertilizing"}]
extra_care: Year-round — avoids only peak summer in hottest microclimates
climate_note: One of the most productive and adaptable vegetables. Cut-and-come-again: always harvest outer leaves only. More heat-tolerant than spinach.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 100g/m² after transplanting or thinning. Kale is a heavy feeder — nitrogen drives leaf production. extra_care: Best cool season crop — can be grown year round with management
climate_note: One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables. Frost dramatically improves sweetness. Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves only to extend production for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone or urea at 100g/m² at knee height. Repeat at shoulder height. In tropical zones, rapid growth means both feeds may be needed within 3-4 weeks of each other.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest quickly in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat the milky stage passes even faster than in temperate zones. Harvest at milky stage and refrigerate immediately — sugars convert to starch extremely rapidly in tropical heat.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Check for corn earworm","details":"Corn earworm (Helicoverpa armigera) is a major pest in subtropical and tropical zones. extra_care: Plant in dry season for best pollination
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":1095,"activity":"Prune lightly following harvest","details":"Prune immediately after harvest to maintain form. Remove dead wood and thin crowded branches. In zone 10, Davidson Plum can reach 6-8m — height management by selective pruning keeps the tree accessible for harvest.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1825,"activity":"Harvest deep purple berries — careful handling","details":"Ripe fruit is very soft and stains intensely. Harvest into buckets by hand — do not drop. Process immediately (freeze or cook) as fresh fruit deteriorates within 2-3 days. The fruit is too sour for fresh eating — cook or process.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian subtropical rainforest native. Takes 5-8 years to fruit from seed; 3-4 from cutting. Fruit is extremely sour (high vitamin C) — used in jams, sauces and beverages. Tolerates shade.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser","details":"One application of complete citrus fertiliser (including zinc and iron trace elements) in September. In cool zones, avoid late-season feeding that stimulates frost-vulnerable new growth flushes.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install winter frost protection — mandatory in zone 9","details":"Protect all bare-ground lime trees below 2°C with frost cloth. Remove protection during daylight.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune lightly following harvest","details":"Remove dead wood and crossing branches in spring after the coldest period. Avoid heavy pruning — lime trees in cool zones are slow to recover.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Harvest when green-yellow and aromatic","details":"Tahitian lime is technically ripe when yellow but is conventionally harvested green for market appearance. Test by squeezing — ripe lime yields slightly. In cool zones lime production is limited but quality is usually good.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Not suitable — lime is the least frost-tolerant common citrus
climate_note: Least frost-tolerant common citrus. Tahitian (Persian) lime is the standard commercial variety. Kaffir lime grown for leaves. Both are essentially ever-bearing in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train vertically or provide 3–5m run space","details":"Pumpkin vines spread 3-6m. If space is limited, train up a strong trellis and support developing fruit in mesh bags. In cool zones, allow 4-6m per plant in a warm sunny position.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser as side dressing","details":"Apply complete fertiliser at 100g/m² when plants are established and spreading. Test: push a fingernail into the skin — it should resist. Cure in a warm sunny position for 10-14 days before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Short season — choose quick-maturing varieties (Jarrahdale, Golden Nugget); Start indoors
climate_note: Large vining crop needing 4-6m space or vertical support. Pollination by bees essential — male flowers appear first. Store cured pumpkins in cool dry conditions for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser with trace elements","details":"Complete citrus fertiliser (with zinc, iron and manganese) in September. In cool zones one application per year is sufficient. Late-season feeding promotes frost-vulnerable soft growth.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection while young","details":"Protect young trees below -2°C with frost cloth. Established Navel oranges can tolerate brief periods to -4°C. Remove frost cloth during the day.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Remove dead wood and crossing branches after harvest. Do not prune heavily — oranges fruit on new season shoots and over-pruning reduces next season's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest by taste — colour not reliable in cool zones","details":"In cool zones, Washington Navels ripen May-August. Taste for sweetness and juice — in cool zones colour development can precede full flavour by several weeks. Orange holds on the tree for months without quality loss in cool conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool nights in winter are needed for the best flavour (sugar-acid balance). Valencia ripens later than Navel and is the best variety for warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Prune and space plants to maximise airflow","details":"Plant in open, well-ventilated positions. In subtropical zones even dry season humidity promotes powdery mildew. Avoid enclosed beds.","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Preventive sulfur spray from 40 days","details":"Apply sulfur-based fungicide from 40 days as a preventive measure in subtropical and tropical zones. Powdery mildew appears earlier and spreads faster in warm conditions.","category":"pest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest daily in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat, zucchini grows even faster than in temperate zones. Harvest every day or two. A missed harvest in tropical heat produces an enormous marrow within 72 hours.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest by cutting stems to 10cm","details":"Cut stems back to 10cm when the plant reaches 20cm. In cool zones, harvest runs from spring through autumn — the plant dies back in winter.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back hard before or at first flowering","details":"When flower buds form, the essential oil in leaves is at its peak. Harvest heavily at this point — cut the whole plant back to 10cm. Dry the harvest in a warm airy place. The essential oil content is highest just before full flowering.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch roots lightly for winter in zone 8","details":"After the plant dies back to the ground in zone 8 winters, apply a light mulch of gravel or coarse sand over the crown. climate_note: Mediterranean perennial. Thrives on neglect — poor, dry soil produces the most aromatic leaves. Do not overwater or over-fertilise.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply protective fungicide at petal fall","details":"Brown rot (Monilinia) is the primary disease threat in warmer zones. extra_care: Brown rot pressure high in humid areas — spray at petal fall
climate_note: Requires 300-900 chill hours. Flowers early — frost damage to blossom is the main risk in cool zones. Insufficient chill hours in zones 11b+.

key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Begin rinsing and draining twice daily for 7 days","details":"Rinse with cool water through the mesh twice daily (morning and evening). Shake gently and drain completely — standing water causes mould. Keep at 18-22°C. Continue twice-daily rinsing.","category":"planting"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at 4-6cm before roots develop extensively","details":"Harvest when sprouts are 4-6cm and the first true leaves are emerging. Rinse a final time, drain well and refrigerate. Use within 3 days.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Indoor crop — grown in a jar or tray, not the garden. Not zone-dependent. The same process applies in all climates.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin to 5-8cm spacing","details":"Thin twice: 3cm at 3 weeks, 5-8cm at 5 weeks. Thinning is the most important and most skipped step. Crowded roots divide and stay small regardless of other management.","category":"planting"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Check root size and quality","details":"Brush soil from shoulder — 1.5cm+ shoulder diameter indicates approaching maturity. Warmer zone carrots mature faster but are less sweet than cool zone equivalents.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest at optimum size","details":"Zone 10 carrots should be harvested at 18-22cm length. Do not leave in the ground through summer — heat makes roots woody and bitter. Pull in the cool of the morning.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Avoid midsummer sowing — roots fork in heat
climate_note: Direct sow — resent transplanting. Deep, loose, stone-free soil essential. Cold improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar).

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Tropical soils drain quickly.
