Fortnightly liquid feeding is more effective than granular slow-release in hot, freely-draining tropical conditions.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest frequently — complete by October","details":"Harvest every 1-2 days. extra_care: Dry season production — web under leaf in dry conditions
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Highly productive but affected by powdery mildew. Male and female flowers separate — pollination by bees essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back in summer heat","details":"In zone 11 summer, cut back to 30cm stubs to prevent heat exhaustion of the plant. extra_care: Productive but requires cutting back in summer heat
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply fertiliser after harvest","details":"Apply low-phosphorus complete fertiliser with trace elements in two applications: after harvest (February-March) and before flowering (August-September). Colour varies by variety. Pick individual fruit when the shoulder drops and the tip yields to gentle pressure. Harvest over 4-6 weeks as fruit matures.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Tropical/subtropical tree requiring a warm dry period to trigger flowering. Frost kills young trees. Most varieties need 8-10 weeks of cool/dry weather to induce flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Copper spray while leafless to control fungal diseases including pear scab. climate_note: Requires more chill hours than apple (600-1500+ hours depending on variety). Needs a cross-pollination partner. Pears are picked hard (before soft) and ripened off the tree — unlike most fruit.

key_activities: [{"timing":50,"activity":"Check laterals for disease","details":"Remove laterals on indeterminate varieties. climate_note: Same principles as pumpkin. Harvest at full maturity with hard skin — unlike summer squash. Cures to 3-6 months storage. Needs bees for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Remove all flower stalks","details":"Any energy going to flowering reduces the already-limited stalk production. extra_care: Very limited — plants rarely thrive or produce usable stalks
climate_note: Requires cold winters for dormancy and vigorous regrowth. The colder the winter, the better the rhubarb. Only harvest stems — leaves are toxic (contain oxalic acid). Do not harvest in year 1.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Provide afternoon shade if possible","details":"In subtropical zones, afternoon shade during the coolest months slightly extends the pod-setting window. Sow on the south side of taller crops.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply light fertiliser","details":"Light application of balanced fertiliser at sowing only. Plants in subtropical zones have a short season — heavy feeding is unnecessary and can promote leafy growth over pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Pinch tips when pods appear","details":"Black bean aphid colonises rapidly in subtropical warmth. Pinch growing tips as soon as lowest pods form. Apply neem oil spray if aphid colonies appear.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest early at 4–5cm","details":"Harvest begins September-October in zone 11a. key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Erect support stakes","details":"Tall varieties (Aquadulce) reach 1.2m and fall over in wind and rain. Do not wait until the pod turns black — beans become starchy. Double-pod varieties: harvest outer pods first. Pick from the bottom up.","category":"harvest"}]

In cool zones, harvest all squash before first frost even if skin test says incomplete.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest with long stem and cure thoroughly","details":"Cut with 10cm of stem — this is essential for storage. Cure in a warm (25-30°C) sunny position for 10-14 days. Curing hardens the skin and seals the stem scar, enabling 3-6 months storage in cool, dry, dark conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Start indoors 3 weeks before last frost
climate_note: Same principles as pumpkin. Harvest at full maturity with hard skin — unlike summer squash. Cures to 3-6 months storage. Needs bees for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Mulch heavily — soil warmth is critical","details":"Apply black plastic mulch (plant through holes) or 10cm of straw mulch over the mounds. Soil warmth drives sweet potato growth — cool soils massively reduce yield. Black plastic mulch raises soil temperature by 3-5°C.","category":"planting"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Harvest before first frost","details":"Dig carefully with a fork before first autumn frost. In cool zones the tubers will be smaller than in tropical zones but perfectly good quality. Cure in a warm (25-30°C) humid position for 10-14 days — this converts starches to sugars and heals any wounds in the skin.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Grown from slips (vine cuttings), not true seedlings or seed. Needs 4-5 frost-free months minimum. Harvest triggers the development of sweetness — cure for 1-2 weeks after harvest.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Blood and bone at 100g/m² after transplanting or thinning. Kale is a heavy feeder — nitrogen drives leaf production. Repeat every 4-6 weeks for continuous production.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Begin cut-and-come-again harvest","details":"Harvest outer leaves only — always leave at least 4-6 central leaves. Kale harvested this way from one planting can produce for 6-12 months in cool zones. Younger, smaller leaves are most tender.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Check for caterpillars and aphids","details":"Cabbage white butterfly caterpillars and grey cabbage aphid are the primary pests. Bt spray for caterpillars, forceful water spray for aphids. Fine insect mesh (exclusion netting) eliminates both without spraying.","category":"pest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest young leaves for best flavour","details":"Young kale leaves (20-30cm) have the best flavour. After frost, taste older leaves — they will have sweetened significantly. Harvest large leaves for cooking, young leaves for salads.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables. Frost dramatically improves sweetness. Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves only to extend production for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 30cm spacing","details":"Thin at 3-4 true leaves. Apply liquid fertiliser after thinning.","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Blanch for 10 days","details":"Blanching is even more important in zone 10 than cool zones — heat increases baseline bitterness. 10 days under cover or with tied leaves significantly improves palatability.","category":"planting"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest when ready","details":"In zone 10, endive overmatured by only 1-2 weeks becomes very bitter. Harvest when the centre is pale and well-blanched regardless of overall head size.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Avoid summer — heat causes intense bitterness
climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Blanching (excluding light for 10-14 days before harvest) is essential to reduce natural bitterness.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin when seedlings have 3-4 true leaves. In cool conditions, coriander can be grown at 5cm spacing for leaf harvest. Thinnings are edible.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Succession sow every 2-3 weeks","details":"A single coriander sowing in cool conditions may produce for only 3-4 weeks before bolting. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.","category":"planting"},{"timing":21,"activity":"Harvest leaves before flower stalk emerges","details":"Cut leaves regularly from young plants. The moment a central flower stalk begins to rise, leaf quality drops. Harvest the entire plant at this point — stems and leaves are still edible.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":40,"activity":"Leave some plants to flower and set seed","details":"Leave one or two plants to bolt and produce seed (coriander seeds are a spice in themselves). Once seed turns brown, cut the whole stem and dry in a paper bag to collect seeds for cooking or next sowing.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Notoriously bolt-prone. Direct sow — resents transplanting. Keep cool and harvest before flower stalks emerge. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Support climbing varieties","details":"Erect 2m trellis or individual stakes before sowing. Train stems upward from 20cm height. Climbing varieties in zone 10 can produce for 8-10 weeks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Side-dress with potassium","details":"Apply sulphate of potash at 20g/m² when plants begin to flower. Beans fix nitrogen — supplemental nitrogen causes foliage at the expense of pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Pick at snap stage","details":"Harvest when pods are 10-15cm, bright green and snap cleanly. Pick every 2 days to maximise production. Beans left to mature on the plant signal the plant to stop producing.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — beans resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation.

key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin seedlings to final spacing","details":"Thin at first true leaf. In zone 10, crowding accelerates bolting in warm autumn conditions.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Harvest small and young","details":"In zone 10, harvest turnips at 4-6cm diameter — slightly smaller than cool-zone equivalents. The window from \"ready\" to \"pithy and overgrown\" is shorter in warmer conditions.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Succession sow every 3 weeks","details":"Keep successive sowings going through the cool season. This prevents the \"harvest glut\" problem common with turnips and maintains steady supply of young, sweet roots.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fast cool-season root crop. Harvest small (5-8cm) — older turnips become pithy and peppery. Leaves are also edible (turnip greens). Frost improves sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² when first flower buds appear. In cool zones feed every 3 weeks to maximise the short growing season. Stake early — fruiting plants topple in wind.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Pick green to stimulate production","details":"In cool zones the season is short. Harvest some fruit green to stimulate continued flowering rather than waiting for all fruit to ripen red. Each fruit left to ripen red on a cool-zone plant delays the production of several more fruits.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest all before frost","details":"Remove all remaining fruit before first autumn frost. Green peppers ripen to red if kept warm indoors. Do not compost plants without removing all fruit.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Grow in heated greenhouse only — outdoor season too short
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Requires warmth to germinate and fruit. Capsicum and Peppers are the same species (Capsicum annuum) — treated identically.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train new canes","details":"Guide new growth to trellis. Zone 10 can produce strong cane growth — train horizontal or fan-shaped to maximise sun exposure and airflow.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest","details":"Cut all fruited canes (floricanes) immediately after harvest. Tie new canes to trellis. Apply compost and potassium dressing. This renovation is the foundation of next season's crop.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest in warm season","details":"In zone 10 blackberries ripen November-January. Pick every 1-2 days — fruit softens quickly in warmth. Pick in early morning before heat of the day.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Adequate chill hours in most winters
climate_note: Requires 200-700 chill hours. Grown from canes or root divisions, not seedlings. Fruits on second-year canes (floricanes).

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Tip-prune following harvest completion","details":"After berry harvest, tip-prune by 30% to encourage bushy, productive growth for the following season. The shrub can be cut back harder (50%) every 3-4 years to rejuvenate it.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest after natural drying on the plant","details":"In warm zones Akudjura berries ripen and dry quickly on the plant. Harvest when fully shrivelled and brown. The caramel-tamarillo flavour is most intense in fully dried berries. Use as a ground spice in marinades, sauces and bread.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian native desert shrub (Solanum centrale). Extremely drought-tolerant. Berries are dried and used as a spice with caramel-tamarillo flavour. Dislikes wet soils.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Very marginal — Asian pear types may perform better). Apply copper while leafless. Pear scab management is important even in zone 10.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a minimal winter prune","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Very marginal — Asian pear types may perform better). Low-chill pears in zone 10 grow less vigorously than in cool zones. Prune conservatively — remove crossing branches and dead wood only in years 1-4, then moderate spur thinning from year 5.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin lightly","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Very marginal — Asian pear types may perform better). Thin to one fruit per cluster. Low-chill varieties in zone 10 may set less fruit than in cool zones — thin conservatively.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Pick firm and ripen off tree","details":"Adapted for zone 10b (Very marginal — Asian pear types may perform better). Same principle as cool zones — pick firm and ripen at room temperature. Nashi (Asian pear) is an exception — it is eaten crunchy, directly from the tree.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very marginal — Asian pear types may perform better
climate_note: Requires more chill hours than apple (600-1500+ hours depending on variety). Needs a cross-pollination partner. Pears are picked hard (before soft) and ripened off the tree — unlike most fruit.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Remove flowers in the first season","details":"For spring-planted runners, remove all flowers in the first season — this redirects energy into root and crown development and significantly improves the following year's yield. For autumn-planted runners in cool zones, allow first-year flowering.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply straw mulch at fruit set","details":"When flowers appear in spring, lay straw mulch around and under the developing fruit. This keeps fruit off the soil (preventing rot and soil splash), deters slugs, and retains moisture.","category":"planting"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Net before colour develops","details":"Birds take strawberries the moment any red colour appears. Net the bed completely before the first fruit shows colour — after is too late.","category":"pest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Harvest daily when ripe — slug and snail monitoring","details":"Harvest fully red fruit daily. Check under straw and leaves daily for slug and snail damage — they cause clean semicircular bites in fruit. Apply iron-based slug pellets around the bed perimeter.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Excellent zone — mulch crowns for winter; Sequoia, Pajaro, Red Gauntlet varieties
climate_note: Grown from runners (not seed). Plant crowns in autumn, harvest spring. Replace plants every 2-3 years — older plants have lower yield. Protect from birds and slugs at fruit set.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest in dry season — flavour is best","details":"In subtropical zones, dry season oregano has the best essential oil content. Harvest freely in April-October. Wet season growth is lush but low in flavour compounds.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Hard prune","details":"Cut back to 10cm at the start of the wet season (October-November). This reduces the amount of soft growth susceptible to fungal disease in wet season humidity.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Replace plant","details":"In subtropical zones oregano is shorter-lived than in cool zones due to wet season stress. Replace with fresh plants or cuttings every 2-3 years.","category":"planting"}]
extra_care: Grows well but reduced essential oil intensity in subtropical humidity
climate_note: Mediterranean perennial. Thrives on neglect — poor, dry soil produces the most aromatic leaves. Do not overwater or over-fertilise.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Stop nitrogen — switch to potassium","details":"When bulbs begin to swell (visible at the soil surface), stop nitrogen fertilising and apply sulphate of potash (40g/m²). This is the critical transition — nitrogen at this stage produces soft necks with poor storage life.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Stop watering when tops begin to fall","details":"When 50-70% of tops have flopped over, stop all watering. This triggers neck curing. Premature watering at this stage causes soft-necked onions that store poorly and rot within weeks.","category":"watering"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest and cure in dry conditions","details":"Lift onions when tops are fully fallen and yellowed. Lay in a single layer in a dry, airy location for 3-4 weeks. In cool zones, a dry shed or under cover is ideal. Cure until the necks are completely dry before storage.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Remove flower stalks","details":"Rhubarb occasionally sends up a flower stalk (thick round stem with seed head). Remove it immediately at ground level — it diverts energy from leaf stalks and signals the plant to stop producing.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting — pull, do not cut","details":"In spring of year 2 (August-October), harvest stalks by gripping at the base and pulling with a twisting motion. Never cut — cutting leaves a stub that can rot into the crown. Take no more than 1/3 of the stalks at any time. Stop harvesting by November to allow the plant to rebuild. Scheduled from approximately year 2 after planting.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires cold winters for dormancy and vigorous regrowth. The colder the winter, the better the rhubarb. Only harvest stems — leaves are toxic (contain oxalic acid). Do not harvest in year 1.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Support climbing varieties","details":"Erect 2m trellis or individual stakes before sowing. Train stems upward from 20cm height. Climbing varieties in zone 10 can produce for 8-10 weeks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Side-dress with potassium","details":"Apply sulphate of potash at 20g/m² when plants begin to flower. Beans fix nitrogen — supplemental nitrogen causes foliage at the expense of pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Pick at snap stage","details":"Harvest when pods are 10-15cm, bright green and snap cleanly. Pick every 2 days to maximise production. Beans left to mature on the plant signal the plant to stop producing.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Direct sow — beans resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation.

key_activities: [{"timing":150,"activity":"Stop watering and fertilising","details":"When approximately half the leaves have yellowed, stop all watering and fertilising. This triggers the final bulb curing process. Premature watering at this stage causes soft, poorly-wrapped bulbs that store poorly.","category":"watering"},{"timing":210,"activity":"Harvest when tops are 50% fallen","details":"Harvest when half the leaves have yellowed and fallen. Do not wait until all leaves die — the outer wrapper splits and bulbs deteriorate. Lift with a fork, not by pulling leaves. Cure in a dry, airy shed for 3-4 weeks before storing or using.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Plant April-May — cold winters trigger excellent bulb formation; Excellent zone
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² at first flower. Okra is a moderate feeder — heavy nitrogen produces lush foliage at the expense of pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days — mandatory","details":"Okra pods become fibrous and inedible within 2-3 days of reaching 5-8cm. In cool zones harvest every 2 days without fail. Wear gloves — okra spines cause skin irritation. Cut with scissors, not pulling.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Remove old pods to maintain production","details":"Any pod allowed to mature beyond harvestable size signals the plant to slow production. Remove all pods including any missed oversize ones to maintain flowering.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Heat-loving tropical vegetable. Harvest pods at 5-8cm — older pods become fibrous and tough within 2-3 days of reaching harvestable size.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Switch to potassium at bulbing","details":"When bulbs are visibly swelling, stop nitrogen and apply sulphate of potash (30g/m²). This firms the bulb layers and improves storage quality and flavour.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Stop watering when tops yellow","details":"Stop all irrigation when 50-60% of tops have yellowed and flopped. This triggers the final curing of the neck — premature watering at this point causes soft-necked bulbs with poor storage life.","category":"watering"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest and cure — 3-4 weeks","details":"Lift when tops are fully yellowed. Lay in a dry, airy shed for 3-4 weeks. Separate the bulb clusters once tops are fully dry. In cool zones, shallots store for 6-12 months in cool, dry, dark conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted from individual bulbs — each divides into a cluster of 4-8 new bulbs at harvest. Same day-length sensitivity as onions. Cure thoroughly before storage.

key_activities: [{"timing":25,"activity":"Harvest as micro-greens or very young","details":"In warm zones harvest spinach as micro-greens (7-10cm) for the best quality. The heat-to-bolt progression is rapid — very young harvest is the only reliable approach.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very limited — consider silverbeet/warrigal greens as alternatives
climate_note: Most bolt-prone cool-season vegetable. Bolts within days of temperatures exceeding 20°C. Asian (Malabar) spinach is an excellent heat-tolerant substitute in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Begin harvesting","details":"In zone 10, harvest year-round. Flavour is most intense in late spring before flowering and in summer dry conditions when essential oils concentrate.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Hard prune twice yearly","details":"Cut back by 40-50% in August (before summer) and March (after summer). Zone 10 thyme can become a woody mound rapidly without regular cutting.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Replace plant from cuttings","details":"Take spring cuttings from 8cm new growth. Strip lower leaves and insert into coarse sand. Roots form in 3-4 weeks. Replace parent plant every 4 years.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial. Thrives in poor, dry, well-drained conditions. Like oregano — rich soil and overwatering reduce flavour and shorten plant life.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Check for Asian citrus psyllid and leafminer","details":"Citrus leafminer (silvery serpentine trails in new leaves) is prevalent in warm zones. Apply horticultural oil sprays to new growth flushes. Asian citrus psyllid must be reported immediately — it is a regulated pest.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after flush to manage size","details":"Lemon trees in subtropical and tropical zones grow vigorously. Annual pruning after the main crop maintains accessible height (3-4m). Remove crossing branches and thin dense canopy for airflow.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting as needed","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, lemons (especially Eureka) produce near continuously. Harvest ripe fruit promptly — in tropical conditions fruit left on the tree deteriorates faster than in cool zones.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very productive — monitor for citrus leafminer
climate_note: Most widely grown backyard citrus. Eureka and Lisbon varieties are nearly ever-bearing — fruit year-round in warm zones. Meyer lemon is a hybrid with softer acidity and more cold-tolerance.

key_activities: [{"timing":40,"activity":"Check head development in cool weather","details":"Zone 10 radicchio is best in the cooler months (May-August). The characteristic red colouration and tight head development are triggered by cold — warmer conditions in early and late autumn produce looser, more bitter results.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest when head is firm and well-coloured","details":"Cut the whole head when compact and firm. The red-white marbling is a quality indicator — it intensifies with cold exposure.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut to stump for second crop","details":"As in cool zones, cut to a stump after main head harvest. Second growth in zone 10 is produced through the cooler months (July-August).","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Italian chicory family. Frost reduces bitterness and tightens the head. Cut back to stump after first head harvest — radicchio regrows and produces again.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Install supports for climbing varieties","details":"Erect 2m stakes or a trellis before plants need it. Climbing beans crop longer than bush types — worthwhile in the short growing seasons of cool zones. Direct tendrils onto the support.","category":"planting"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Use low-nitrogen fertiliser only","details":"Beans fix their own nitrogen. Apply potassium (sulphate of potash) and phosphorus only — excess nitrogen produces lush foliage and poor pod set.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Harvest while pods are slim","details":"Pick when pods snap cleanly (before seeds bulge). In cool zones harvest every 2-3 days — pods left too long reduce further production. Picking encourages continued flowering.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Inoculate seed with rhizobium before sowing
climate_note: Direct sow — beans resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium for nitrogen fixation.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"When corn reaches knee height (30-40cm), apply blood and bone at 100g/m² or pelleted nitrogen fertiliser alongside the row. This is the critical \"knee-high by holiday\" feed that drives cob development. Repeat at shoulder height.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"Never allow soil to dry at silking (when the silks emerge from the cob tips). Moisture stress at silking causes unfilled kernels — the single most common cause of poor corn. Daily watering if needed during silk emergence.","category":"watering"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Check silk browning — harvest test","details":"When silk turns brown and dry, the cobs are approaching maturity. Pull back the husk and pierce a kernel — if milky liquid squirts out, harvest immediately. Clear liquid = too early; no liquid (doughy) = too late. The milky stage lasts only 2-3 days.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":75,"activity":"Harvest at peak sweetness","details":"Pick at milky stage. Twist and pull downward to detach from the stem. In cool zones, boil or refrigerate within 30 minutes of harvest — sugars convert to starch rapidly after picking. Supersweet varieties are more forgiving.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train vertically and pinch laterals","details":"Train main stem up the trellis. Lateral (side) shoots: pinch out at 2 leaves each. This concentrates production on the main stem and improves airflow critically important for preventing powdery mildew which is near-universal in zone 10 by midsummer.","category":"planting"},{"timing":35,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser and potassium (1 of 4)","details":"Cucumbers in zone 10 are heavy feeders over their 8-10 week production peak. Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser plus potassium topdress every 4-5 weeks.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":49,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser and potassium (2 of 4)","details":"Cucumbers in zone 10 are heavy feeders over their 8-10 week production peak. Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser plus potassium topdress every 4-5 weeks.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest every 1-2 days","details":"Cucumbers grow 2-5cm per day in zone 10 warmth. Harvest every day or two. Remove any yellowing fruit immediately — it signals the plant to wind down production.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":63,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser and potassium (3 of 4)","details":"Cucumbers in zone 10 are heavy feeders over their 8-10 week production peak. Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser plus potassium topdress every 4-5 weeks.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":77,"activity":"Apply complete fertiliser and potassium (4 of 4)","details":"Cucumbers in zone 10 are heavy feeders over their 8-10 week production peak. Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser plus potassium topdress every 4-5 weeks.","category":"fertilizing"}]
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Highly productive but affected by powdery mildew. Male and female flowers separate — pollination by bees essential.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a winter structural prune","details":"Remove crossing branches and deadwood. Select 3-5 main scaffold branches. In zone 10, figs can become large — manage height to 3-4m by removing dominant leaders. Apply sulphate of potash (60g per tree) in late winter to promote fruit development.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":600,"activity":"Leave breba fruit on plant","details":"In zone 10, the early breba crop (November) can partially ripen. Leave it on the tree. The main crop follows in February-April and is substantially larger.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":800,"activity":"Harvest in morning before fruit softens","details":"Ripe figs are fragile — pick in the cool of the morning. In zone 10, figs ripen from February-April. A large established tree can produce 50+ kg. Process excess into jam or dry in the sun.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Two crops per year possible (breba in Nov + main crop Feb-April)
climate_note: Extremely drought-tolerant once established. Two crops possible in warm zones: breba (on old wood, Nov) and main (on new wood, Jan-April). Most varieties are self-pollinating.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Apply liquid complete fertiliser every 2 weeks. In warm soils, granular slow-release leaches too quickly. Steady nutrition is critical for any head formation in tropical zones.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (2 of 4)","details":"Apply liquid complete fertiliser every 2 weeks. In warm soils, granular slow-release leaches too quickly. Steady nutrition is critical for any head formation in tropical zones.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Net for insect control","details":"Multiple caterpillar species attack cauliflower in warm climates. Install fine insect mesh at transplant. Check under netting weekly.","category":"pest"},{"timing":42,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (3 of 4)","details":"Apply liquid complete fertiliser every 2 weeks. In warm soils, granular slow-release leaches too quickly. Steady nutrition is critical for any head formation in tropical zones.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Blanch early","details":"In subtropical and tropical conditions, blanch the curd as soon as it appears — sunlight exposure is more intense and rapid discolouration occurs quickly. Secure outer leaves firmly.","category":"planting"},{"timing":56,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (4 of 4)","details":"Apply liquid complete fertiliser every 2 weeks. In warm soils, granular slow-release leaches too quickly. Steady nutrition is critical for any head formation in tropical zones.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":65,"activity":"Harvest at any size","details":"Do not wait for full cauliflower size in warm zones — curds develop quickly then rapidly deteriorate. Harvest when solid regardless of size. Season ends before wet season onset.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cool season only — harvest window very short before warmth causes premature flowering
climate_note: More cold-sensitive than broccoli. The curd (head) must be blanched by tying outer leaves over it to prevent yellowing and bitterness in sunny conditions.

key_activities: [{"timing":35,"activity":"Calcium-rich soil amendment and potassium at first flower","details":"Apply dolomite lime (100g per plant) around the drip zone to prevent blossom end rot (calcium deficiency). At first flower, apply sulphate of potash (60g per plant). Consistent calcium and potassium are the two most important nutrients for fruit quality.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":50,"activity":"Remove laterals (side shoots) on indeterminate varieties","details":"For tall/indeterminate varieties: remove all side shoots (laterals) growing in the \"armpit\" between the main stem and a leaf. This keeps the plant to a single stem with maximum fruit size. Bush/determinate varieties: do not remove laterals — they are the fruiting structure.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured and aromatic","details":"Harvest when fully coloured and just yielding to gentle pressure. In cool zones, the season is short — harvest promptly. Green tomatoes picked before frost ripen well on a sunny windowsill. Do not refrigerate tomatoes — it destroys the flavour compounds.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Start indoors September-October for November transplant
climate_note: Stop setting fruit when night temperatures exceed 30°C or drop below 10°C. Consistent watering prevents blossom end rot and fruit cracking.

key_activities: [{"timing":7,"activity":"Thin to 5cm spacing","details":"Thin at 2 true leaves. In zone 10 warm soil, thinning delay causes crowded, forked roots faster than in cool zones.","category":"planting"},{"timing":14,"activity":"Water at pod fill","details":"In zone 10 cool months, dry spells can cause cracking. Water every 2 days in dry weather. Mulch between rows.","category":"watering"},{"timing":22,"activity":"Check from 18 days in zone 10","details":"Zone 10 radish matures faster than cool-zone equivalents. Start checking root size at 18 days. Harvest at 2-3cm before pithy deterioration which comes quickly in warm conditions.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Harvest entire row at once if warm spell approaches","details":"If a warm spell is forecast, harvest all remaining radish regardless of size. A 2-day heat wave can make an entire sowing pithy and unusable.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Fastest vegetable in the garden (25-35 days). Bolts and becomes hot/woody in heat. Harvest promptly at correct size — even 3-4 days too late produces pithy, harsh radish.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Install supports for climbing varieties","details":"Erect 2m stakes or a trellis before plants need it. extra_care: Inoculate seed with rhizobium before sowing

key_activities: [{"timing":70,"activity":"Blanch for mild flavour","details":"Wrap stems in cardboard or newspaper 2 weeks before harvest. Check for slugs and snails under wrapping — they shelter in the dark warm space.","category":"planting"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest by August","details":"In zone 10, harvest celery before spring warming — heat makes stalks pithy and bitter. climate_note: Slow crop needing consistent moisture and cool but not cold conditions. Blanching by excluding light produces milder, less bitter stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply citrus fertiliser with trace elements","details":"Complete citrus fertiliser (with zinc, iron and manganese) in September. key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Check for aphids — repeat weekly for 4 weeks","details":"In zone 10, green peach aphid colonises lettuce heads. Check centres of developing heads weekly. key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Trim to manage spread","details":"In warm zones sea asparagus spreads vigorously. Trim annually to keep within bounds. key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Begin rinsing and draining twice daily for 7 days","details":"Rinse with cool water through the mesh twice daily (morning and evening). key_activities: [{"timing":10,"activity":"Thin seedlings to final spacing","details":"Thin to 8-10cm. key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Check for powdery mildew — treat if needed","details":"Powdery mildew is universal on zone 10 zucchini by midsummer. Apply sulfur spray at first signs. Remove badly affected leaves. The plant typically outlasts mildew for 4-6 weeks if managed.","category":"pest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days without exception","details":"In zone 10 warmth, zucchini grows 3-5cm per day. climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune lightly after harvest","details":"Remove dead wood, crossing branches and any water shoots growing vertically from main scaffold branches. climate_note: Most frost-tolerant citrus. Compact tree suitable for container growing. Self-fruitful. Fruit is eaten whole — skin is sweet, flesh is tart.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply fertiliser","details":"Complete fertiliser with high nitrogen at transplant. Side-dress every 3 weeks through the cool months. extra_care: Avoid warm springs — sprouts button prematurely
climate_note: Slow-growing brassica. Flavour significantly improves after frost. Firm planting prevents wind rock which causes loose sprouts.

key_activities: [{"timing":50,"activity":"Check laterals for disease","details":"Remove laterals on indeterminate varieties. extra_care: Dry season planting for fruit fly management
climate_note: Stop setting fruit when night temperatures exceed 30°C or drop below 10°C. Consistent watering prevents blossom end rot and fruit cracking.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Thin to 25-30cm spacing","details":"Thin promptly — endive needs space to form a full head. Thinnings are edible (young endive leaves are tender and less bitter than mature).","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Blanch before harvest","details":"10-14 days before harvest, tie the outer leaves loosely over the head with a rubber band, or cover with an upturned pot or plate. climate_note: Cool-season salad crop. Blanching (excluding light for 10-14 days before harvest) is essential to reduce natural bitterness.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply mango-specific fertiliser","details":"Use a low-phosphorus complete fertiliser with trace elements. Apply in October after the flowering period and again in February. In zone 10, a third application in June-July when growth resumes.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Withhold water June-August to trigger flowering","details":"In zone 10, the cool-dry period naturally reduces rainfall. Supplement this by withholding irrigation in June-August. This water and temperature stress triggers the flower induction that produces the following season's crop.","category":"watering"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Tip-prune after harvest for compact form","details":"After harvest, lightly tip-prune the new growth to maintain a compact tree. This improves the light environment within the canopy and manages tree size for easier netting.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when stalk end of fruit colours","details":"Kensington Pride yellows at the stem end when ripe. R2E2 and Calypso develop red blush. Pick when slightly soft at the tip and aroma is sweet and tropical. Zone 10 mango harvest: November-February.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Tropical/subtropical tree requiring a warm dry period to trigger flowering. Frost kills young trees. Most varieties need 8-10 weeks of cool/dry weather to induce flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Apply potassium at bulbing","details":"As bulbs start to swell (visible above the soil), apply sulphate of potash at 30g/m². Stop all nitrogen. In warm zones this transition comes earlier than in cool zones.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":130,"activity":"Reduce watering as tops yellow","details":"Reduce then stop watering as tops yellow and begin to fall. The warm dry season climate in subtropical zones assists natural curing.","category":"watering"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest and store in warm dry conditions","details":"In tropical zones, bulbs left in the ground after tops fall deteriorate rapidly. Harvest promptly. Cure in a warm, well-ventilated covered area for 2 weeks. Shelf life is shorter in warm humid zones than in cool-zone equivalents.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Day-length sensitive. Long-day varieties suit cool zones (plant autumn, harvest summer); short-day varieties suit warm zones. Stop watering when tops fall over for proper curing.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Earth up as plants grow","details":"As leeks grow, mound soil progressively around the shaft every 3-4 weeks. This extends the length of the blanched white portion. In cool zones leeks can be earthed up 3-4 times through their growing season. Each earthing up must cover all previously exposed green growth.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Check shaft thickness","details":"Leeks are harvestable from 1.5cm shaft diameter but best at 2.5-4cm. In cool zones they hold well in the ground through winter — harvest as needed rather than all at once.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":150,"activity":"Harvest by twisting and pulling","details":"Grip the leek at the base and twist while pulling upward. If the soil is hard, loosen with a fork first. Trim roots and outer leaves. Leeks left in the ground in cool zones continue growing and hold quality for months.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow-growing cool-season allium. Deep planting and earthing up blanches the white shaft — the primary eating part. More cold-tolerant than onions.

key_activities: [{"timing":2,"activity":"Begin rinsing and draining 3 times daily for 7 days","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, rinse sprouts 3 times per day (morning, midday, evening) to prevent mould growth that warm temperatures accelerate. Complete drainage between rinses is critical.","category":"watering"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Harvest at 4-5cm","details":"In warm climates, harvest at 4-5cm before the sprouts begin to deteriorate. Refrigerate immediately after a final rinse. Use within 2 days (shorter shelf life in warm climates).","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: 3x daily rinsing in tropical humidity — or use single layer method
climate_note: Indoor crop — grown in a jar or tray, not the garden. Not zone-dependent. The same process applies in all climates.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray","details":"Copper spray while leafless to control fungal diseases including pear scab. Pear scab (Venturia pirina) is the main foliar disease — dormant spraying followed by a post-petal-fall spray controls it in most years.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune to central leader or modified leader in winter","details":"Pears are pruned more lightly than apples — they fruit on long-lived spurs that are removed only when unproductive. Maintain the central leader. Remove crossing branches and vigorous vertical water shoots. Do not heavily prune — pears can produce excessive vegetative growth called \"woolly butt\" if over-stimulated.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit lightly — 10-15cm spacing","details":"Thin to one fruit per cluster at 2-3cm fruitlet size. Pears thin naturally to some extent — supplement the natural drop to 10-15cm final spacing.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1460,"activity":"Harvest hard and ripen off the tree","details":"This is the most important pear-specific instruction: do not wait for pears to soften on the tree. Pick when the fruit separates cleanly with an upward twist but still feels firm. Ripen in a cool area (15-18°C) for 1-2 weeks. Beurre Bosc: harvest April-May; Williams: February-March; Packham: May-June.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Requires more chill hours than apple (600-1500+ hours depending on variety). Needs a cross-pollination partner. Pears are picked hard (before soft) and ripened off the tree — unlike most fruit.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Train new canes to trellis wires","details":"Tie new primocanes to the trellis as they grow through spring and summer. Summer-bearing varieties: these canes will fruit next year. Autumn/everbearing varieties: these canes will fruit at their tips in autumn of the same year.","category":"planting"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Remove old canes after harvest — critical annual task","details":"For summer varieties: immediately after harvest, cut all floricanes (the canes that fruited) to ground level. Tie the new primocanes neatly to the trellis. For autumn varieties: cut all canes to the ground in winter — they re-shoot and fruit on the new canes.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":400,"activity":"Harvest every 2-3 days at peak season","details":"Ripe raspberries separate from the core (receptacle) cleanly, leaving behind the hollow cone shape. They are fragile — pick into shallow containers and refrigerate immediately. Harvest every 2-3 days to prevent waste from overripe fruit.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Good production — summer and autumn varieties
climate_note: Requires 600-900 chill hours. Fruits on second-year canes (summer varieties) or current-year canes (autumn/everbearing varieties). Post-harvest cane removal is the key annual task.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Train shoots onto trellis","details":"Train stems onto trellis when 10-15cm tall. In zone 10, growth is faster than in cool zones — get plants onto the trellis early.","category":"planting"},{"timing":28,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash 25g/m² at first flower. Monitor soil moisture carefully in zone 10 — dry spells cause flower drop and empty pods.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest every 2 days — complete before heat","details":"Harvest every 2 days at full pod development. Complete all harvesting by September in zone 10 before heat causes the crop to collapse.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Thick-walled edible pod (both pod and peas eaten together). Taller vine than snow peas — needs 1.8m support. Same management principles as snow peas and peas.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and support plants","details":"In cool zones wind can be damaging. Stake each plant to a 60cm stake at transplant. Apply potassium-rich fertiliser (sulphate of potash at 40g/m²) at flowering — potassium drives fruit development.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest green or wait for full colour","details":"In cool zones the season may end before capsicum fully ripen. Harvest green if frost threatens. Red capsicum is the same fruit — simply allowed to fully ripen — and is sweeter with higher vitamin C.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost; Shortest outdoor window
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Needs 10°C+ at all times. Pick red for full sweetness — green capsicum is simply unripe.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray — essential","details":"Apply copper oxychloride or Bordeaux mixture while leafless. Nectarines are extremely susceptible to leaf curl and brown rot which overwinter on bark. Thorough dormant spraying is the single most effective disease management step.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune to open vase shape","details":"Prune in summer (January-February) after harvest — not winter. Winter pruning leaves entry wounds for silver leaf disease. Remove inward-facing shoots. Open vase structure admits light and air to reduce brown rot.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit heavily in spring","details":"When fruitlets are 1-2cm, thin to one fruit per 10-15cm of branch. Heavy thinning seems counterintuitive but dramatically increases final fruit size and reduces brown rot pressure from crowded touching fruit.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when fully coloured and fragrant","details":"Nectarines picked even one day early are disappointing — they do not ripen further off the tree. Harvest when the background colour changes from green to yellow and the fruit yields to gentle palm pressure. The aroma intensifies as ripeness is reached.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Very good production — choose 600-700 chill hour varieties
climate_note: Smooth-skinned peach variant with identical chill hour requirements. Brown rot at harvest is the main management challenge. Harvest timing is critical — nectarines do not improve after picking.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply summer mulch","details":"Deep mulch (10cm) around the drip line. In zone 10, lemons need weekly deep watering in dry summer months. Drought stress causes fruit drop and bark splitting.","category":"watering"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main heavy crop, remove crossing branches and manage height for access. Lemons do not need heavy pruning — mostly thinning and access management.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Begin harvesting when fruit is ripe","details":"In zones 9-10, Eureka and Lisbon lemons produce multiple crops per year. Harvest when fruit reaches full size and turns from deep green to yellow. The fruit holds on the tree for months — harvest as needed.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most widely grown backyard citrus. Eureka and Lisbon varieties are nearly ever-bearing — fruit year-round in warm zones. Meyer lemon is a hybrid with softer acidity and more cold-tolerance.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Do a structural prune","details":"Prune after the main harvest to maintain access height. In humid subtropical zones, thin the canopy to improve airflow and reduce fungal disease pressure.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Check fruit maturity with oil test","details":"Tropical avocados can produce year-round depending on variety. Sharwil, Reed and Monroe perform well in subtropical zones. Harvest when skin turns colour (Hass) or when flesh oil content exceeds 8% (confirm by picking a test fruit).","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Monitor for fruit fly and anthracnose
climate_note: Requires warm, frost-free conditions. Shallow roots are drought-sensitive. Type A and B varieties needed for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Install plant supports","details":"Erect stake-and-string support when plants reach 30cm. Zone 10 broad beans can produce tall crops — good support prevents wind damage.","category":"planting"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Pinch out tips — black aphid control","details":"Pinch out growing tips when 4-6 pods are visible on the stem. Black bean aphid infests broad bean tips in zone 10 and spreads rapidly in warm conditions. Pinching out removes the primary colony site.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest before heat returns","details":"In zone 10, the window before warming spring temperatures closes the harvest is short. Pick when pods are full but green. Process or freeze quickly — pods deteriorate rapidly in warm conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Cool-season crop. Direct sow — resent transplanting. Inoculate with rhizobium. Do not grow where temperatures regularly exceed 21°C at flowering.

key_activities: [{"timing":21,"activity":"Thin to 5cm","details":"Thin as soon as seedlings are identifiable. key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Remove side shoots from the root","details":"As the root swells, it produces small shoots (tillers) from its sides. key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Remove lower leaves regularly","details":"More frequent removal needed in warm humid conditions — fungal disease (especially black rot) spreads quickly in zone 11+ without good airflow around the base.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Top early to force development","details":"Top at 50-60cm height — earlier than cool zones. key_activities: [{"timing":7,"activity":"Thin to 5cm","details":"Thin at 2 true leaves. key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply acidic fertiliser","details":"Pineapple prefers slightly acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5). Use azalea/camellia fertiliser or ericaceous fertiliser. key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After fruit removal (August-September in cool zones; timing varies in tropical zones), remove crossing branches and any dead wood. extra_care: Productive but less tart than cool-zone grapefruit
climate_note: Least cold-tolerant of commercial citrus. Requires warm nights to develop balanced acidity and sweetness. Self-fertile but large tree — allow 6m spacing.

key_activities: [{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest daily in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat, okra pods reach harvestable size and become fibrous within 2-3 days. During peak production in tropical zones, harvest daily. Pods at 5-8cm are ideal — tender and flavoursome.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":80,"activity":"Cut back and regrow for second season","details":"In subtropical and tropical zones, cut plants back to 40cm after 4-5 months of production. climate_note: Heat-loving tropical vegetable. Harvest pods at 5-8cm — older pods become fibrous and tough within 2-3 days of reaching harvestable size.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply nitrogen at knee height and shoulder height","details":"Blood and bone or urea at 80g/m² when plants reach knee height. Repeat at shoulder height. In zone 10, rapid warm-season growth means the two-feed program must be timed precisely to plant growth stage, not calendar dates.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Water at silking","details":"In zone 10 warm summers, heat and dry spells at silking are common. extra_care: Excellent warm season crop — multiple plantings possible
climate_note: Wind-pollinated — plant in blocks (4x4 minimum), not single rows. Milk stage lasts only 2-3 days — harvest at peak sweetness.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Cut down fern in winter","details":"After fronds yellow in autumn, cut to ground level. Remove and compost debris. Apply potassium-rich fertiliser (sulphate of potash) and top-dress with compost.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Begin harvesting spears","details":"Cut spears when 15-20cm tall with tight tips, using a knife 2-3cm below soil. climate_note: Perennial — do not harvest in year 1 (cool zones) or years 1-2 (warm zones). Requires winter dormancy for reliable annual cropping.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Stake and apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash at 40g/m² when first flower buds appear. In cool zones feed every 3 weeks to maximise the short growing season. Stake early — fruiting plants topple in wind.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Pick green to stimulate production","details":"In cool zones the season is short. Harvest some fruit green to stimulate continued flowering rather than waiting for all fruit to ripen red. Each fruit left to ripen red on a cool-zone plant delays the production of several more fruits.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest all before frost","details":"Remove all remaining fruit before first autumn frost. Green peppers ripen to red if kept warm indoors. Do not compost plants without removing all fruit.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Requires warmth to germinate and fruit. Capsicum and Peppers are the same species (Capsicum annuum) — treated identically.

key_activities: [{"timing":150,"activity":"Stop watering and fertilising","details":"When approximately half the leaves have yellowed, stop all watering and fertilising. This triggers the final bulb curing process. Premature watering at this stage causes soft, poorly-wrapped bulbs that store poorly.","category":"watering"},{"timing":210,"activity":"Harvest when tops are 50% fallen","details":"Harvest when half the leaves have yellowed and fallen. Do not wait until all leaves die — the outer wrapper splits and bulbs deteriorate. Lift with a fork, not by pulling leaves. Cure in a dry, airy shed for 3-4 weeks before storing or using.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply summer mulch","details":"Deep mulch (10cm) around the drip line. In zone 10, lemons need weekly deep watering in dry summer months. Drought stress causes fruit drop and bark splitting.","category":"watering"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"After the main heavy crop, remove crossing branches and manage height for access. extra_care: Excellent lemon zone — multiple flushes per year possible
climate_note: Most widely grown backyard citrus. Eureka and Lisbon varieties are nearly ever-bearing — fruit year-round in warm zones. Meyer lemon is a hybrid with softer acidity and more cold-tolerance.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Begin harvesting when 15cm tall","details":"Cut stems to 5cm above ground when plants reach 15-20cm. This stimulates bushy growth. Harvest regularly — mint not cut back becomes leggy and flavourless. Harvest before flowering for maximum aroma.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":60,"activity":"Cut back hard before flowering","details":"When flower spikes appear, cut the entire plant back to 5cm. This delays flowering and forces a new flush of aromatic leaves. A plant that flowers loses most of its essential oil content and becomes less flavoursome.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Divide plant","details":"Lift the container, remove the root mass, divide and replant the most vigorous outer sections. Discard the old central root mass — it is woody and less productive.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch roots for winter in zones 8-9","details":"After the plant dies back in autumn, mulch the container or root zone with 5cm of compost. The roots survive winter and re-shoot reliably in spring.","category":"planting"}]
climate_note: Perennial spreading herb — grow in containers to prevent invasive spreading throughout the garden. Regrows from roots even after killing frost.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Trim to manage spread","details":"In warm zones sea asparagus spreads vigorously. Trim annually to keep within bounds. The trimmed stems are edible.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Begin harvesting young tips","details":"In warm zones sea asparagus is productive year-round. extra_care: Excellent — tolerates drought and salt spray
climate_note: Australian coastal native (Sarcocornia/Tecticornia species). Extremely salt-tolerant. Crunchy, salty succulent shoots harvested as a vegetable. Almost no care required once established.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at flowering","details":"Sulphate of potash 40g/m² at first flower and again at first fruit set. Zone 10 chillies can produce for 6-8 months from one planting. High potassium maintains this extended production.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest green or red at preference","details":"Harvest at any stage — green chillies are fresh and grassy; fully red are sweeter and hotter. Continuous picking extends production dramatically. Leave some to ripen fully for seed saving.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Overwinter in zone 10b","details":"In zone 10b, chilli plants can survive winter if cut back to 30cm and mulched heavily. extra_care: Outstanding production — can overwinter as short-lived perennial
climate_note: Warm-season crop that thrives in heat. Can be treated as a perennial in frost-free zones (10b-12). Extended ripening produces full colour and maximum heat.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Install frost protection in first 3 winters","details":"Young grapefruit are vulnerable to frost damage. key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Install supports for climbing varieties","details":"Erect 2m stakes or a trellis before plants need it. key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Prune to control spread if needed","details":"Sea asparagus can spread via runners in moist conditions. Trim back with shears if it exceeds its intended area. The harvested tips are the most tender part — regular tip harvesting acts as pruning.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":300,"activity":"Harvest young shoot tips 3-5cm","details":"Snap or cut the bright green young shoot tips (the tips, not the thicker woody stems). climate_note: Australian coastal native (Sarcocornia/Tecticornia species). Extremely salt-tolerant. Crunchy, salty succulent shoots harvested as a vegetable. Almost no care required once established.

key_activities: [{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune following harvest completion","details":"Lime trees produce prolifically in warm zones and can overcrowd the canopy. Harvest green for culinary use or allow to turn yellow for higher juice content. Fruit holds on the tree for several weeks — harvest as needed.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Least frost-tolerant common citrus. Tahitian (Persian) lime is the standard commercial variety. Kaffir lime grown for leaves. Both are essentially ever-bearing in warm zones.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Apply liquid fertiliser (1 of 4)","details":"Fortnightly liquid complete fertiliser in warm zones. climate_note: One of the most cold-tolerant vegetables. Frost dramatically improves sweetness. Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves only to extend production for months.

key_activities: [{"timing":70,"activity":"Blanch stalks for mild flavour","details":"2-3 weeks before harvest, wrap cardboard or black plastic around the stem cluster to exclude light. This is optional but produces the pale, mild-flavoured celery sold commercially. Blanching takes 2-3 weeks.","category":"planting"},{"timing":100,"activity":"Harvest outer stalks or entire plant","details":"Harvest outer stalks as needed from 10-12 weeks, or cut the entire plant at the base for bulk use. Cool zone celery holds on the plant for several weeks in cold conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Slow crop needing consistent moisture and cool but not cold conditions. Blanching by excluding light produces milder, less bitter stalks.

key_activities: [{"timing":0,"activity":"Succession sow every 2-3 weeks","details":"Sow direct or transplant. Press seed onto surface — lettuce needs light to germinate (do not bury deep, 3-5mm maximum). 25-30cm spacing for head lettuce, 15-20cm for leaf lettuce. In cool zones, lettuce can be grown almost year-round with succession sowing — avoid only the hottest 4-6 weeks of summer.","category":"planting"},{"timing":10,"activity":"Apply liquid nitrogen at thinning","details":"After thinning to final spacing, apply diluted fish emulsion or liquid complete fertiliser. Lettuce is a fast crop — one or two liquid feeds is sufficient for the full season.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":30,"activity":"Check for slugs and aphids","details":"In cool zones, slugs are the main lettuce pest (particularly in autumn and spring). Use iron-based slug pellets. Aphids cluster in head lettuce centres — blast with water or apply pyrethrum.","category":"pest"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Harvest before bolt","details":"Cut whole heads at the base when firm and full. For leaf lettuce, harvest outer leaves only (cut-and-come-again). Remove plants at first sign of a central flower stalk forming — bolted lettuce is immediately bitter and inedible.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Bolts (goes to seed) when temperatures exceed 25°C or day length increases beyond 14 hours. Succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous supply.

key_activities: [{"timing":30,"activity":"Install frost protection","details":"Young avocados are killed at -2°C. Install a frame for frost cloth before first winter. Have cloth ready from May. Remove cloth during the day to prevent overheating.","category":"planting"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Apply avocado fertiliser","details":"Apply zinc-containing complete fertiliser (avocados are very zinc-sensitive) in spring. Use 200-300g per year of tree age. Apply to drip line, not trunk.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune to manageable height","details":"Keep trees to 4-5m for harvesting. Prune after fruiting in autumn. Remove any frost-damaged wood in spring after last frost risk.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest by squeeze test","details":"Avocados do not ripen on the tree — they ripen after picking. Test one fruit; if it softens in 5-7 days on the bench, the crop is ready. Harvest all with a clean cut leaving the stem attached.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Frost protection essential — likely unsuitable without heated shelter
climate_note: Requires warm, frost-free conditions. Shallow roots are drought-sensitive. Type A and B varieties needed for pollination.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply protective fungicide at petal fall","details":"Brown rot (Monilinia) is the primary disease threat in warmer zones. Apply copper or approved fungicide at petal fall and again 3 weeks later. Critical for fruit quality.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Prune after harvest in summer","details":"Prune immediately after harvest to allow regrowth before dormancy. Open vase form preferred for airflow. Avoid winter pruning — silver leaf disease risk.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin heavily in productive years","details":"In zone 10, trees can overcrop and exhaust themselves. Thin to 8cm between fruit. Supports placed under heavy limbs prevent splitting.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Pick firm-ripe","details":"Warmer zone fruit ripens November-December. Pick when orange and slightly soft — do not wait for tree softening as fruit drops quickly in heat.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Brown rot and shot hole monitoring required
climate_note: Requires 300-900 chill hours. Flowers early — frost damage to blossom is the main risk in cool zones. Insufficient chill hours in zones 11b+.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Begin harvesting young tips","details":"Harvest young shoot tips year-round. Cut stems back by 30-40% to stimulate regrowth. In warm zones production is continuous and prolific.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":90,"activity":"Blanch before eating — mandatory","details":"ALWAYS blanch warrigal greens: boil 2 minutes, drain, refresh in cold water, squeeze dry. The oxalates that cause kidney issues are removed by blanching. Raw consumption is not safe. Post-blanching, use exactly like spinach.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Do a hard prune to manage size","details":"In warm zones warrigal greens can become very large (2m spread). Annual hard pruning to 15-20cm keeps the plant compact and productive. The cut material is edible (blanch first).","category":"pruning"}]
extra_care: Year-round — most productive in tropical zones
climate_note: Australian native coastal plant (Tetragonia tetragonioides). Edible leaves MUST be blanched (boiled 2+ minutes) before eating to reduce oxalates. Extremely drought and salt tolerant.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Cut back to crown after main harvest","details":"After the primary harvest (central heads cut), cut the plant back to 30cm stubs. In cool zones this triggers a second flush of heads in autumn. Clear all old leaf material to prevent fungal disease.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Mulch crowns heavily for winter","details":"After the growing season, cut plants to ground level in cool zones. Apply 15cm compost mulch over the crown to protect from hard frosts. The crown overwinters underground and re-shoots in spring.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest central bud before scales open","details":"Cut the central bud (largest) first when it is 8-12cm across and the scales are still tightly closed. A small gap between scales indicates the bud is past prime. Cut with 15cm of stem for ease of eating. Side buds follow.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Cut back and mulch crowns heavily in winter
climate_note: Perennial — survives for 5-8 years from division. Harvest the central bud first, then side buds. Cut back after harvest in cool zones to stimulate new growth.

key_activities: [{"timing":45,"activity":"Apply potassium at first flower","details":"Sulphate of potash 40g/m² at first flower. Repeat every 6 weeks through the long zone 10 fruiting season. Complete fertiliser monthly maintains plant vigour.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":70,"activity":"Harvest at green or red stage","details":"Harvest at preferred ripeness. Green = fresh/crisp flavour; red/yellow/orange = sweeter and higher in vitamin C. Consistent harvesting extends production in zone 10 from November through to May.","category":"harvest"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Cut back and overwinter in zone 10b","details":"In zone 10b, cut plants to a 30cm framework in April-May. Mulch heavily. Most plants regrow in spring from the root system — year 2 plants are larger and often more productive than year 1.","category":"pruning"}]
climate_note: Warm-season crop. Requires warmth to germinate and fruit. Capsicum and Peppers are the same species (Capsicum annuum) — treated identically.

key_activities: [{"timing":90,"activity":"Switch to potassium at bulbing","details":"When bulbs are visibly swelling, stop nitrogen and apply sulphate of potash (30g/m²). This firms the bulb layers and improves storage quality and flavour.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":110,"activity":"Stop watering when tops yellow","details":"Stop all irrigation when 50-60% of tops have yellowed and flopped. This triggers the final curing of the neck — premature watering at this point causes soft-necked bulbs with poor storage life.","category":"watering"},{"timing":120,"activity":"Harvest and cure — 3-4 weeks","details":"Lift when tops are fully yellowed. Lay in a dry, airy shed for 3-4 weeks. Separate the bulb clusters once tops are fully dry. In cool zones, shallots store for 6-12 months in cool, dry, dark conditions.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted from individual bulbs — each divides into a cluster of 4-8 new bulbs at harvest. Same day-length sensitivity as onions. Cure thoroughly before storage.

key_activities: [{"timing":150,"activity":"Reduce then stop water","details":"When 30-40% of leaves yellow, reduce watering. When 50% yellow, stop completely. Earlier water reduction in zone 10 compared to cooler zones because spring warming arrives sooner.","category":"watering"},{"timing":210,"activity":"Harvest October-November","details":"In zone 10, harvest typically October-November — earlier than cool zones. Lift carefully with a fork. Cure in a well-ventilated dry shed for 2-3 weeks. Do not leave in wet ground as spring rains begin.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Planted as individual cloves (not seedlings/seed). Requires cool winter temperatures for bulb formation. Harvest when tops fall over and yellow.

key_activities: [{"timing":14,"activity":"Prune and space plants to maximise airflow","details":"Plant in open, well-ventilated positions. In subtropical zones even dry season humidity promotes powdery mildew. Avoid enclosed beds.","category":"planting"},{"timing":45,"activity":"Preventive sulfur spray from 40 days","details":"Apply sulfur-based fungicide from 40 days as a preventive measure in subtropical and tropical zones. Powdery mildew appears earlier and spreads faster in warm conditions.","category":"pest"},{"timing":55,"activity":"Harvest daily in tropical conditions","details":"In tropical heat, zucchini grows even faster than in temperate zones. Harvest every day or two. A missed harvest in tropical heat produces an enormous marrow within 72 hours.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Most productive vegetable by weight. Harvest at 15-20cm — fruit left on plant to size stops production and quickly becomes inedible marrow. Hand pollinate if bee numbers are low.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply dormant copper spray — essential","details":"Apply copper oxychloride or Bordeaux mixture while leafless. Nectarines are extremely susceptible to leaf curl and brown rot which overwinter on bark. Thorough dormant spraying is the single most effective disease management step.","category":"pest"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Summer prune to open vase shape","details":"Prune in summer (January-February) after harvest — not winter. Winter pruning leaves entry wounds for silver leaf disease. Remove inward-facing shoots. Open vase structure admits light and air to reduce brown rot.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":730,"activity":"Thin fruit heavily in spring","details":"When fruitlets are 1-2cm, thin to one fruit per 10-15cm of branch. Harvest when the background colour changes from green to yellow and the fruit yields to gentle palm pressure. The aroma intensifies as ripeness is reached.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Smooth-skinned peach variant with identical chill hour requirements. Brown rot at harvest is the main management challenge. Harvest timing is critical — nectarines do not improve after picking.

key_activities: [{"timing":180,"activity":"Tip-prune following harvest completion","details":"After berry harvest, tip-prune by 30% to encourage bushy, productive growth for the following season. The shrub can be cut back harder (50%) every 3-4 years to rejuvenate it.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Harvest after natural drying on the plant","details":"In warm zones Akudjura berries ripen and dry quickly on the plant. Harvest when fully shrivelled and brown. The caramel-tamarillo flavour is most intense in fully dried berries. Use as a ground spice in marinades, sauces and bread.","category":"harvest"}]
climate_note: Australian native desert shrub (Solanum centrale). Extremely drought-tolerant. Berries are dried and used as a spice with caramel-tamarillo flavour. Dislikes wet soils.

key_activities: [{"timing":60,"activity":"Apply mango-specific fertiliser","details":"Use a low-phosphorus complete fertiliser with trace elements. Apply in October after the flowering period and again in February. In zone 10, a third application in June-July when growth resumes.","category":"fertilizing"},{"timing":180,"activity":"Withhold water June-August to trigger flowering","details":"In zone 10, the cool-dry period naturally reduces rainfall. Supplement this by withholding irrigation in June-August. This water and temperature stress triggers the flower induction that produces the following season's crop.","category":"watering"},{"timing":365,"activity":"Tip-prune after harvest for compact form","details":"After harvest, lightly tip-prune the new growth to maintain a compact tree. This improves the light environment within the canopy and manages tree size for easier netting.","category":"pruning"},{"timing":1095,"activity":"Harvest when stalk end of fruit colours","details":"Kensington Pride yellows at the stem end when ripe. R2E2 and Calypso develop red blush. Pick when slightly soft at the tip and aroma is sweet and tropical. Zone 10 mango harvest: November-February.","category":"harvest"}]
extra_care: Possible in warm spots — frost protection for young trees
climate_note: Tropical/subtropical tree requiring a warm dry period to trigger flowering. Frost kills young trees. Most varieties need 8-10 weeks of cool/dry weather to induce flowering.
